title: Broncos safety Brandon Jones goes 3-for-4 filling in for kicker Wil Lutz at training camp
summary: The Broncos have only one kicker on their 90-man roster: Wil Lutz, who missed Saturday's practice to attend former teammate Drew Brees' induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
full_text: The Broncos have only one kicker on their 90-man roster: Wil Lutz, who missed Saturday's practice to attend former teammate Drew Brees' induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. And that's how they found out that they have another kicker on their roster: Brandon Jones, a safety who can kick in a pinch. Jones went 3-for-4 on field goals at practice on Saturday and said afterward that he became the Broncos' backup kicker after what started as a joke with special teams coordinator Darren Rizzi. "I didn’t kick in high school or college, I just have some history in playing soccer," Jones said. “I don't know how I even got to kick. I think I just was joking with Riz like, ‘Yo, I can kick if you ever need an emergency-kicker-type of situation.’ Then he called my bluff and put me to the test one day, I think it was some time last year, and I made an extra point." The longest of Jones' field goals at practice on Saturday was 41 yards. He said he once made a 50-yard field goal while working with Lutz. Broncos fans at training camp were chanting Jones' name as he showed off his kicking skills, which he said was a thrill, but he doesn't know if he could handle the pressure of the Broncos needing him to make a game-winner. "If we're winning by a lot, no big deal. Hopefully, I don't think it would ever come down to a game-time thing where I would need to make it to win. If it comes down to that, just pray for me, that's all I can say," Jones said. Jones knows he's not good enough to play Major League Soccer, but he said he would love to try out for an MLS team when he retires from the NFL, just for the challenge of it. "Played some club soccer, stopped in high school because I was like, 'Let's be real, I'm a football player,'" Jones said. He showed on Saturday that he's a football player who can play two positions.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bears expect Luther Burden to miss about a month, be ready for Week One
summary: Burden suffered a groin injury in practice on Saturday.
full_text: The Bears are optimistic that wide receiver Luther Burden can play in Week One against the Panthers. Burden is expected to miss about a month after suffering a groin injury in practice on Saturday, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS. The Bears' regular-season opener is a little more than a month away on September 13, which means if all goes according to plan, Burden will be on the field. Last year Burden caught 47 passes as a rookie, finishing second among the Bears’ wide receivers in receptions behind D.J. Moore. This year Moore has been traded away, and the Bears want more from Burden. Bears head coach Ben Johnson recently praised Burden’s competitiveness and spoke as if he's expecting a very big season from Burden in Year Two. This groin injury will be a setback that keeps him off the practice field and out of the preseason, but shouldn't keep him off the field when the season starts.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Free agent CB Terrion Arnold visits Seahawks
summary: Free agent cornerback Terrion Arnold visited the Seahawks on Sunday, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.
full_text: '' Free agent cornerback Terrion Arnold visited the Seahawks on Sunday, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. Arnold, 23, previously met with the Texans and has drawn interest from the Colts and Jets. The Seahawks cut Arnold on June 29 following his arrest in Florida on four felony counts each of armed robbery and kidnapping. It could bring a life sentence if he is convicted. The Lions drafted Arnold in the first round in 2024, and he played 24 games with 22 starts in two seasons. He has totaled 91 tackles, an interception and 18 pass breakups.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions worked out free agent CB Trevon Diggs
summary: The Lions worked out free agent cornerback Trevon Diggs, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
full_text: The Lions worked out free agent cornerback Trevon Diggs, according to the NFL's personnel notice. Diggs, 27, became a free agent Jan. 20 when the Packers cut him after two games and 34 snaps. The Packers had claimed him off waivers from the Cowboys on Dec. 31. Diggs led the league with 11 interceptions in 2021, but he has not been the same player since his knee problems began in 2023. He tore his ACL in September 2023 and underwent an additional surgery on his knee in December 2024. In January 2025, Diggs underwent a chondral tissue and bone graft surgery on his left knee to repair persistent cartilage damage. He has played only 22 games over the past three seasons. The Cowboys drafted Diggs in the second round in 2020, and he was twice a Pro Bowler and, in 2021, was an All-Pro.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Giants agree to terms with S JT Woods
summary: The Giants are signing safety JT Woods, Aaron Wilson of KPRC reports.
full_text: The Giants are signing safety JT Woods, Aaron Wilson of KPRC reports. Woods, 26, worked out for the team Sunday. The Chargers selected Woods in the third round of the 2022 draft, and he played 10 games with one start as a rookie. He totaled three tackles while playing 31 defensive snaps and 73 on special teams. Woods played three games in 2023 and recorded five tackles. He has not appeared in a game since. Woods has also spent time with the Eagles, Bears, Seahawks, Raiders and Jets.
author: Charean Williams

title: Packers sign WR Kisean Johnson
summary: The Packers announced three roster on Sunday.
full_text: The Packers announced three roster on Sunday. They have signed wide receiver Kisean Johnson as a free agent. They waived safety Johnathan Baldwin and cornerback Marlon Jones in corresponding moves. Johnson went undrafted out of Western Kentucky last year and signed with the Browns. He spent time on the Packers' practice squad during the regular season, but did not appear in any games. Johnson had 75 catches for 925 yards and seven touchdowns in his final college season. Baldwin played in one game for Green Bay last season and Jones signed with the team after going undrafted this year. Both players will revert to injured reserve if they are unclaimed.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Jones believes rookie Demond Claiborne is a "special back"
summary: The running game has largely been an afterthought during Kevin O'Connell's first four years as the Vikings' head coach.
full_text: The running game has largely been an afterthought during Kevin O'Connell's first four years as the Vikings' head coach. This year, with former Dolphins offensive coordinator Frank Smith (now assistant head coach in Minnesota) helping to install a wide-zone rushing attack, the Vikings could be running it more. And they could end up relying on speedy sixth-round rookie Demond Claiborne. For now, Claiborne has a firm believer in veteran Aaron Jones. “You can see it,” running back Aaron Jones Sr. said, via Ben Goessling of the Minneapolis Star Tribune . “Right away, just getting in and out of the cuts. He’s a special back in this league . I get to mentor him up and show him the way. I told him I want him to be successful, I want to see him go on and get paid and those kinds of things. He’ll be playing in this league as long as he wants to, but just got to lock in here and take care of the business.” Claiborne, who spent four seasons at Wake Forest, ran the 40-yard dash in 4.37 seconds at the Scouting Combine in February. He nevertheless fell to pick No. 198. The Vikings also have Jordan Mason, Zavier Scott, and Jordan Mims in the backfield. It remains to be seen if the Vikings make the full commitment to running the ball. O'Connell is a quarterback guru, and the passing game has taken precedence. But nothing opens up the passing game like an effective running game that can force a defense to get caught flat-footed while trying too hard to get to the tailback with the ball. And with so much focus on the team's quarterback competition, a potent running game could make life a lot easier for whoever wins the job.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Donald decision is currently expected this week
summary: Donald will take a little more time to make his play-or-don't-play call.
full_text: Aaron Donald continues to ponder whether he'll return to football after two years of retirement. And his play-or-don't-play decision is indeed coming soon. But apparently not quite as soon as recently expected. Donald's target, we're told, has shifted from early this week to the end of this week. (Given the ramifications of a decision to return, Donald could take a little more time before making the decision to take the pigskin plunge.) The Rams have plenty of time to get Donald ready to go. They'd deploy the same plan utilized in 2017 and 2018 to ramp him up after protracted contract holdouts. The Rams would want Donald to have a few weeks of football activities before playing, with the goal of 30-40 snaps in the Week 1 game against the 49ers in Australia. Unless Donald's workouts include the equivalent of football sparring sessions, he won't know how he moves in relation to other players until he's back on the practice field. Hall of Famer Lawrence Taylor retired after realizing that the younger players seemed to be getting faster. His coach, Bill Parcells, told Taylor that he was getting slower. Unless and until Donald is practicing against other players, he won't be able to make that assessment. And that's an important factor, because Aaron Donald wants to be sure that he'll still be the Aaron Donald of old. Still, Donald currently seems to be planning to make the decision on whether to play before officially rejoining the Rams and participating in practice. And he'll be taking a bit more time to make that call. It remains hard to envision Donald putting in so much work only to not play. Until he decides to do it, however, there's a chance he'll decide not to do it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Luke Altmyer: A joy to spend time with Teddy Bridgewater, his retirement creates opportunity
summary: Rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer is set to see a lot of action in the Lions' first preseason game.
full_text: Rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer is set to see a lot of action in the Lions' first preseason game. Teddy Bridgewater's retirement left Altmyer as the only quarterback behind Jared Goff on Detroit's roster. Josh Dobbs is set to sign with the team, but he's just joining the team and Goff is not going to play against the Bengals on Thursday. That leaves the undrafted rookie with a chance to make a big impression. "First of all, best wishes to [Bridgewater]," Altmyer said, via the team's website. "I'm so thankful to spend time with him and [Goff], obviously, learning from both of them, different perspectives (and) different outlooks on how they see things. It was a joy to spend some time with him. But it brings about opportunity for myself. The standard is to play good football no matter how many reps or whatever my role is. I have a job to do, and my job is to do that very well at a high level. I'm thankful and believe in my abilities and I'm going to go cut it loose whatever that looks like." Dobbs's experience makes him likelier to be the No. 2 when the regular season starts, but Altmyer could make the decision about keeping a third quarterback more difficult if he can lead the offense successfully in Cincinnati.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears sign DB Beanie Bishop
summary: The Bears continue to be busy adding defensive backs to their roster.
full_text: The Bears continue to be busy adding defensive backs to their roster. They announced the signing of Beanie Bishop on Sunday. They have also signed Xavier Woods, Brandon Hill, and William Wright over the last few days. All of the moves come after the Bears saw safety Coby Bryant go down with a knee injury that will keep him out for an extended period of time. Cam Lewis left Saturday's practice with an injury and the Bears have not had Kyler Gordon or Elijah Hicks on the field at all this summer. Bishop made the Steelers as an undrafted rookie in 2024 and appeared in every game. He finished the season with 45 tackles, four interceptions, a half-sack and a fumble recovery, but was limited to the practice squad in Pittsburgh and New Orleans last season. The NFL suspended Bishop for the first three games of the 2026 season in March, so he won't be able to help the Bears patch any early season holes in the secondary. The Bears waived long snapper Luke Elkin in a corresponding move.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions put Teddy Bridgewater on reserve/retired list
summary: Bridgewater stepped away from the team on Sunday.
full_text: The Lions have not announced the signing of quarterback Josh Dobbs yet, but they did announce some other transactions on Sunday. They formally placed Teddy Bridgewater on the reserve/retired list after head coach Dan Campbell revealed the quarterback is stepping away from football. Campbell said he believes this is a permanent decision by Bridgewater, which is why they're adding Dobbs to back up Jared Goff. Detroit also signed linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga and cornerback Ryan Cooper. Ogbongbemiga spent the last two seasons with the Bears and saw most of his action on special teams. He had 30 tackles and a sack with Chicago and spent his first three seasons with the Chargers. Cooper played one game for the Ravens in 2024 and also spent time in the UFL. The Lions waived tight end Nick Muse to round out the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Trent Williams is sued for not making payments on a 2021 Porsche lease
summary: Although it's hard to envision 49ers tackle Trent Williams fitting inside a Porsche 911, he leased one in 2021.
full_text: '' Although it's hard to envision 49ers tackle Trent Williams fitting inside a Porsche 911, he leased one in 2021. Now, the company that leased it to him is suing for failing to make the payments. Via TMZ, OpenRoad Auto Group claims that Williams signed a four-year lease for the vehicle in August 2021. He allegedly made the first two payments (totaling $10,617.26) by bank debit. He allegedly closed the account before any of the remaining 46 payments could be made. The lease expired last August. The company contends that it doesn't know the whereabouts of the car. It alleges that Williams may have sold it to a car company, which then sold it to someone else. OpenRoad has sued Williams for breach of contract, fraud, and other specific legal claims. The whole thing is confusing. First, why would OpenRoad wait so long to take formal action (assuming the case was filed recently)? Second, how could Williams have sold the car without being able to transfer a valid title to it? Regardless, the lawsuit has been filed. And OpenRoad is seeking from Williams $244,199.28, along with other charges, attorneys' fees, and litigation costs.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lions will sign Josh Dobbs to replace Teddy Bridgewater
summary: A rocket scientist is heading to the Motor City.
full_text: A rocket scientist is heading to the Motor City. With quarterback Teddy Bridgewater leaving the team (he has already been placed on the reserve/retired list), the Lions will fill the void by signing veteran Josh Dobbs. Per NFL Network, Dobbs will get a one-year $1.425 million deal with $475,000 guaranteed. He'll arrive as the likely No. 2 to Jared Goff. The only other quarterback on the Lions roster is Luke Altmyer, an undrafted free agent who played last year at Illinois. Dobbs, 31, was a fourth-round pick of the Steelers in 2017. He also has spent time over the last 10 seasons with the Jaguars, Browns, Titans, Cardinals, Vikings, 49ers, and Patriots. In 2022, he spent 16 days on the Lions' practice squad before being signed to Tennessee's active roster. Dobbs has played in 27 regular-season games, with 15 starts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan's recent concussion changes his perspective on head injuries
summary: For most coaches, the issue of player concussions requires sympathy.
full_text: For most coaches, the issue of player concussions requires sympathy. Moving forward, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan will easily be able to empathize with players who have suffered head trauma. In his first training-camp press conference following a July 11 automobile accident, Shanahan was asked if the severe concussion that he sustained will change his perspective on players who are dealing with the effects of brain injuries. “Yeah, no doubt," Shanahan said. "I've been told so much by these guys, don't compare a sports concussion to an accident like this. I'm starting to realize that now. Just little things, like when they label things, like whether it's severe or mild. You hear someone has a mild one, I'm like, ‘Oh, alright. It might be one game, but usually that's two.’ Then you kind of learn those are just words. Each one's a little bit different. I definitely can relate to how scary it is when you don't know if you will feel right again. It's definitely made me more educated on it. Usually I just listen, and like, ‘Tell me when, OK?’ and I move on, but I understand it a lot better and what guys got to go through and the protocol to get back. There’s not a protocol for me on paper, but it's really cool to be in a profession that knows what to do with those things. All the people that I need help from, it was already built in here. They’ve got a lot of experience with it, and it's been really good for me.” If anything, players need to be encouraged to not return until they're fully back to normal. Some players will try to hide their symptoms. Some will resist being evaluated. Some will tank the baseline cognitive exams so that it will be easier to be cleared to return. (Peyton Manning once admitted to doing that , before walking it back as a joke .) Starting in 2009, when Congress got involved in the issue of brain health, the NFL began to take concussions very seriously. For the most part, it does. (There are still periodic lapses in the concussion-spotting process.) Moving forward, Shanahan will have a better understanding of the challenges created by a concussion. And while very few players use a concussion as a crutch to avoid practicing and/or playing, Shanahan could be a valuable resource when it comes to encouraging players to take their time. It also could make him less likely to allow a player to lose his prior spot in the depth chart due to missing time because of a head injury.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers starters will play Saturday night against the Bills
summary: The Panthers opened their preseason slate in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
full_text: The Panthers opened their preseason slate in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. In one of the most entertaining exhibition games in recent memory, Haynes King had a 5-yard touchdown run on the final play to beat the Cardinals 33-30. Carolina's starters did not play Thursday night. The Panthers will play their starters, including quarterback Bryce Young, on Saturday night in the Bills' first game at the new Highmark Stadium. "Yes, yes," Canales said Sunday about the starters playing, via Anthony Rizzuti of USA Today. " We will play this week , for sure. We'll take it week by week. We'll get them out there, probably play something similar to what Kenny [Pickett] and that group played in the Hall of Fame Game. So it'll be somewhere between 10 and 20 plays, depending on how those drives pan out, so we can just get some good work in."
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts bring back WR D.J. Montgomery
summary: The Colts signed free agent wide receiver D.J.
full_text: The Colts signed free agent wide receiver D.J. Montgomery on Sunday, the team announced. Montgomery spent last season on the Colts' injured reserve list. He has played 10 career games and has made six receptions for 92 yards and a touchdown. Montgomery also has totaled one special teams tackle. He has spent time with the Colts (2022-25), Texans (2022), Jets (2020-22) and Browns (2019-20). In a corresponding move, the Colts waived wide receiver Liam Clifford. Clifford signed with the team as an undrafted free agent on July 30. In college, he played 52 career games with 15 starts at Penn State (2021-25) and made 42 receptions for 530 yards and one touchdown. Clifford also registered three carries for 16 yards and scored one touchdown on a blocked punt.
author: Charean Williams

title: Saints guard Dillon Radunz is out for the year with torn ACL
summary: The Saints have lost another player to a torn ACL.
full_text: The Saints have lost another player to a torn ACL. Via Katherine Terrell of ESPN, guard Dillon Radunz will miss the season after suffering the knee injury during individual drills at practice on Saturday. Radunz, a second-round pick of the Titans in 2021, signed a two-year, $6.9 million contract with the Saints as a free agent in 2025. Last year, he appeared in 15 regular-season games with 10 starts. He participated in 699 total snaps on offense and 65 special-teams plays. Radunz was expected to serve as the primary backup to David Edwards at left guard. Earlier in camp, defensive lineman Bryan Bresee suffered a torn ACL.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bucs sign S Xavier Williams
summary: The Buccaneers signed safety Xavier Williams on Sunday, the team announced.
full_text: The Buccaneers signed safety Xavier Williams on Sunday, the team announced. Williams joins the Buccaneers as a college free agent after trying out during the team’s rookie minicamp in May. He played at four different college programs over five years, finishing his career at the University of Cincinnati (2025). Last season, Williams appeared in 12 games, totaling 39 tackles, one forced fumble and one pass defensed. Williams also played at Middle Tennessee State (2024), the University of Central Florida (2023) and Charlotte (2021-22). In a corresponding move, the Bucs waived cornerback Chase Lucas with a failed physical. Lucas entered the NFL as a seventh-round pick of the Lions in 2022. He made Detroit's roster as a rookie and played 18 games in two seasons there, contributing six tackles. During the 2024 offseason, he signed with the 49ers and stayed on the practice squad all season. Lucas then made San Francisco's active roster in 2025. In his 15 games played last season, Lucas totaled nine tackles, a pass defensed and a quarterback hit.
author: Charean Williams

title: Cardinals sign former UFL players Shawn Bowman, Eugene Asante
summary: The Cardinals signed tight end Shawn Bowman and linebacker Eugene Asante on Sunday, the team announced.
full_text: ''' The Cardinals signed tight end Shawn Bowman and linebacker Eugene Asante on Sunday, the team announced. Bowman most recently played for the Orlando Storm in the UFL. He appeared in 11 games this spring and caught seven passes for 53 yards. He entered the NFL in 2024 with Jacksonville as an undrafted rookie free agent from Rutgers. Bowman spent his rookie season on the Jaguars' practice squad. While in college, Bowman appeared in 44 games at Rutgers (2023) and Maine (2019-22) and made 90 receptions for 984 yards and 11 touchdowns. Asante spent this spring with the Houston Gamblers of the UFL and appeared in nine games. He totaled 34 tackles, four tackles for loss, two passes defensed and two forced fumbles. He entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent from Auburn in 2025, signing with the Dolphins. Asante spent his rookie season on the Dolphins, Browns and Falcons practice squads. During his six-year collegiate career at Auburn (2022-24) and North Carolina (2019-21), he saw action in 65 games. Asante totaled 196 tackles, 14 tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries and a forced fumble. Asante was third-team All-SEC in consecutive seasons (2023-24).
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Luther Burden to miss time with groin injury
summary: Bears receiver Luther Burden exited practice early on Saturday, and now there is more information about his status.
full_text: Bears receiver Luther Burden exited practice early on Saturday, and now there is more information about his status. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Burden suffered a groin injury and is set to miss some time. His timetable to return has not been reported. Burden suffered the injury in one-on-one drills, with reporters noting he limped back to the locker room. Last year as a rookie, Burden caught 47 passes for 652 yards with two touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Tomlin: Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini scandal will get quiet if Patriots win games, loud if they lose
summary: In the same week that Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers literally crapped on ESPN, while appearing on ESPN, for not sufficiently covering the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini situation, former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin addressed the issue during his debut on NBC.
full_text: '' In the same week that Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers literally crapped on ESPN, while appearing on ESPN, for not sufficiently covering the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini situation, former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin addressed the issue during his debut on NBC. The offseason scandal became a topic during halftime of the Hall of Fame game between the Panthers and Cardinals. And here's how Tomlin addressed it, concisely and accurately. "When games start, winning matters," Tomlin said. "And so if they get off to a fast start, they've got a chance to quiet some of that noise. If they don't, things could get extremely loud." Unlike last year, the 2026 schedule won't be a patsy-fest for the Patriots. The Patriots face four 2025 playoff teams out of the gates: Seahawks, Steelers, Jaguars, and Bills. (The Pittsburgh game could be a little more interesting, given the things Rodgers said.) If the Patriots start 3-1, Russinigate will fade. If the Patriots start 1-3, the team could become engulfed by it. The good news is that the schedule softens in Week 5, with a visit from the Raiders. Then again, the 2025 season opened with a visit from the Raiders — and the Patriots somehow lost that game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Downs' groin injury is not considered serious
summary: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Colts.
full_text: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Colts. Via Stephen Holder of ESPN, head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Sunday that receiver Josh Downs' groin injury is not considered serious and Downs should return to the field soon. Downs could even potentially be on the field for the Colts’ joint practice with the Patriots on Tuesday. Downs is a critical piece for Indianapolis’ starting offense, particularly as Alec Pierce continues to recover from offseason ankle surgery. In 2025, Downs caught 58 passes for 566 yards with four touchdowns in 16 games. He is entering the final year of his rookie contract after the Colts selected him in the third round of the 2023 draft.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Grass at new Bills stadium drew rave reviews (some of the sight lines did not)
summary: The Buffalo Bills had a soft launch of their new stadium this weekend, with a practice there on Saturday night.
full_text: '' The Buffalo Bills had a soft launch of their new stadium this weekend, with a practice there on Saturday night . The team wore their new Nickel City Batman uniforms , which continue to be panned despite Josh Allen's effort to give them a boost . The best news for the players was the playing surface. The Bills opted to switch from artificial turf at the old stadium to natural grass at the new stadium. Here's the verdict from offensive lineman Spencer Brown: "Perfect. I love it. I might sleep out here tonight , actually." Some of the fans may not have loved the view from their seats. Consider this . Or this . Or this . Then there are the video boards. They're small. Which prompted one person on Twitter to compare them to Michael Scott’s plasma TV . The Bills host the Panthers next Saturday for the preseason opener. The official regular-season christening happens on Thursday, September 17, when the Lions face the Bills on Prime Video.
author: Mike Florio

title: Teddy Bridgewater steps away from Lions, retirement likely
summary: Detroit needs a new backup QB, with HC Dan Campbell saying the team may bring someone in as soon as Monday.
full_text: The Lions need a new backup quarterback. Teddy Bridgewater has informed the club that he's going to step away, with retirement likely. Bridgewater had not attended the last two practices. " Teddy Bridgewater is going to step away ," head coach Dan Campbell said in his Sunday press conference. "I’ve known Teddy a long time and, man, the human being is unbelievable — certainly the player. Everything that he’s about, the type of teammate he is, the way that he prepares, [he] always played the game up here, and had a huge heart. He’s going to be missed. "So, I’ll never forget 2019 [with the Saints] when Drew [Brees] got injured — we’d just gone out to the Rams, got beat out there, and Drew got his thumb, and we lost him for five weeks. And Teddy stepped in, we won five in a row, man. That was Teddy. And just his time being with us [with the Lions] meant a lot and it meant a lot to our guys. So, he’s going to be missed." Campbell added that he thinks this time Bridgewater will stay retired. "His biggest worry was letting us down," Campbell said. "That’s the type of guy he is. And he’s not." But that means the Lions do now need a backup quarterback, as the only other QB on the roster aside from starter Jared Goff is undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer. “We’re going to add somebody,” Campbell said. “We like Luke. Luke is growing, he’s getting better. He just needs reps. He needs a million reps. With the reps that he has gotten at this point, he has improved. So, we like him. “But we are going to add somebody, and we’d like to add a veteran quarterback. We’re hoping maybe something happens tomorrow. We’ll see. But, yeah, that’s the plan.” Bridgewater signed with the Lions on a one-year deal back in March. He was previously with the club in 2023 and 2024 before spending the 2025 season with Tampa Bay. The No. 32 overall pick of the 2014 draft, Bridgewater appeared in 83 games with 65 starts, accumulating a 33-32 record as a starter. He appeared in games for Minnesota, New Orleans, Carolina, Denver, Miami, Detroit, and Tampa Bay.
author: Myles Simmons

title: The "BS" from Deebo Samuel's contact squabble is irrelevant to his 49ers' reunion
summary: Receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. is back in San Francisco, and back in the number he wore from 2019 through 2023: 19.
full_text: Receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. is back in San Francisco, and back in the number he wore from 2019 through 2023: 19. Coach Kyle Shanahan explained on Saturday that any contract-driven awkwardness from years past is a non-issue now. “Deebo's always been one of the closest guys we've been to, just relationship-wise," Shanahan told reporters. "When Deebo went through his contract negotiations, [I'll] try not to put words in his mouth, but I think he thought it'd be advantageous to make it look like there was a little bit of a battle. Sometimes that helps, sometimes it doesn't. . . . "Those OTAs [in 2022], I was at Deebo's house on the eighth OTA day, and I was talking about how all that was just BS. He came to minicamp. We had a great summer together. I think he signed the first day back at training camp. We got over that in OTAs. That was just stuff from the negotiating periods back in April and stuff. There were stuff, definitely, that made me like, ‘What the hell is going on?’ We're not around Deebo. Then we see him in OTAs and we got to talk man-to-man and it was fine as soon as we got with each other.” Shanahan also said that Deebo's return was unrelated to losing receiver Ricky Pearsall for the entire season. "They're just two completely different types of players," Shanahan said. "Deebo was someone that we were hoping it would work out, depending on Deebo's other opportunities and what it could be here. That was something that we were hoping for a long time could work out and it ended up working out for both of us. The Ricky thing changed nothing.” And so both Samuel and linebacker Dre Greenlaw have returned to the 49ers, after a year elsewhere. Shanahan believes it will make a difference for the team. "They've been away for a year, but to see them out there, they look exactly like the guys I remember,” Shanahan said. That's good news for the 49ers, who will need everything they can to compete with the Rams and Seahawks in the NFC West.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots scramble to replace turf field before Thursday's preseason opener vs. Colts
summary: The first surface installed after the World Cup was deemed to be "noncompliant."
full_text: After the final World Cup game at Gillette Stadium, out went the FIFA-mandated grass and in came an artificial turf field. Now, the artificial turf field will be hastily replaced with a different one. Via Mike Reiss of ESPN, the NFL and NFL Players Association independent laboratory testing protocol determined that the first artificial surface was " noncompliant ." Patriots chief operating officer Jim Nolan explained the situation to Reiss but, frankly, Nolan's quotes are sort of confusing and subtly oozing with spin. The bottom line is that the first field wasn't good enough, forcing the Patriots to rip it out and try again. Quickly. "The field we're installing is the latest version of the field we took out in January," Nolan told Reiss. "From a player perspective, it will be incredibly consistent with what they played on last year." It's unclear why that field wasn't reinstalled in the first place. The new field is being installed this week. And the clock is ticking. The Patriots host the Colts to open the 2026 preseason on Thursday night. What if the new field doesn't pass muster? It wouldn't be the first time a preseason game was scrapped. Ten years ago, the Hall of Fame Game between the Colts and Packers didn't happen due to paint that had become " congealed and rubberized ." (The debacle, which sparked litigation from those who bought tickets and in many cases traveled to Canton, caused the NFL to move the game from after the enshrinement ceremony to before it.) Twenty-five years ago, a Ravens-Eagles game at Veterans Stadium in Philadelphia was cancelled due to " uneven cutouts " in the playing surface that, at the time, was used for both football and baseball. The rush to install another new field seems like a fairly big deal, something that merits more attention from ESPN than the second item in Reiss's weekly news and notes column. But, hey, that's what can happen when the NFL owns 10 percent of the media outlet making the editorial decisions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Caley: Texans are on a "crusade" to be the best offense they can be
summary: Last year, the Texans' defense was nearly good enough to propel the team to the Super Bowl with minimal help offensively.
full_text: Last year, the Texans' defense was nearly good enough to propel the team to the Super Bowl with minimal help offensively. The problem was that, in the playoffs, the help from the offense was less than minimal. Against the Steelers in the wild-card round, Houston was clinging to a 7-6 lead entering the fourth quarter, even though Pittsburgh's offense lacked any real punch. Against the Patriots six days later, five turnovers (including four C.J. Stroud interceptions) made it impossible to advance. This year, the defense seems to be as good as it was last year — if not better. On Saturday, offensive coordinator Nick Caley was asked whether the offense has any "extra pressure." "I always take my job seriously," Caley told reporters. "I think everybody else here does. The biggest thing we want to do is be at our best and give ourselves a chance to perform at the highest level we can possibly do. Not to make it any more simplified than that, but that's really what it is. Coming out here, there's a standard. This was sloppy to start today. That's not good enough. We have to do a better job of being more consistent, starting with me. "Moving the needle there, but in terms of the pressure, I think we have a great opportunity to work in this profession. We have great people here with good characters that [General Manager] Nick [Caserio] and [coach] DeMeco [Ryans] have given us. We're busting our ass every single day to be the best that we can be and trying to just be truth tellers to each other. 'Hey, it's either good enough or it's not and here's how we have to rid the bad stuff and be able to move the needle.' That's the reality of it. We're on a crusade to do that. "It's not perfect. We have a ways to go. I want to give ourselves an opportunity to play our best football when it matters the most." It will matter the most in January, if the Texans can do enough to qualify for the single-elimination phase. And if the offense fails to provide a better complement to one of the very best defenses in football, the Texans will be facing some big decisions after the dust settles on the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Downs missed Saturday's Colts practice with a groin injury
summary: The Colts have not had Alec Pierce on the practice field at all this summer and they were missing another wideout at practice on Saturday.
full_text: The Colts have not had Alec Pierce on the practice field at all this summer and they were missing another wideout at practice on Saturday. Josh Downs did not take part in the session and the Colts said that he is dealing with a groin injury. They did not offer further information about the extent of the injury or how long Downs might be out of action. Pierce is on the physically unable to perform list after having ankle surgery this offseason and head coach Shane Steichen said earlier this week that there's no timetable for his return. Ashton Dulin, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, and Anthony Gould worked as the first team wideouts for the Colts on Saturday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers sign QB Kyle Trask, waive two players
summary: Quarterback Kyle Trask officially joined the Panthers on Sunday.
full_text: Quarterback Kyle Trask officially joined the Panthers on Sunday. Word on Saturday was that the Panthers would sign Trask to fill out their quarterback room in the wake of Haynes King's hamstring injury. The rookie was injured in the Hall of Fame Game and is expected to miss some time. Trask was a second-round pick in Tampa in 2021 and he played in seven games as a backup. He failed to make the team last summer and spent time on the Falcons' practice squad during the regular season. The Panthers also announced that they have waived wide receiver Malick Meiga and linebacker Nick Hampton with injury designations.
author: Josh Alper

title: New Cowboys defensive Christian Parker doesn't like media, fans filming practice
summary: The Cowboys love attention.
full_text: ' The Cowboys love attention. New Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker doesn't love one specific aspect of it. Via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News , Parker recently addressed the habit of media and fans filming training-camp practice. “ It’s weird ," Parker said on 105.3 The Fan. "Not a fan." On Saturday, the full practice was broadcast locally in Dallas and streamed online. Parker's boss, Brian Schottenheimer, doesn't share the new defensive coordinator's viewpoint. "You know me, I think at the end of the day, I don't worry about that stuff too much,” Schottenheimer said, per Watkins. “I mean, we all have each other's playbooks. We all know what we run. We have videos going back decades that we can pull up. It's not like they're showing it from a game standpoint; the camera's on, it's moving. Are there things you can get? Yeah. But we get the same thing. So that doesn't bother me.” Schottenheimer's shift may be a simple product of the reality that his boss, Jerry Jones, prefers the reward of extra attention over the risk of competitive disadvantage. “I've not always been that way," Schottenheimer said regarding his current attitude toward the filming of practice. "I think my dad [Marty] was definitely like, absolutely not. I think it's more as I've gotten older and been around it and understanding. And look, we like eyes on us with the Cowboys. It's a good thing. We're proud of our brand and it doesn't bother me." It bothers Parker for one specific reason. In past stops on his coaching journey, Parker's teams used the available footage from Cowboys training camp to help prepare to face them in early-season games. “Once you get past Game 3 or 4, everything is on tape," Parker said on 105.3 The Fan. "When you’re in Week 1 or 2, you’re looking for things. So actually, I don’t know if people realize this, I was following some of our media members and stuff even before I got [to the Cowboys] because when I was in Green Bay and Denver and Philadelphia, I’ve played Dallas in all three spots, us kinda trying to look for things.” Now that Parker is in Dallas, he could be on the other end of that. It's just one of the prices to pay when getting paid to work for America's Team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Have Giants, Saints finally found franchise QBs? History points to Year 2 leaps for Jaxson Dart, Tyler Shough
summary: Dart and Shough don't have to become Eli Manning or Drew Brees, but their rookie seasons suggest they could finally end two long QB searches
full_text:
The Giants have spent the better part of a decade looking for Eli Manning's replacement. The Saints have taken nearly as long trying to find life after Hall of Famer Drew Brees . Different cities, different organizations, same question: did they finally get their guy?
New York cycled through names like Daniel Jones , Tommy DeVito and Russell Wilson before handing the offense to Jaxson Dart . In New Orleans, the list included Teddy Bridgewater , Jameis Winston , Derek Carr and Spencer Rattler before turning to Tyler Shough . Every move started with guarded optimism and ended with the search continuing.
This time feels different.
Not because Dart and Shough are guaranteed to become franchise quarterbacks, but because their rookie seasons in 2025 resembled those of quarterbacks who historically took major steps forward in their sophomore campaigns. Giants and Saints fans have heard such promises before. This time, there are reasons to believe.
Quarterbacks don't usually break out because they throw for 4,000 yards as rookies. They break out because they already show the traits that consistently translate -- efficiency comes before production and limiting mistakes comes before stardom. The breakout usually arrives later, a function of everything else coming together.
To see how Year 2 often unfolds, I looked at every quarterback since 2010 who started at least eight games as a rookie and tracked what happened in his second season.
The quarterbacks who break out in Year 2 don't all get there the same way. But history shows a few recurring paths.
Elite rookie became an even better Year 2 quarterback.
Coaching change unlocked his talent.
Offensive coaching change disrupted his development.
Supporting cast and offensive environment deteriorated.
Knee injury fundamentally altered his trajectory.
The lesson isn't that every quarterback falls into one of these distinct categories. It's that context matters as much as talent.
Herbert built on an outstanding rookie season. Lawrence took off once Jacksonville got the coach right. Prescott regressed when the offense around him regressed ( Ezekiel Elliott was suspended, the offensive line was banged up). Mac Jones lost momentum after an offensive overhaul that included losing coordinator Josh McDaniels. And Griffin's trajectory changed because of injury late in his rookie season. Development is rarely linear, and it's almost never isolated from what's happening around the quarterback.
So where does that leave this year's class? If there's one quarterback I'd bet on to make a Year 2 leap, it's Dart. What surprised me most was how consistent the results were. Whether I looked at historical comparisons or projections, they kept pointing back to the Giants quarterback.
The Giants didn't spend Dart's rookie season trying to hide him. Once he became the starter, Brian Daboll asked him to run the offense, push the ball downfield and consistently make big-boy NFL throws. As the season progressed, Dart looked increasingly comfortable doing exactly that. And while it didn't always work, the results were encouraging.
Dart's rookie numbers were modest: 2,272 passing yards, 15 touchdowns and a 91.7 passer rating across 12 starts. The more encouraging story lived beneath those numbers. Dart consistently challenged defenses downfield while protecting the football -- just five interceptions on 339 attempts -- even after Malik Nabers was lost for the season in Dart's first NFL start.
By November, Daboll wasn't calling games like he was trying to protect a rookie. He was calling them like he expected Dart to make NFL throws. (And, yes, also like he was trying to save his job. Both things can be true.) Dart rewarded that trust. The game never felt too big, and that's a common thread for many successful Year 2 quarterbacks.
Dart's closest rookie profiles produced a variety of successful Year 2 seasons. Bo Nix's statistical output most closely resembles Dart's projected production, while Russell Wilson and Marcus Mariota represent more efficient versions of that same developmental path.
The point isn't that Dart will become Wilson or Mariota; it's that his closest historical comps generally built on their rookie seasons instead of plateauing or regressing.
These aren't projections carved in stone; they're a range of likely outcomes based on how quarterbacks with Dart's rookie profile have historically developed. The takeaway is simpler: quarterbacks who looked like Dart as rookies usually became legitimate NFL starters, not placeholders. That's the standard in New York -- finding a quarterback good enough to stop searching.
If there's one quarterback I think we (and "we" is doing a lot of work here -- I mostly mean "me") may have underestimated, it's Shough. His rookie season hinted at something the box scores couldn't fully capture.
Dart has the higher ceiling, but Shough may have the higher floor. The NFL saw an older, often-injured quarterback coming out of college, and that's why he lasted until the second round. But his rookie season suggested something more interesting: a quarterback who already played the position with surprising efficiency. He completed 67.6% of his passes, averaged 7.3 yards per attempt and posted a 91.3 passer rating over nine starts for a Saints offense that never quite established a consistent identity around him.
Continuity matters, too, with the second-year quarterback returning alongside his second-year coach. There is no learning a new offense. Instead, Shough can grow within the one he already knows.
The names tell an interesting story. Carr, Dalton and Bridgewater: two second-round picks and a late first-rounder, all multi-season starters. Not an All-Pro among them (there are eight Pro Bowls), but all proved they could win in the league. Carr and Dalton started for nearly a decade. Bridgewater was on his way before a devastating knee injury changed his career. Even Minshew carved out multiple productive seasons despite being a Day 3 pick.
As for Shough, his historical comps aren't built around superstardom -- their superpower is stability.
New Orleans doesn't need an MVP. It needs a quarterback it can stop replacing every offseason. For a franchise that has most recently cycled through Carr, Rattler and Haener, stability would be a revelation. Shough does not need to become Brees. He just needs to become the quarterback the Saints stop trying to replace.
The focus here is on Dart and Shough because they're the quarterbacks the historical analysis kept pointing back to. That doesn't mean Cam Ward and Shedeur Sanders won't become good NFL starters. It just means their rookie seasons produced much wider ranges of possible Year 2 outcomes.
Ward belongs in the conversation because he was the No. 1 overall pick and started all 17 games as a rookie. Sanders belongs because he could very well open 2026 as Cleveland's starter. Neither, however, produced the same combination of historical matches and Year 2 projections that made Dart and Shough stand out.
Ward's rookie season looked different from Dart's and Shough's: he threw for 3,169 yards and finished with an 80.2 rating that undersold how much the Titans offense asked of him. The closest Year 2 path is Lawrence: improvement without automatic stardom. Lawrence's second season was cleaner and more productive, but it did not instantly turn Jacksonville into a juggernaut.
Sanders is the opposite. In eight starts, Sanders threw seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, flashing enough ability to keep Cleveland curious -- and enough volatility to keep everyone guessing. He has the widest range of outcomes in Year 2 because he showed flashes that make you think there's more there. He was also more inconsistent than Dart, Shough and Ward.
Sure, Sanders could turn into a functional starter, but he could also remain a high-variance player. Neither outcome would be shocking.
author: Ryan Wilson

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Luther Burden III, Laremy Tunsil, Zay Flowers and more
summary: Keep track of every major injury, setback, and recovery timeline across the league as teams prepare for the upcoming season
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn delivered some troubling news on Tuesday, as first-round pick tight end Kenyon Sadiq is going to miss some time after "having a little setback." There's not an exact timetable for his return, although Glenn doesn't think Sadiq will miss the season opener. The rookie had offseason hernia surgery.
The No. 16 overall pick was the top tight end in his past draft, setting career highs with 51 catches for 560 yards and eight touchdowns for the Oregon Ducks last season. No FBS tight end caught more touchdowns than Sadiq. He was expected to make an immediate impact on this Jets offense, but New York does have another capable tight end in Mason Taylor.
Bailey injured his ankle during Saturday's practice and will likely be considered day-to-day, according to head coach Aaaron Glenn, who also said the linebacker should be "fine."
Pearsall is expected to undergo season-ending surgery on his ongoing PCL injury that has been an issue since last season. Niners general manager John Lynch said that Pearsall is expected to make a full recovery.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
Bosa missed Saturday's practice with "soreness," but 49ers fans can breathe a sigh of relief because head coach Kyle Shanahan said the team has no concerns regarding the star defensive end.
Allen, who had been enjoying a strong start to his first NFL camp, was carted off the field on Saturday after colliding with Kaiir Elam on a special teams drill. ESPN later reported that test conducted on Allen revealed a shin bruise. Nothing was torn or broke, so he appears to have dodged a bullet.
Worthy suffered a shoulder injury on the same day Allen was injured. Andy Reid described the injury as a sprain and said Worthy should return to practice the following week.
During Saturday's practice, Johnson went down and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was aided off the field. He was also seen clutching the area around his Achilles. Despite being carted to the locker room, ESPN reports that Gardner-Johnson merely suffered a lower calf strain, so he avoided any serious injury.
Johnson, 28, was enjoying a solid start to training camp. A seven-year veteran, Johnson's NFL accolades includes a Super Bowl win with the Eagles and leading the NFL in interceptions back in 2022.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
Atlanta brought its Aug. 4 practice to a close after Walker went down with a leg injury. It is feared to be a torn ACL for the second-year edge rusher. His Falcons teammates took knees and surrounded him while trainers evaluated him, and he was then carted off the field. Walker sustained the injury in an 11-on-11 two-minute drill at the Falcons' non-padded practice.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
Former first-round pick Xavier Legette reportedly went down hard on his back and head while attempting to make a catch during drills on Tuesday. After remaining on the turf for some time, the wideout was helped up and carted off the field, per WCNC .
While it doesn't appear Legette suffered a serious, season-ending injury, it was another scare for a team that has already suffered too many losses in training camp. Legette is still looking to live up to his No. 32 overall pick billing. In 15 games played last year, he caught 35 passes for 363 yards and three touchdowns.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press . The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
Brown told NFL Media that he dislocated his thumb at a Patriots practice. Brown returned to practice and caught several passes. "Thumb out of place," he said. "You keep going." This is certainly going to be an important injury to monitor.
Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during the Bears' practice on Monday and is expected to miss 8 to 10 weeks, per ESPN . It's a brutal blow for a Bears secondary that was already one of the thinner units on the team. It's also rough for Bryant, who signed a big free-agent deal with Chicago this offseason.
Burden exited Saturday's practice with a groin injury, according to the NFL Network . He is expected to miss time, but the exact timeline is not clear. The injury occurred during one-on-one drills, and he was spotted limping to the locker room.
Benson experienced discomfort and flaring in his surgically-repaired knee, according to head coach Mike LaFleur. He was feeling better on Monday August 3, which LaFleur said was good news, and added that it's not likely to be a multi-week issue. Still, it's never a good sign when a player who had surgery experiences "discomfort" in the body part that was repaired.
Flowers is considered day-to-day with a left quad contusion, the team…
author: Jared Dubin

title: Teddy Bridgewater retires again at age 33; Lions quickly sign veteran QB Josh Dobbs as replacement
summary: Bridgewater is calling it a career for the second time, but Detroit moved quickly to add Dobbs behind Jared Goff
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' search for a new backup quarterback behind five-time Pro Bowler Jared Goff after announcing that Pro Bowl backup QB Teddy Bridgewater is retiring from football at age 33 after 11 NFL seasons didn't last long. Detroit placed him on the reserve/retired list Sunday.
"Teddy Bridgewater is going to step away," Lions head coach Dan Campbell announced on Sunday . "I've known Teddy a long time. Man, the human being is unbelievable. Certainly the player: everything that he is about, the type of teammate that he is, the way he prepares. Always played the game up here [in his mind] and had a huge heart. He is going to be missed."
The Lions moved quickly to sign his replacement, adding veteran journeyman Joshua Dobbs on a one-year contract Sunday afternoon, according to his agent Mike McCartney . The deal is worth $1.425 million with $475,000 fully guaranteed, per ESPN .
Dobbs, a fourth-round pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers in the 2017 NFL Draft, will join his seventh NFL team . He most recently backed up 2025 NFL MVP runner-up Drake Maye on the AFC champion New England Patriots last season. Dobbs has started 15 of his 27 NFL games , including eight with the Arizona Cardinals in 2023.
Dobbs has thrown for 3,346 yards, 17 touchdowns and 15 interceptions while completing 62.8% of his passes for a 78.3 passer rating. The 31-year-old comes to Detroit well-versed in numerous offensive systems throughout his NFL career.
Bridgewater, a first-round pick of the Minnesota Vikings in the 2014 NFL Draft , overcame a horrendous knee injury after dislocating his knee and tearing his ACL in practice before the start of the 2016 season. The injury derailed his tenure as Minnesota's franchise quarterback, but he rebounded with the New Orleans Saints as a fill-in for Pro Football Hall of Famer Drew Brees in 2019, when Campbell was the Saints' tight ends coach and assistant head coach.
When Brees went down with a thumb injury that sidelined him for five games, Bridgewater balled out from Weeks 3-7, throwing for 1,205 yards, nine touchdowns and just two interceptions while completing 69.7% of his passes. New Orleans won all five games during that stretch. The Saints finished the regular season 13-3 and won the NFC South in part because of Bridgewater's heroics.
That stretch propelled Bridgewater back into the ranks of full-time NFL starting quarterbacks, as he signed a three-year, $63 million contract with the Carolina Panthers in the 2020 offseason. Carolina traded him to the Denver Broncos in 2021.
He eventually reunited with Campbell on the Lions on a one-year, $3 million contract in 2023 to serve as Goff's backup. Bridgewater retired for the first time at the end of that season before unretiring to rejoin the Lions in 2024. He left for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2025 before returning to Detroit this offseason.
Just a few weeks into training camp, Bridgewater decided to call it quits for good. He finishes his career with 15,182 passing yards, 75 touchdowns and 47 interceptions while completing 66.3% of his passes for a 90.3 passer rating in 83 games with 65 starts.
"I'll never forget 2019 when Drew [Brees] got injured, and we had just gone out to the Rams and got beat out there. Drew had his thumb [injury], and we lost him for five weeks. Teddy stepped in, and we won five in a row, man," Campbell said. "That was Teddy. His time being with us [in Detroit] meant a lot, and it meant a lot to our guys. He's going to be missed."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Carson Beck isn't taking Jacoby Brissett's job yet, but the Cardinals like what they're seeing
summary: Arizona has been encouraged by the rookie quarterback since drafting him in the third round, with some in the organization believing he has the tools to eventually become an NFL starter
full_text:
For the Arizona Cardinals staff, the best parts about Carson Beck's preseason performance against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday weren't the two long completions or the final stat line of 15 for 19 for 188 yards.
It was more so things that wouldn't stick out to the casual fan watching the 2026 Hall of Fame Game: the rookie quarterback's work pre-snap, flipping a protection at one point after recognizing an incoming blitz from the Panthers, consistently making the right reads and avoiding bad decisions while also continuing to show his understanding of Arizona's offense.
Yes, it was against Carolina's backups. Yes, the Panthers were vanilla defensively and played just a few coverages during Beck's two-plus quarters of action. Still, it was a stellar performance on national television and -- as shared by multiple sources -- a continuation of what the Cardinals have seen from Beck ever since selecting him in the third round of this year's NFL draft .
"It was another good step for him," a team source said.
That doesn't mean Arizona suddenly has a quarterback controversy. Barring a surprising development, Jacoby Brissett will be the Cardinals' starter when they open the season against the Los Angeles Chargers Sept. 13. Brissett and the Cardinals just hammered out a one-year deal worth $15.5 millio n. Arizona also has veteran Gardner Minshew as an additional backup option at quarterback.
But Beck's work throughout OTAs, minicamp, training camp and now the first game of the preseason has Arizona's staff high on its rookie QB and has left at least some around the Cardinals organization believing the former Georgia and Miami star has the tools to eventually become a starter at the NFL level.
"Everyone thinks he has a lot of potential," a source said. "He works hard. He played a lot of games in college and he's very mature, really smart, can process, can throw the ball and he's an alpha in his own way. It's just about being consistent day in and day out, and that's what he's been doing."
Despite an unfortunate ending to his run as a two-year starter at Georgia, which included an uneven 2024 campaign and a season-ending elbow injury, Beck rebounded last year at Miami by leading the Hurricanes to an appearance in the national championship game while accumulating 3,813 passing yards and 30 passing touchdowns.
In fact, in the week leading up to the draft, there were some high-level NFL front office staffers that thought Beck could go as early as the latter part of the first round. Instead, he went to the Cardinals as the first pick of the third round. They have really liked what they have seen.
"He's been really sharp during (training) camp," a source said. "He's got a shot to be a good quarterback in this league."
author: Matt Zenitz

title: Who's next for Canton? Ranking the biggest names eligible for the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2027
summary: Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson and Ben Roethlisberger headline a star-studded group of first-time eligible players for the 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class
full_text:
In addition to 2026 snubs Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft and Eli Manning, a slew of other big names will be eligible for induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2027.
The list of first-time eligible players for 2027 includes two former league MVPs, a two-time Super Bowl champion quarterback, a former All-Pro defensive back and arguably the greatest tight end in NFL history. To get ready for 2027, we analyze first-time eligible stars in addition to some predictions along the way.
While former Patriots haven't had much luck in recent years, it's hard to imagine that stopping Gronkowski, who wasn't affiliated with Spygate and remains in seemingly good standing with football media.
Injuries may have slowed him down, but it hasn't stopped Gronkowski from being in the conversation among the greatest tight ends in NFL history. Along with being a constant mismatch in the passing game, Gronkowski was a devastating blocker, which strengthens his case as the most complete tight end of all time. His unique talent helped him win four Super Bowls.
Peterson is also widely regarded as one of the best ever at his position. The fifth leading rusher in NFL history, Peterson is the last non-quarterback to win league MVP. That season (2012), Peterson ran for 2,097 yards, the second-highest single-season total in league history. He won his third rushing title at age 30 and was still putting up 1,000-yard seasons at age 33.
The only thing that could hurt Peterson's chances next year is some recent legal issues , including an arrest in October of 2025. Peterson also ended his career with two forgettable seasons, but that alone would likely not be enough to prevent him from being voted in next year.
Roethlisberger is undoubtedly a future Hall of Famer; the question is whether or not enough voters feel that he is first-ballot worthy.
Roethlisberger's career milestones suggest that he is. He's seventh all-time in passing yards (64,088), ninth in touchdown passes (418), a two-time Super Bowl champion and is the youngest starting quarterback to win a Super Bowl. He twice led the NFL in passing yards and has the most 500-yard passing games (four) in NFL history. Roehtlisberger is also the only quarterback to throw six touchdowns in back-to-back games, doing so in 2014. He also holds the unofficial title of one of the hardest quarterbacks to take down.
Roethlisberger's magnum opus was at the end of Super Bowl XLIII, when he capped off the Steelers ' game-winning drive with a touchdown pass to Santonio Holmes that has gone down as one of the greatest plays in Super Bowl history.
Sherman should receive a gold jacket at some point. A member of the 2000s All-Decade Team, Sherman was a three-time All-Pro cornerback and the leader of the Seahawks ' "Legion of Boom" defense, which led Seattle to its first Super Bowl title.
A fellow 2000s All-Decade Team member, Mack delivered impressive longevity for an offensive lineman. He earned his first Pro Bowl nod at 25 and his last one at age 36. In between, he was named to five additional Pro Bowls and was a model of consistency.
Weddle -- another member of the 2000s All-Decade Team -- was a complete safety who excelled in both pass coverage and run support. He led the NFL in interceptions once and had over 100 tackles in a season on four occasions. At age 36, Weddle returned from retirement and helped the Rams win the Super Bowl.
Sherman's condensed prime (he made one Pro Bowl after his age-28 season) could prevent him from being a first-ballot inductee. Mack's lack of All-Pros will likely hurt his case, as offensive linemen are underrepresented in the Hall of Fame. Weddle also played a position that is underrepresented in Canton.
Taking next year off the table, it'll be interesting to see if these players ever get inducted.
McCoy was an excellent defensive tackle who was named to six straight Pro Bowls while manning the Buccaneers ' defensive line. But like Mack and Weddle, McCoy played a position that is often overlooked by voters unless you were the undisputed best at that position for a sustained period of time. For McCoy, that player is Aaron Donald , who will likely be inducted as soon as he is eligible.
Whitworth could potentially receive induction one day based on the fact that he was a two-time All-Pro who, at age 40, helped the Rams defeat his former team (the Bengals ) in the Super Bowl. More Pro Bowl selections would have strengthened his case, though. He was ultimately named to four Pro Bowls, including three straight from 2015-17.
Meteoric highs and lows largely embody Newton's career. In 2015, for example, he won the league MVP while leading the Panthers to a 15-1 regular-season record and an NFC title. He had a forgettable Super Bowl, however, marked by his lack of urgency in recovering his second fumble of the game, which ultimately set up the Broncos ' game-clinching score. Newton also had a short prime that was likely the byproduct of being one of the greatest running quarterbacks in NFL history. It came at a price: exposing himself to major hits.
From a talent and production standpoint, Brown did put together a Hall of Fame career. A former sixth-round pick, Brown built arguably the greatest six-year run in NFL history for a receiver. From 2013-18, he averaged 114 receptions for 1,525 yards and 11 touchdowns per season. He led the NFL in receptions and receiving yards twice and led the league in touchdown receptions once over that span.
Brown won a Super Bowl with the Buccaneers later in his career, but that was after an ugly breakup in Pittsburgh that was followed by even uglier breakups in Oakland and New England. Brown's time in Tampa -- and in the NFL, for that matter -- also ended on a sour note after he ran off the field -- shirtless -- during the middle of a game. It's safe to say that those moments, in addition to some off-field incidents, have put his Hall of Fame future in serious jeopardy.
Haden, Kerrigan, Jenkins, Brooks and Hightower enjoyed long, successful careers that included 15 combined Pro Bowl selections. Each one, however, will likely face an uphill climb for future induction, given that they were never tabbed as an All-Pro. Jenkins, Brooks and Hightower's cases are likely strengthened by the fact that they were key members on Super Bowl-winning teams.
A versatile running back, Bell was on his way to a potential Hall of Fame career after earning three Pro Bowls and two All-Pro nods during his first five seasons while playing alongside fellow "Killer B" teammates Roethlisberger and Brown. A season-long holdout, however, negatively changed the course of Bell's career and all but ended his Hall of Fame chances.
Gore, the NFL's third all-time leading rusher, should be a lock this year after he did not receive enough votes during his first year of eligibility. Suggs, the 2011 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and the owner of the most tackles for loss in NFL history, is surely hoping that a third time is a charm after he did not receive enough votes for induction during his first two years of eligibility.
Like Gore, Jason Witten also didn't receive enough votes last year, his first year of eligibility. If recent history repeats itself, Witten will have better luck this time around. Last year, Antonio Gates, another prolific tight end, was inducted in his second year of eligibility.
Regarding Roethlisberger, it's very possible that voters treat him similarly to Gates, Gore and Witten by not voting him in on his first year of eligibility. Conversely, it's safe to assume that Belichick will get enough votes after he was surprisingly omitted from this year's induction class.
Other players that will undoubtedly receive votes are Manning, Witten (who, like Gore, did not receive enough votes in his first year of eligibility), offensive linemen Willie Anderson, Jahri Evans, Marshal Yanda, receivers Tory Holt, Hines Ward and Reggie Wayne, safety Darren Woodson, quarterback Ken Anderson and defensive lineman…

summary: The Arizona Cardinals annual Red and White Practice is today and we have all the information you need to help you get ready if you are heading out to Glendale. full_text: Arizona Cardinals defensive lineman Walter Nolen III takes photos with fans during training camp at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on July 26, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Arizona Cardinals annual Red and White Practice is today and we have all the information you need to help you get ready if you are heading out to Glendale. While both parking and admission are free, digital tickets will be required for entry into the Red & White Practice. The practice will be from 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. today, gates opening at 3:30 p.m. STADIUM ENTRY: Gates will open on Sunday to season ticket members at 3:15 p.m . and for all guests at 3:30 p.m. Fans can enter State Farm Stadium at BetMGM Gate 1 (west side), Hyundai Gate 2 (north side) and Bud Light Gate 3 (east side). FREE PUBLIC PARKING : Carparks on the east side (Green and Grey) and west side (Orange) of the stadium will open on Sunday beginning at 3:00 p.m. Similar to gamedays, 95 th Avenue will be closed for thru-traffic beginning at 1:00 p.m. SECURITY: In accordance with current NFL security guidelines, all fans will be subject to screening including the use of magnetometers prior to entry. In addition, the NFL Clear Bag policy will be in effect and all fans are asked to limit the items brought inside the stadium to expedite security entry. For more information, please visit www.azcardinals.com/camp . Large strollers, wagons, carts and car seats are prohibited. Umbrella style strollers, cloth baby carriers and booster seats (without pockets) are permitted. FAN SEATING: Open seating for fans on Sunday will be available in the entire lower level of the stadium. AUTOGRAPHS: Following practice on Sunday, the entire team will sign autographs along the lower field wall on both sidelines for a limited time prior to leaving the field. To ensure all fans have an enjoyable and safe experience, fans are asked to be considerate of each other and especially to those younger fans attempting to get an autograph. Guests with disabilities are invited to visit the Kids Zone Waiver Tables on the South Bridge to receive a wristband for a post-practice autograph session. They may be accompanied by one companion who will be assigned a wristband. CONCESSIONS: Stadium concessions will be open for food and beverage needs, offering classic fare, and new items for the 2026 season. There will also be select Training Camp value items for fans to enjoy. All concession sales will be cashless. For more information regarding training camp, please visit www.azcardinals.com/camp .

The signings took place today at State Farm Stadium, site of 2026 Arizona Cardinals Training Camp. Bowman (6-4, 249) most recently […]
full_text: DAYTONA BEACH, FLORIDA - JUNE 7: Shawn Bowman #87 of the Orlando Storm watches the scoreboard during the UFL playoffs against DC Defenders at Daytona Stadium on June 7, 2026 in Daytona Beach, Florida. (Photo by Alex Menendez/UFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals added two players to their 2026 training camp roster on Sunday morning. From the team: The Arizona Cardinals Football Club today announced that the team has signed tight end Shawn Bowman and linebacker Eugene Asante . The signings took place today at State Farm Stadium, site of 2026 Arizona Cardinals Training Camp. Bowman (6-4, 249) most recently played with the Orlando Storm of the UFL and appeared in 11 games where he caught seven passes for 53 yards. He entered the NFL in 2024 with Jacksonville as an undrafted rookie free agent from Rutgers and spent that season on the Jaguars practice squad. While in college, Bowman appeared in 44 games at Rutgers (2023) and Maine (2019-22) and recorded 90 receptions for 984 yards (10.9 avg) and 11 TDs. Asante (6-0, 226) spent last season with the Houston Gamblers of the UFL and appeared in nine games where he tallied 34 tackles (18 solo), four tackles for loss, two passes defensed and two forced fumbles. He entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent from Auburn in 2025 with Miami and spent the season on the Dolphins, Browns and Falcons practice squads. During his six-year collegiate career at Auburn (2022-24) and North Carolina (2019-21), he saw action in 65 games (25 starts) and totaled 196 tackles (120 solo), 14 tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries and a forced fumble. Asante was named to the All-SEC third-team in consecutive seasons (2023-24). Both players will wear jersey #48. Training camp moves are always interesting, especially this late in the process, but we wish both well. The corresponding moves were safety and special teams ace Joey Blount and tight end Kenny Yeboah going to the injured reserve.
