title: The Browns’ “X-factor” on defense for 2026
summary: To use a famous Brady Bunch expression, “Offense! Offense! Offense!” Why is that side of the ball always getting the attention? Unfortunately, even after a good amount of training camp, the Cleveland Browns quarterback situation isn’t any further along than on Day 1, and some drama kicked up on Day 10. RELATED: 3 SECRET SUPERSTARS […]
full_text: Players celebrate a Tyson Campbell interception during an 11 on 11 at the Browns OTA camp in Berea on May 20, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co To use a famous Brady Bunch expression, “Offense! Offense! Offense!” Why is that side of the ball always getting the attention? Unfortunately, even after a good amount of training camp, the Cleveland Browns quarterback situation isn’t any further along than on Day 1, and some drama kicked up on Day 10 . RELATED: 3 SECRET SUPERSTARS ON THE 2026 ROSTER And with all that flux, everybody that covers pro football wants to see if the three-time Pro Bowler Deshaun Watson can rekindle his skills, or if the young Shedeur Sanders is actually the darling of the league and everyone but the Browns know about it. And the media has certainly taken notice. Recently, The Athletic ranked the league’s Top-35 quarterbacks. Yes, there are only 32 clubs, but a few teams have two guys competing for the starting role, like Cleveland. The publication placed QBs into four tiers. Both Watson and Sanders were ranked in the bottom tier, rated #31 and #35, respectively. So, we will see once the pads come on and big boy football begins. The defense, in case anybody wants to know, has really developed. They were ranked #4 last year . Yes, Jim Schwartz has left the building, and we are very sad about that. Hopefully, the new DC, Mike Rutenberg, will keep the scheme intact and pretty much allow the defense to do what it knows to do. There are some new faces and departed players. Right off, EDGE rusher Myles Garrett and LB Devin Bush are gone (insert sad face emoji). LB Quincy Williams will step in for LB Mohomoud Diabate. Also missing is starting DT Shelby Harris. Backups that departed include DE Cameron Thomas, S Rayshawn Jenkins, LB Jerome Baker, DE Joe Tryon-Shoyinka , CB Cameron Mitchell, and S Damontae Kazee. The Cleveland Browns have expectations of not being one of the league’s worst clubs for a second consecutive year. GM Andrew Berry worked overtime this offseason to address the weak spots and bring in new players to replace those who weren’t getting it done. The focus will then be on which players will fit best at all positions. There are many good-to-great players on this year’s roster, and still some problem areas. Hopefully the new backup players will become dependable assets. But there is one player on defense who can change the narrative and perhaps be the difference in games, and is this year’s defensive “X-factor” player: CB Tyson Campbell While most would point to the defensive line position as being the key component to success this year, the fact is, CB Tyson Campbell brought something new to the Browns’ cornerback room last year: and that is a second guy who can play man successfully. With the Browns, we all know the experience and leadership that CB Denzel Ward emits. That is why the team inked him to a two-year extension worth a total of $62.2 million. The new deal makes Ward the highest-paid cornerback in the league currently. With that side signed, sealed, and delivered, the other cornerback side has accolades on its own. Campbell took the place of Greg Newsome , who was a roller coaster in man coverage and an above-average tackler. Campbell is quite the opposite. He excels in man coverage and is an absolute beast in the tackling game. The Browns know exactly what to expect from Ward , who owns five Pro Bowls, including the past three consecutive seasons. With Campbell (6’-1”, 195 pounds) manning the opposite side, the coaching staff doesn’t have to worry about his coverage, doubling his man, or sending a safety over to his side on every play. Campbell is also one of the best tackling cornerbacks in the league, and he continues to be an asset against the run regardless of where he lines up. He has it covered. That is why he is the “X-factor” player for the defense this year. If Campbell falters, then it’s full-go for the other team’s offense. Just toss it long, or in the intermediate soft zones, and watch the yardage add up as the team simply glides down the field. Simple arithmetic. A cornerback who is easily fooled , and a great day of stats for every receiver that passes his way. But Cleveland has the luxury of having two very capable corners to play man coverage. Every team in the league is looking for one great cornerback. The Browns have a pair. And while Newsome was about to be at the conclusion of his rookie contract, Campbell came to Cleveland with three years remaining on his deal. Now with Ward’s extension, the franchise is in great shape with shutdown corners until 2029. The AFC North Division is certainly pass-happy. QB Joe Burrow with the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers love to air it out. QB Lamar Jackson of the Baltimore Ravens will throw some, but their running game is their offensive strategy. With all the greatness at quarterback within the division, Cleveland needs a great group not only at corner, but in the safety room as well. And that is a tight bunch as well. Last year, Campbell started five games with the Jacksonville Jaguars, then all 12 contests once he landed in Cleveland. Throughout his five-year career, he has been very durable, another plus. In his annual stats, he has very few numbers with the pass rush since he rarely is sent on a blitz. His DC has always kept him centered on shadowing his man. But he is certainly active in the run stoppage game. And is a willing tackler. In all 17 games in 2025, he had 87 total tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 0 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 18 pass defenses, 1 QB hit, 1 knockdown, 1 pressure, 1 interception, and 7 missed tackles. With this pass defense last year, his receivers had 92 targets with just 49 completions for 658 yards, 6 touchdowns, and a 52.3 completion ratio. Even if he is beaten, he is excellent at ball strips. No corner is going to knock away every ball, b ut Campbell has a knack at reaching and pulling the ball loose. This has happened over and over. Campbell has gotten comfortable in this defense, whether it is Schwartz running the show or Rutenberg. He has already seen the likes of the other division signalcallers, so that’s not going to be anything new. Straight up: The defense is dependent upon Campbell taking care of business on his side of the field in order to make the defense successful. Who do you think is the defense’s X-factor this year? title: George Pickens explains why his time in Dallas has worked out
summary: The Dallas Cowboys sent a third-round pick in 2026 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 to the Pittsburgh Steelers last May for wide receiver George Pickens. Immediately after the deal went down, there were plenty of eyebrows raised. That’s because during his time with the Steelers, the word was that Pickens had some baggage attached […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys sent a third-round pick in 2026 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 to the Pittsburgh Steelers last May for wide receiver George Pickens. Immediately after the deal went down, there were plenty of eyebrows raised. That’s because during his time with the Steelers, the word was that Pickens had some baggage attached to him. Specifically, he got the “diva” label placed on him, which made a lot of people nervous about the addition. With that said, Pickens ended up having a big year with the Cowboys in 2025 as he set career highs in receptions (93), yards (1,429), and touchdowns (9). Then came the offseason, and the talks about a long-term deal for Pickens in Dallas came about. The hope for many was that it would get done, but executive vice president Stephen Jones shot that down and said that Pickens would play on the franchise tag for a fully guaranteed $27.3 million this season. Despite his reputation in the past, Pickens hasn’t caused any waves since coming to the Cowboys. He spoke recently about why things have worked out up until this point in Dallas, and the people in place around him play a key factor. I’d say the type of coaches and the people around. When it’s a different vibe and environment, then that’s mostly what you’re seeing out of me now. They’re more lighthearted people, ask questions first and see your answer before going with their own narrative. One person that certainly deserves a pat on the back is wide receiver CeeDee Lamb. He and Pickens had a bond before the trade was made due to training together in the offseason when he was still with the Steelers. Since Pickens has gotten to Dallas, he and Lamb have been almost inseparable, which undoubtedly helps him feel secure. Another big factor is head coach Brian Schottenheimer. He has continuously supported Pickens and vouched for his love of the game. Although he signed the franchise tag, there was concern that Pickens wouldn’t be at mandatory minicamp in June. However, Schottenheimer kept saying he expected Pickens to be there, and Pickens was there. He is currently having a strong camp as he looks to show once again why he deserves a lucrative contract with the Cowboys. Yes, Pickens has had a few slip ups when it comes to being late to meetings and stuff like that, but there’s been nothing of any major significance since he got to Dallas, and it’s because he’s learned from some of his errors. Definitely. The older you get, you definitely get mature. Pickens has said that he’s focused on winning a Super Bowl more than anything and that all the financial stuff will work itself out. As for now, the good thing is that Pickens is comfortable, which allows him to be the dominant player that he’s capable of being.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 35
summary: It is Day 35 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: IRVING, TX - JANUARY 8: Guard Nate Newton #61 of the Dallas Cowboys fires off the line to block against the Green Bay Packers in the 1994 NFC Divisional Playoff Game at Texas Stadium on January 8, 1995 in Irving, Texas. The Cowboys defeated the Packers 35-9. (Photo by Joseph Patronite/Getty Images) It is Day 35 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome in for Day 35 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a playoff victory that rarely receives the attention given to the championship games surrounding it. Dallas entered as the defending Super Bowl champion and the NFC’s second seed, while Green Bay arrived as an emerging contender behind Brett Favre. Sunday, January 16, 1994 — 12:30 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Green Bay Packers 17 The matchup showcased two franchises at different stages of their development. Dallas, already the league’s dominant young team, sought to defend its title with Troy Aikman, Emmitt Smith, and Michael Irvin. Meanwhile, Green Bay, under the guidance of Mike Holmgren and Brett Favre, was beginning its return to relevance. Despite a Wild Card round victory over Detroit, securing their first postseason win in 11 years, the Packers faced a much steeper test at Texas Stadium. The game opened with mistakes from both teams. Smith lost a fumble that LeRoy Butler recovered at the Dallas 43-yard line, giving Green Bay an immediate opportunity. The advantage disappeared on the next snap when Tony Tolbert sacked Favre and forced a fumble, which Leon Lett recovered for the Cowboys. Before either offense had established anything, the defending champions had already answered one turnover with another. Dallas attempted to build momentum with a fake punt, but Green Bay intercepted it and took possession at the Cowboys’ 28-yard line. Despite the interception, the Cowboys’ defense prevented the mistake from turning into a touchdown, holding the Packers to a 30-yard field goal by Chris Jacke. Green Bay led 3-0, but the Cowboys had managed to limit the damage from two early failures to just three points. In the second quarter, the Cowboys’ offense settled down. Aikman completed four consecutive passes during a 65-yard drive, navigating through Green Bay’s coverage until Alvin Harper broke free for a 25-yard touchdown. This touchdown secured the Cowboys’ lead, putting them ahead 7-3. Although Dallas had played unevenly in the opening quarter, a controlled possession proved decisive in securing their victory. Favre immediately demonstrated why the Packers believed they had found their franchise quarterback. He connected with Sterling Sharpe for 48 yards, moving Green Bay into Dallas territory. However, the Cowboys tightened near the edge of field-goal range, and Jacke’s 49-yard attempt struck the upright. Instead of reclaiming the lead, Green Bay left Aikman enough time to create the sequence that would change the afternoon. Dallas drove 45 yards in 10 plays, with Aikman using Smith and Irvin to move the chains against a defense that was beginning to struggle with the Cowboys’ precision. Eddie Murray made a 41-yard field goal with 23 seconds left in the half, extending the lead to 10-3. It looked like a useful but unspectacular finish to the quarter. Then the Cowboys’ special teams transformed it into something much bigger. Kenneth Gant forced Corey Harris to fumble the ensuing kickoff, which Joe Fishback recovered for Dallas. Aikman immediately capitalized on the short field, finding Jay Novacek for a six-yard touchdown. In just 23 seconds, the Cowboys had scored 10 points, turning a competitive 7-3 game into a 17-3 halftime advantage. This burst of momentum became the separation Green Bay struggled to overcome throughout the rest of the day. The Cowboys then delivered their best drive of the second half. Aikman completed a pass to Irvin for 18 yards, with a facemask penalty adding another 15. Irvin finished the six-play, 65-yard march with a 19-yard touchdown reception, giving Dallas a 24-3 lead. Green Bay had focused much of its attention on stopping Smith, but that left Aikman and Irvin with enough room to control the game through the air. The Cowboys’ pass rush and secondary ensured the comeback never became serious. Early in the fourth quarter, Jim Jeffcoat deflected a Favre pass that Charles Haley intercepted. Dallas converted the takeaway into a 38-yard Murray field goal, pushing the lead to 27-10. The Packers later drove from their own 15 to the Dallas 15, but Darren Woodson intercepted Favre and ended their last realistic chance to turn the game. This game belongs on the countdown because repeat championships are rarely built entirely from famous moments. Before Dallas could win another NFC Championship showdown with San Francisco or return to the Super Bowl against Buffalo, it had to remove an ambitious Packers team that was beginning to understand its own potential. #Cowboys vs #Packers 1994 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Green Bay Packers 17 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/yZHyXcfQE7 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 9, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Aikman’s three touchdown passes went to Harper, Novacek, and Irvin, showcasedg his control over the game. This victory was more of an Aikman-led triumph than an Emmitt Smith rushing showcase, with 302 passing yards. title: Cowboys add UFL player continuing an offseason pattern
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have quietly found a roster-building advantage by turning spring football into their own farm system. While most teams splash around in free agency, the Cowboys tread lightly, but that doesn’t mean they aren’t stalking the waters, letting the current lead them to an unsuspecting, undervalued talent. In recent years, those waters have […]
full_text: WASHINGTON, DC - MAY 31: Jack Plummer #13 of the Orlando Storm hands the ball off to Jashaun Corbin #6 during the first half of the UFL game against the DC Defenders at Audi Field on May 31, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/UFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have quietly found a roster-building advantage by turning spring football into their own farm system. While most teams splash around in free agency, the Cowboys tread lightly, but that doesn’t mean they aren’t stalking the waters, letting the current lead them to an unsuspecting, undervalued talent. In recent years, those waters have included the United Football League, as they have been rather fortuitous in some impressive All-Pro finds. This season they’ve once again mined the UFL looking for a player who can help make the team better. Before we get into that, let’s run down what they’ve done in recent years to get a stronger understanding of how they used this avenue to score some gems. 2022 – KaVontae Turpin Turpin played for the New Jersey Generals, taking down the league MVP honors in the spring of 2022 after leading the league in receiving yards. He joined the NFL and made an immediate impact, earning Pro Bowl honors as a returner, something the Cowboys never had before in their 60+ year history. While he contributes some as a receiver, his bread and butter is his return ability, earning Pro Bowls in three of his four years in the league, including All-Pro selections in each of the last two seasons. 2023 – Brandon Aubrey Before knocking down long field goals in Dallas, Aubrey was a back-to-back champion for the Birmingham Stallions. And before that, he was a professional soccer player and software engineer. Fortunately, his career path led him to the Cowboys, where he immediately started launching himself into the record books. He broke the record for most consecutive field goals made to start a career, and he also holds the record for most field goals made of 60 yards or more, with a grand total of six! Aubrey has been an All-Pro in all three seasons he’s been in the league and just signed a four-year, $28 million extension. He’s awesome. 2024 – Willie Harvey Jr. After going undrafted and hanging on the practice squad with the Cleveland Browns for a few years, Harvey Jr. got a reboot when he joined the St. Louis Battlehawks. In his second season with the team, he was a first-team All-UFL player, leading the league in tackles in 2024. He was also breaking up passes and forcing fumbles as the crème de la crème of off-ball linebackers that spring. Unfortunately, those achievements didn’t translate at the next level, and the Cowboys’ streak of landing stud UFL’ers came to an end as Harvey Jr. was released during final roster cuts, never playing a down for the team. 2025 – Perrion Winfrey Like Harvey Jr., Winfrey’s pro journey also started with the Browns as he was their fourth-round pick in 2022. He had off-field problems, was released, and then briefly was on the New York Jets practice squad before finding himself out of the league entirely. The Birmingham Stallions gave him new life in 2025, where he put together a strong season, coming up with a huge sack in the USFL championship game. He put up a nice training camp last year, and it looked like once again the Cowboys were on to something as Winfrey was the only UFL player from the 2025 season to make an NFL roster. Sadly, a back injury put him on injured reserve before the season started, and when he finally returned, he only played in one regular-season game. With the team making huge upgrades along the interior defensive line, Winfrey became expendable and was released back in March. 2026 – Jashaun Corbin That brings us to now. On Friday, the team signed running back Jashaun Corbin to replace the recently cut Dominic Richardson. Undrafted in 2022, Corbin spent time on the practice squads for the New York Giants and Carolina Panthers. He played six games for the Giants in 2023, but suffered a season-ending injury in training camp the following year, and just like that, he was out of the league. He then became a well-traveled UFL’er, playing for the San Antonio Brahmas in 2025, where he led the league in rushing. Last year, he played for the Orlando Storm, finishing third in rushing. He showed some all-purpose appeal, adding value both as a receiver and kick returner. He now finds himself in a dogfight for one of the last running back spots on the team in what is already a crowded backfield. The team hopes his one-cut acceleration, good vision, receiving skills, and special teams value could spice up the competition. The Cowboys have a strong track record when it comes to spring scouting, but their luck has faded a bit after coming out hot. Taking a flyer on a player who is most likely to be a final roster cut is no risk, but it has provided some huge rewards when they stick. So, the question is, will Corbin be lightning in a lightning-in-a-bottle strike, or will he soon be a player of no consequence? We’ll find out in the coming weeks.

title: Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson continues to impress

Breyvn Spann-Ford and rookie undrafted free agent Michael Trigg were gaining a lot of steam and dominating discussion about the tight end position. Recently in training camp […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: Jake Ferguson #87 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the main talking points on the offensive side of the ball heading into OTA’s and training camp was who could breakout in the tight end room. Breyvn Spann-Ford and rookie undrafted free agent Michael Trigg were gaining a lot of steam and dominating discussion about the tight end position. Recently in training camp practices, Jake Ferguson has taken over the conversation. Ferguson had a disappointing 2025 season after averaging just 7.3 yards per reception and fumbling three times. He has been a quality player for the Cowboys since being drafted in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL draft. Despite posting a career high in receptions and touchdowns, the Cowboys need a bigger impact from their tight end room between the 20’s, and that’s why people were getting excited about what Spann-Ford and Trigg could add. Through the first weeks of training camp, Ferguson has been one of the better players on the offensive side of the football. Not only does Ferguson look like he’s picking up where he left off in terms of touchdowns in 2025, he is also making a lot of plays up the seams and in the intermediate-to-deep portions of the field. In Saturday’s practice, Ferguson caught multiple touchdowns, and made multiple big plays in team period work. Jake Ferguson TD with Dee Winters in coverage ( @JoeJHoyt ) pic.twitter.com/7k28wm4yeZ — SleeperCowboys (@SleeperCowboys) August 8, 2026 With CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and the Cowboys running game getting so much attention from opposing defensive coordinators, Ferguson has an opportunity in 2026 to put up career high numbers in all major categories with a healthy Dak Prescott. We are just three days away from the Cowboys joint practice with the NFC favorite, the Los Angeles Rams. That will give us all a great glimpse into how high of ceiling Ferguson may have for the upcoming season, but as of now the fifth-year tight end is proving to be ahead of schedule and showing signs that 2026 could be one of the better years of his career.

title: Shavon Revel Jr. is showing signs of growth
summary: One of the biggest stories heading into Oxnard for the Dallas Cowboys was their cornerback room. In 2025, the Cowboys secondary graded out as one of the worst units in the league, and gave up some historical bad numbers through the air. With Caleb Downs, Cobie Durant, Derion Kendrick, and Devin Moore all added to […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 3: Shavon Revel Jr. #28 of the Dallas Cowboys walks onto the field during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 3, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the biggest stories heading into Oxnard for the Dallas Cowboys was their cornerback room. In 2025, the Cowboys secondary graded out as one of the worst units in the league, and gave up some historical bad numbers through the air. With Caleb Downs, Cobie Durant, Derion Kendrick, and Devin Moore all added to the cornerback mix, there was a lot of excitement surrounding the secondaries ability to make a jump in 2026. One of the key factors in that happening was second-year cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. showing positive signs of development. While Revel Jr. has still taken his lumps against George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb so far in camp, Saturday’s practice gave a good look into the growth he is showing during his first full training camp and offseason. Covering George Pickens has to be frustrating as hell. pic.twitter.com/2CCXmt353k — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 8, 2026 Early in Saturday’s practice, Revel Jr. was in perfect coverage on Pickens down the left sideline down in the red-zone. Unfortunately for him, the result was what a lot of defensive backs felt in 2025 with Pickens making a ridiculous grab, despite the tight coverage. For many young cornerbacks, this frustration can lead to more-and-more struggles and eventually lead to a lack of concentration and confidence in their abilities, but like many other practices this offseason, Revel Jr. is maintaining his composure and bouncing back next time the ball is thrown his way. But as he’s done before, Shavon Revel gets his revenge. https://t.co/LNxJ48zUTA pic.twitter.com/mWbsmWgHiL — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 8, 2026 Not long after, quarterback Dak Prescott tried to fit a tight window ball in the back of the end zone for Pickens, but Revel Jr. was in perfect coverage and flashed impressive ball skills to knock the ball away for a touchdown-saving PBU. Revel Jr. is currently in a battle for a starting cornerback job with Cobie Durant to see who will be the starting outside cornerback opposite of DaRon Bland, with Caleb Downs as the third corner when the Cowboys are in nickel. So far, the starting cornerback battle has been one of the most competitive battles in camp with Revel Jr. and Durant both making their fair share of plays in coverage. The lack of talent at the top of the cornerback depth chart was a big reason the Cowboys pass defense struggled last season, but they also lacked any sort of quality depth. While the top end of the depth chart may still lack a true difference-maker, the Cowboys seem to have multiple NFL-level cornerbacks in training camp, and Revel Jr. is proving to be one of those through two weeks of training camp practices.

title: Cowboys news: Dallas head coach makes a point to his players
summary: Heading into his second year as an NFL head coach, Brian Schottenheimer still has a lot to prove despite the legacy his name carries. He made sure his intentions were direct with his players Saturday. After the Hall of Fame game festivities, could another All-Time Cowboys great be enshrined in Canton as soon as next […]
full_text: Heading into his second year as an NFL head coach, Brian Schottenheimer still has a lot to prove despite the legacy his name carries. He made sure his intentions were direct with his players Saturday. After the Hall of Fame game festivities, could another All-Time Cowboys great be enshrined in Canton as soon as next season? Plus, CeeDee Lamb is an amazing receiver but had one thing that was holding him back. 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates – Todd Archer, ESPN Coach Schottenheimer makes sure his message was received loud and clear at practice after things didn’t start the way he wanted. Practice was not very old when coach Brian Schottenheimer wanted to get a point across to the players. While in the middle of individual drills, he called the group together from both practice fields and appeared to light into the players, expletives and all. After the Cowboys were in pads for three straight practices, perhaps Schottenheimer wanted to remind the players that padless practice doesn’t mean less effort. Cowboys legend Jason Witten predicted to make Hall of Fame history with Class of 2027 – Todd Brock, Cowboys Wire Jason Witten had a fantastic career that no doubt will have him immortalized in the Cowboys Ring of Honor some day. Yet, could he already be primed for the Pro Football Hall of Fame as early as next summer? As this year’s inductees enjoy Hall of Fame Weekend and put the finishing touches on their enshrinement speeches, some analysts are already looking ahead to forecast who will join them next summer. According to one expert, Cowboys fans may want to start looking at travel arrangements to Canton, Ohio to witness one of their own receive his gold jacket. NFL.com has made its predictions for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027’s modern-era players , with former tight end Jason Witten picked to not only make the Hall but also perhaps make history in the process. CeeDee Lamb’s drops went away. So what happened? – Cody Warren, Inside the Star Lamb worked to limit and acknowledged the most maddening aspect of his game. I’ve watched CeeDee Lamb make enough ridiculous catches as a Cowboy that you almost expect the hard ones to be the easy ones. Throw it behind him, put a defender in his face, make him twist in midair, it doesn’t matter, he will come down with it. Then we watch the ball hit him right in the hands and it flops to the ground. George Pickens’ blazing hot start in camp, channeling Mamba Mentality-Patrik Walker, dallascowboys.com George Pickens performance of camp is becoming of the late, great Lakers legend. Absorbing competitive cues from three of the best NBA players of all-time, namely, Michael Jordan, LeBron James and Kobe Bryant, the 25-year-old native of Hoover, AL leans heavily into the Mamba Mentality from Bryant, but also the competitive fire and accomplishments of all three. “Oh, I kind of always had it [in me], honestly,” Pickens said of the Mamba Mentality, specifically. “When you hear me say that it doesn’t matter what happens on the field or what happens on — I just want to do my best. When I say sentences like that, it’s the mentality that I have. Malik Hooker all but confirms Cowboys found something ‘special’ in Caleb Downs-Jason Kandel, The Landry Hat Game recognizes game. Malik Hooker, a highly touted Ohio State safety product himself, can see what already separates Caleb Downs from other young players in his position. “Every play he lines up, he feels like he’s gonna win that rep [against anybody], and that’s the type of mentality we want on this defense; and especially coming from a guy that we’re expecting to play a lot,” Hooker said . “And not only play a lot, but to be a difference maker in our defense. Man, to see what he brings to the stable this year too, ’cause, right now, he’s everything they hyped him up to be — a special player.” Stephen Jones offers glimpse where Cowboys could add to roster-RJ Ochoa, Blogging the Boys Once again, the job’s not finished. Stephen Jones explains his thoughts how the team can continue to build the roster despite the team being in full swing at training camp. At one point during the scrimmage/broadcast team EVP Stephen Jones was being interviewed. He was discussing the state of the team’s roster and noted that they have done some small things over the course of camp, but he specifically said that he believed the 90-man roster would look different in the coming weeks. He went as far as saying that he would say this if he were a betting man. Daily discussion question: Who will be the big winner from the preseason opener this time next week?

title: Game week returns to Broncos Country
summary: For the first time since last season’s AFC Championship game, the Denver Broncos will play football this Friday night in Atlanta against the Falcons. While just a meaningless exhibition game, it’s one of the necessary steps toward shocking the football heart back into a beating rhythm for the upcoming season. Speaking of ‘rhythm,’ Broncos play-caller […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 17: Calvin Throckmorton #76 of the Denver Broncos tackles Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on November 17, 2024 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since last season’s AFC Championship game, the Denver Broncos will play football this Friday night in Atlanta against the Falcons. While just a meaningless exhibition game, it’s one of the necessary steps toward shocking the football heart back into a beating rhythm for the upcoming season. Speaking of ‘rhythm,’ Broncos play-caller Davis Webb had this to say: I think I’m looking forward to everyone getting the rhythm — our staff, our players, in and out of the huddle. We’ll learn something every game, every drive. Then we’ll kind of review it as the game goes and especially postgame and try to get three good opportunities before Kansas City on ‘Monday Night.’ It will be rocking, and I know they’ll be a good team. So, it’ll be a good opportunity for us to kind of feel that out because most of these practices are scripted, and we kind of know what we’re going to run and they kind of know what they’re going to run. Not that you need me to tell you, but don’t expect to see many, if any, starters on the field on Friday. If they do find their way onto the field, it won’t be more than a series. Instead, get ready, Broncos Country, to fall in love with that fourth string fullback that flashed against a group of guys with no prayer of making Falcons (or any other team’s) roster – or as I call it, the Joe Don Duncan effect. The gameplans on both sides of the ball will be simplified versions of a limited playbook. Expectations will be focused around execution at every position around every opportunity. Who will rise to the occasion and who shrinks? Are points of emphasis from training camp registering with the players in a way that translates on the field or is there difficulty grasping those core concepts? Expectations in Denver remain high after a disappointing end to an almost-stellar 2025 season. Last season’s excitement won’t return in totality on Friday night, but it’s an important step along the way to getting there. Watch these games to evaluate the position battles. Watch these games to see how Davis Webb and Sean Payton work together (or don’t) to manage the game. Watch these games to root on the Denver Broncos. It ain’t real football yet, but at least it’s football-ish.

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: 5 things we have learned through 8 days of Broncos Camp
summary: The Denver Broncos just wrapped up their 8th day of Broncos Camp, and the intensity has started to pick up. They practiced for six straight days, had the pads on for all but one day, and had their most intense and physical practices yet. During these practices, we learned a lot about the Broncos and […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 29: Jonah Elliss (52) of the Denver Broncos works out during practice at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos just wrapped up their 8th day of Broncos Camp, and the intensity has started to pick up. They practiced for six straight days, had the pads on for all but one day, and had their most intense and physical practices yet. During these practices, we learned a lot about the Broncos and what storylines and narratives will be surrounding them as they head towards their first preseason game of the summer. With all that said, here are the five things we have learned about the Denver Broncos after 8 days of training camp practices. Broncos defensive line remains strong There was some concern that the Broncos may have a hard time replacing veteran John Franklin-Myers. While that still could be factual down the road, currently, the Broncos are showing they have multiple players ready to step up and may even be a stronger overall unit than they were last season. We know about Zach Allen and veteran DJ Jones, but the other players behind these two have been having excellent training camps thus far. Malcolm Roach, who signed an extension with the team last season, has been making plays in the run game and as a pass rusher. When he signed with the team, he was known for his run-stopping ability, but he has proven he can get after the passer and just add some big-time energy to this defense. Head Coach Sean Payton told reporters that Roach has a lot of juice and explained his importance to this team and the defense “He’s got a lot of juice. He’s one of those compound multipliers. A lot of his traits it’s infectious. I’ve said that about [RB] J.K. [Dobbins], you hear him before you see him. They practice hard. I think all the way back to when he was undrafted out of Texas and we signed him, the improvement at his position for him has been remarkable. He’s always going to be looking at what he can do a little better, how he can play on third down relative to the rush. He’s got really good football I.Q. and I think that it kind of shows up on film even at the defensive tackle position.” Roach isn’t the only player standing out along the Broncos defensive line. Enyi Uwazurike, the Broncos mammoth defensive lineman, has been having an excellent camp. Vance Joseph told reporters on Saturday that Uwazurike worked on his body this offseason and changed his game. He said, Enyi has always been a good run defender, but now he is a pass rusher. A 6-6, 320-pound pass rusher who is very strong and has long arms sounds pretty difficult to block, and well, that appears to be the case in Broncos Camp. Veteran nose tackle DJ Jones told reporters that Enyi “can’t be blocked” and that “he’s scary”. "Speaking of Enyi, he can't be blocked… he's scary" 🔥 DJ Jones has some BIG praises for Eyioma Uwazurike 👀 pic.twitter.com/SIjKdEO8Xf — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 5, 2026 Then you have young players in rookie Tyler Onyedim and second-year player Sai’vion Jones who are also flashing a bit in camp. The Broncos defensive line is deep and talented, and we could see a pretty dominant rotation beginning to develop in the Mile High City. A continuous rotation of talented defensive lineman will keep their legs fresh throughout the game and wear down the opposing team’s offensive line as the game progresses. On top of that, the Broncos are five or so deep on the edge as well, so the Broncos’ front 7 remains strong and could be improved if these young players continue to improve and develop Riley Moss is having a great camp One of the potential storylines heading into camp was Riley Moss. He is in a contract year, has a former 1st-round pick in Jahdae Barron pushing him for his job behind him, and some even speculated that he should be traded. Well, Moss has silenced all that noise and is showing the Broncos why they should sign him to an extension. Riley Moss is on track to have a really good year, per Vance Joseph. pic.twitter.com/WvVzJG3RcY — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 8, 2026 Moss has been making plays seemingly every day of Broncos Camp. Sure, the offense has gotten the better of him a few times, but overall, Moss has been excellent. He was pretty good last year too, but his season and performance were tainted by penalties, which, if we’re being honest, weren’t very good calls. However, they happened, and Moss is looking to grow from that and turn those penalties into turnovers by simply turning his head. “Specifically, when I get those ‘go’ balls and stuff, I’m in great position and I was in great position for the most part the entire year last year. Now it’s turning my head and trusting my ability to go and play the ball because the receiver is also playing the ball. It’s just getting out of that habit of that man-to-man instead of just going out there and looking for the ball. It’s a hard habit to break, I won’t lie to you, but that’s why we’re out here practicing. It’s been a big point of emphasis for myself.” Despite these penalties being called on him, Moss isn’t going to change his game. He told reporters that he is going to remain aggressive this upcoming season and that he has always learned the hard way. “My parents have always told me this, I like to learn the hard way. It actually helps me out in those situations because yes they’re going to throw the flag because I’m being too aggressive, but even ‘VJ’ (Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) will tell me, ‘Keep going out there. Keep playing aggressive.’ It happens. I know I need to do better as a whole this season, and I have been. It’s been a big focus of this camp. I’m still going to play aggressive and not shy away from it.” Moss will be a very important part of this Broncos defense. He gets heavily targeted due to teams shying away from CB1 in the NFL, Pat Surtain II, and if he can step up his game, even a little bit, that will make this secondary even better. His future with the team remains up in the air right now, but through 8 days of Broncos Camp, Moss is showing the Broncos why he should get an extension from them. Pat Bryant is ascending One of the biggest roster battles to watch at the start of training camp was for the WR3 job. Star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and veteran Courtland Sutton are your starters, but the battle for snaps and targets behind those two was expected to heat up during camp. Marvin Mims is known for his big plays in key moments, his speed, and All-Pro return ability, but has yet to put it all together as a pass catcher. Troy Franklin had a productive 2025 season, but still left some plays on the field. Finally, Pat Bryant had a productive rookie year that was unfortunately derailed by injuries late in the season. You could make a strong case for all three of these players, but through 8 days of Broncos Camp, there is already a clear winner. Pat Bryant is ascending. Davis Webb likes what he’s seeing from Pat Bryant at Broncos camp so far 👀 pic.twitter.com/A62NhJFkSG — Guerilla Sports (@guerillasports) August 9, 2026 Vance Joseph called Bryant the “complete package” after yesterday’s practice, and offensive coordinator and play-caller Davis Webb had high praise for him as well. Webb told reporters that “Patty Ice has had some really, really good practices,” called him “very, very savvy,” and said it’s really cool to see him take another jump this early in year two. Bryant is going to have a role in this offense, and it could be a significant one. He can play inside or out, can block, has strong hands, and is underrated after the catch. As Sean Payton said, “It’ll be easy creating his role”. “I think his weight’s at a good spot. He has some of the better hands in traffic with his feet on the ground, he’s really good [at] run after the catch. I said this to you guys a year ago, he’s real smart. So he’s someone that can move from ‘X’ to…

title: Broncos’ offense, Payton-Webb dynamic top fans’ early interests from training camp
summary: Whether it’s new Broncos receiver Jaylen Waddle or new offensive coordinator Davis Webb — or just another year of Bo Nix heroics — the Broncos’ offense is what fans say excites them the most for the upcoming season after the first week of training camp. And it makes the most sense. While paying attention to […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 7: Offensive pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos celebrates with quarterback Bo Nix #10 after he threw a touchdown during the second quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Empower Field at Mile High on September 7, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Whether it’s new Broncos receiver Jaylen Waddle or new offensive coordinator Davis Webb — or just another year of Bo Nix heroics — the Broncos’ offense is what fans say excites them the most for the upcoming season after the first week of training camp. And it makes the most sense. While paying attention to the offense is usually the main event for training camp, this offseason’s changes do make it the most intriguing aspect of the team. And so far, all those changes seem to be paying off. Waddle has jumped right into the offense as well as team culture. And he couldn’t be happier with his quarterback. “Bo is great,” Waddle said. “Last week he saw me thinking about the plays, and he kind of just walked up to me and said, ‘Hey brother, don’t think, just play. I got you,’ and he’s been having me. I love Bo.” That’s music to Davis Webb’s ears because there’s no bigger sigh of relief for an OC than knowing his QB and new star wideout are getting along. But even more important than that is just overall growth year to year for Nix. And Webb is confident No. 10 is where he should be heading into year three. “I’m really satisfied where he’s at, both getting in and out of plays, getting to the huddle, getting in and out of the huddle fast, checking plays when it’s appropriate, not overthinking, getting completions underneath and using his feet,” Webb said. “I think the injury last year, it was important for him to kind of move around a little bit early here and I think he’s done a really good job. I’m really satisfied with where he is.” "I think the best team in football that we're not talking about is the Denver Broncos.. They should be the favorite from the AFC to go to the Super Bowl" ~ @danorlovsky7 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/VxWjBNv3MF — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 7, 2026 It’s not just Nix’s surgery recovery that is impressing Webb, either. It’s the cerebral part of the game that is getting better for Nix too. “He’s not someone who’s slow to progress and slow to process; it’s the other way. So there are sometimes where he’s through one so fast where one’s going to be… But I’d rather deal with that than the slow processor who’s getting sacked that doesn’t,” Webb said. “He can get through a progression really fast. I’ll be honest with you, his movement that we’re seeing right now is back to where it was. There are a few plays where maybe he gets closed offers, but his health looks really good.” Sean Payton also noted Nix’s progress as training camp began, particularly in reading defenses. “I think to simplify all of it, the sub-defenses, the third-down defenses that they face in our league sometimes can be a little bit more complex. I think it begins to slow down a little bit when you get into Year 2, Year 3. You begin to see and maybe not get fooled as much,” Payton said. “There are certain indicators, certainly we get a lot of pressure from our defense, and you’re always working to find those tells to help the quarter. So I think in that area, he’s a lot further along.” Webb’s detailed comments and Payton’s obvious interest in the development of the quarterback he specifically wanted to draft, also make the revised working relationship between Webb and Payton an intriguing one, which also seemed to be a big interest among fans (and full disclosure, my poll choice). The head coach gave some interesting hints as to how the new play calling scenario is going to work. “I’m sure in a healthy way… This is going to work,” Payton said when asked how he might interject plays on game day, which will happen. “Yes. Some suggestions, some mandates. (Laughs) . It’ll work fine.” It better.

title: Davis Webb looking forward to Broncos’ offense finding their rhythm in the preseason
summary: One of the biggest storylines to watch as the 2026 NFL season unfolds is how the Denver Broncos will perform on offense. Virtually every starter from last season is slated to return and the franchise made several big additions via trade and through the NFL Draft to boost the unit’s productivity this season. The continuity […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - AUGUST 6: Offensive coordinator Davis Webb for the Denver Broncos looks at a stack of papers during practice on Thursday, August. 6, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images One of the biggest storylines to watch as the 2026 NFL season unfolds is how the Denver Broncos will perform on offense. Virtually every starter from last season is slated to return and the franchise made several big additions via trade and through the NFL Draft to boost the unit’s productivity this season. The continuity on offense is one big reason for optimism. It’s another year of the same scheme, but one significant change looms large. At the beginning of the offseason, Head Coach Sean Payton made it clear that Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb would be calling the plays for the Broncos’ ‘26 gridiron campaign. Though earlier in the week, Payton did acknowledge at times, there will be suggestions [and some mandates] to what plays end up being relayed to quarterback Bo Nix’s headset. After yesterday’s practice, Webb noted that wouldn’t pose an issue for what he hopes to accomplish as a play-caller this year. Considered a rising star in the coaching community—and a good bet to eventually earn the top role for a franchise in the near future—how Webb approaches Denver’s offensive endeavors this year will be of significant intrigue. Last preseason, he called every game, so this isn’t uncharted territory. The Broncos begin the season on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football on September 14th. Before then, they will have three preseason games for Webb to put his play-calling vision and offensive craft to work. This coming Friday will be the first opportunity for that to transpire when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. “I’m looking forward to everyone getting the rhythm. Our staff, our players and now the huddle. We’ll learn something every game, every drive. Then we’ll kind of review it as the game goes and especially postgame and try to get three good opportunities before Kansas City on Monday Night Football,” stated Webb. “It will be rocking, and I know they’ll be a good team. It’ll be a good opportunity for us to kind of feel that out because most of these practices are scripted, and we kind of know what we’re going to run and they kind of know what they’re going to run. We’ll see what happens in a few weeks,” added Webb. Improvement in the passing game is an absolute must for the Broncos’ offense to get to the next level. In order to make that happen, they made a big splash trading for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. With Waddle in the mix, Denver is now five-deep at receiver with Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims Jr., Troy Franklin, and Pat Bryant. Waddle and Sutton figure to be Denver’s top duo. Though it’s uncertain how target share will unfold thereafter. Either way, Mims, Franklin, and Bryant are all talented and add unique dimensions to Denver’s offense. All things considered, it’s safe to say the Broncos have no shortage of weapons at the position to help Nix make a jump in his third season as the franchise’s signal caller. Yet success in the run game will be just as critical if Denver hopes to be a Top 10 group this season. The Broncos drafted Washington Huskies standout Jonah Coleman in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft to bolster their running game. Alongside veteran J.K. Dobbins and second-year pro RJ Harvey, Coleman’s nose for the endzone and ability to run effectively between the tackles should improve Denver’s ground attack efficiency this year. The rookie running back has impressed in camp thus far. However, Webb acknowledged that the depth beyond the aforementioned trio. Players like Jaleel McLaughlin and Tyler Badie, in his opinion, makes them arguably the deepest and most well-rounded stable of running backs in the NFL. “Name six running backs on an NFL team that are as good as our depth right now,” remarked Webb. The Broncos have today off and will have three practice sessions, Monday through Wednesday, before they take on the Falcons on Friday. It’s been a long offseason wait, but we are just days away from real football. I’m looking forward to seeing what Webb can dial up on offense. Sure, it’s just the preseason, but hopefully we see some creativity and aggression right out the gate.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Broncos’ defense motivated to perform better in 2026
summary: Turn back the clocks a few years ago and the Denver Broncos defense was in disarray. It was the first stretch of the 2023 season, and they had just given up 70 points in their Week 3 loss to the Miami Dolphins. Undoubtedly the worst defensive performance in franchise history—and one of the worst ever […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, COLORADO - AUGUST 1: Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph of the Denver Broncos looks on during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on August 1, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Turn back the clocks a few years ago and the Denver Broncos defense was in disarray. It was the first stretch of the 2023 season, and they had just given up 70 points in their Week 3 loss to the Miami Dolphins. Undoubtedly the worst defensive performance in franchise history—and one of the worst ever in the NFL—the Broncos’ defense had hit rock bottom. Fast forward to the present day and the vibe of the defense is entirely different. It’s no longer a disaster. In fact, it has been quite dominant. Led by Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph, the unit has become one of the league’s best. Entering their fourth year in Joseph’s scheme, this year’s defense has a shot at being the best thus far. With a star-filled roster and quality depth at most positions, the Broncos are in great shape. Those factors, alongside continuity and scheme familiarity, are key reasons why the expectations on that side of the ball are sky high in 2026. Yesterday after practice, Joseph stated on how that should help their efforts this season. “It helps because there are certain things that we don’t have to teach in our fourth season together, as far as scheme stuff. Obviously with football, the technique stuff, fundamental stuff, you teach every single day, every year,” stated Joseph. “It’s been fun to watch them coach themselves and to correct themselves. That’s a sign of a good unit. It’s a great unit, but they’re motivated and they’re not satisfied with what we did last year,” added Joseph. Last year, the Broncos were the top force in the NFL when it came to putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. They set a new franchise record with 68 sacks. Though there are some players who believe the defense is poised to break the all-time record currently held by the 1984 Chicago Bears. That’s a lofty statement, but the team’s players are confident that can achieve. However, it wasn’t just sacking quarterbacks that made Denver’s defense one of the best in 2025. As a whole, they ranked third in points allowed and were the seventh-best unit with respect to yards allowed. Their red zone defense was terrific allowing the lowest touchdown rate in the league. Additionally, they were one of the best teams getting off the field on third downs. Two areas for improvement for the ‘26 season are with respect to turnovers and penalties. The Broncos led the league in defensive penalties and yards. On the turnover front, they were in the bottom five with just 14 takeaways. Even with those issues, Denver found themselves on the winning side of fourteen regular season games in ‘25. With one of the hardest schedules, especially early in the season, the Broncos defense is going to be tested right out the gate. While creating more turnovers is a focus of theirs, Joseph emphasized the importance of fundamentals and doing things the right way. If they can accomplish that and stick to their aggressive style of play, he is confident the turnovers will come, and that the defense can be even better in ‘26. “It’s about playing good football. Stopping the run, winning third downs, winning red zone, but also being intentional. When you have a chance to get the ball off the quarterback, you have to do it. It can’t be, ‘Well, I forgot’ or ‘I hope.’ It has to be intentional. I think that’s going to be a non-issue in my opinion. If we play to our play style, I should say, it won’t be an issue.”

title: Pat Bryant continues to make his case at Broncos training camp
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Pat Bryant is having himself a training camp. The second-year Denver Broncos receiver is mentioned as one of the standout players from the media covering the practices on a daily basis. In fact, Bryant made the play of the day on Saturday. To have Bryant consistently showing up and showing out […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 26: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos catches a pass for a second quarter touchdown under coverage by Trikweze Bridges #25 of the Dallas Cowboys at Empower Field at Mile High on October 26, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Pat Bryant is having himself a training camp. The second-year Denver Broncos receiver is mentioned as one of the standout players from the media covering the practices on a daily basis. In fact, Bryant made the play of the day on Saturday. To have Bryant consistently showing up and showing out at this stage is huge for him, the offense, and the Broncos. “I feel like that’s how you are successful in this league, focusing on that consistency,” Bryant said to the media on Friday after practice. “Honestly coming out here every day, working on my craft. As a receiver, you have to catch the ball, so I do that as much as I can.” Vance Joseph with HUGE praise for Pat Bryant. Said he’s the complete package. pic.twitter.com/S5rP7vIrjo — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 8, 2026 We all know the top two receivers in Denver are Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. But there was question as to who would step into the No. 3 spot. Whether it was Bryant, Mavin Mims or Troy Franklin, those were the three guys vying to take that role. At this point, it’s Bryant. As defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said on Saturday after practice, Bryant is the “complete package.” But this will also drive rest of the receivers in that competition to up their game to keep pace with Bryant. “It’s healthy competition is what we like to call it,” he said to the media. “At the end of the day, everybody’s job is on the line, but to come out here and compete, push each other, make sure everybody’s doing their job, helping each other out when it’s needed. At the end of the day, we all have the same goal: let’s go out there and win.” Even Broncos head coach Sean Payton has noticed Bryant’s consistent and strong play. “(I’m) really pleased with how he’s doing,” Payton said to the media earleir this week. “He’s just one of those congested ball catchers. His feet stay on the ground. So when receivers catch the ball with their feet on the ground, they’re usually pretty good run after the catch. You don’t see him skipping in the air or jumping. That means he has a lot of confidence in catching this thing the right way. “I think in college in that final year (at Illinois), I think he had three walk-off touchdowns. Like literally last play of the game in-cuts where he caught it and didn’t … He was full stride when he caught it. If you’re breaking stride for a catch, there’s that tick of a second everyone gets a little bit of leverage on you. He’s extremely smart. He’s doing really well.” There is still a long ways to go for Bryant and the offense. But the fact the young receiver is making the strides he is at this point in his second year is a positive sign. To have a strong No. 3 wide out in this offense for Bo Nix will only make that unit better and harder to defend. “Just going into Year 2 in the offense, I feel like I kind of understand things a little bit differently,” Bryant said to the media. “Then just my ability last year, I played just about every position, so it kind of helped me going into this year. Whenever a guy’s tired during camp, I’ll go out there and take a rep because at the end of the day, I know my job being Year 2 in this offense.” Horse Tracks

title: Discussion: Should the Detroit Lions trade for a backup quarterback?
summary: To the surprise of many, quarterback Teddy Bridgewater stepped away from professional football, leaving the Detroit Lions in need of further depth. They filled that vacancy with haste, signing veteran Joshua Dobbs mere hours after Bridgewater’s departure was announced. While the quarterback room has returned to three-players deep, is that deep enough? Jared Goff is […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 01: Joshua Dobbs #9 of the Arizona Cardinals passes the ball during the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 01, 2023 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images To the surprise of many, quarterback Teddy Bridgewater stepped away from professional football , leaving the Detroit Lions in need of further depth. They filled that vacancy with haste, signing veteran Joshua Dobbs mere hours after Bridgewater’s departure was announced. While the quarterback room has returned to three-players deep, is that deep enough? Jared Goff is the starter and key cog of the franchise. Now that Dobbs enters the fold, the backup quarterback position becomes a true battle between him and undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer. Altmyer was signed by the Lions after the 2026 NFL Draft, meaning he has an extra few months of familiarity with the Lions, but Dobbs’ familiarity with the NFL could give him the edge down the road. Neither Dobbs nor Altmyer are among the elite backups in the league—after all, there is a reason why Dobbs remained unsigned and Altmyer went undrafted. If something were to happen to Goff atop the depth chart, are the Lions really comfortable with either of these players stepping into the lineup? Today’s Question of the Day is: Should the Detroit Lions trade for a backup quarterback? My answer: No. When news of Bridgewater’s retirement was first revealed, there were two thoughts at the forefront of my mind. Firstly, this was an excellent opportunity for Altmyer to stake a claim at a roster spot, regardless of whom else the Lions sign. The second is that Goff is so integral to this offense that almost no available quarterback can replace his production—what really matters is finding a quarterback that can lend a hand in the film room. With Dobbs in the fold, I think that the Lions have all they need in their quarterback room. Dobbs checks a lot of boxes for the Lions. He has familiarity with Drew Petzing from their time in Arizona, including eight starts. Although the Arizona Cardinals went 1-7 in those games started by Dobbs, it is worth remembering that their roster was subpar at best, a supporting cast including James Conner, Trey McBride (before his ascension to elite tight end), Marquise Brown, and a rookie Michael Wilson. Dobbs himself was not awful in those games either, throwing for eight touchdowns, five interceptions, and 1,569 yards across those eight games, as well as scrambling for 258 yards and three touchdowns. When you examine the other free agent quarterbacks still available on the market, only players like Jimmy Garoppolo, Russell Wilson, and Trevor Siemian have more starts than Dobbs. When you factor in Dobbs’ intangibles (he is known as “the Passtronaut” for a reason), he is about as good of a backup as you can sign in the middle of August—experienced, athletic, smart, and, best of all, inexpensive. Via trade, you might be able to get an upgrade, but not without a larger price tag. Looking around at NFL rosters, there is a bevy of veteran backups with starting experience, such as Marcus Mariota, Carson Wentz, or Andy Dalton. However, are any of these players such an upgrade over Dobbs to warrant trading away assets? I personally do not think so. You can also consider former draft picks that have fallen out of favor. Players like Will Levis, Spencer Rattler, and Anthony Richardson are no longer viewed favorably for their respective teams, so a change of scenery would make sense. Yet these players have fallen down the depth chart for a reason—would it truly benefit Detroit to take on a reclamation project at an important position during a pivotal season? If Goff gets hurt, I personally would not want a player like Levis or Richardson stepping in. For as high as their ceilings are, I want a backup to have a safe floor. With Dobbs and Altmyer on the roster, I think the Lions are in a decent position. At the end of the day, Goff is irreplaceable to this team, and any injury replacement would be treading water at best—good quarterbacks are hard to find in this league. Preseason has not yet started. Let us give Dobbs and Altmyer some time to show if reinforcements are truly needed. Join the conversation! title: Trevon Diggs among 8 Detroit Lions free agent tryouts
summary: The Detroit Lions tried out eight different players, according to Sunday’s NFL transaction list, including former Dallas Cowboys All-Pro cornerback Trevon Diggs. The following players were in Allen Park to try out: Plummer and Haener reportedly impressed during their workouts, but the Lions opted to sign veteran Josh Dobbs to fill the hole left by […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Trevon Diggs #7 of the Dallas Cowboys in action against the Washington Commanders during the first half of the NFL game at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions tried out eight different players, according to Sunday’s NFL transaction list, including former Dallas Cowboys All-Pro cornerback Trevon Diggs. The following players were in Allen Park to try out: QB Jack Plummer QB Jake Haener WR Julian Hicks WR Ray-Ray McCloud LB Amari Burney LB Milo Eifler LB Amen Agbongbemiga (Lions signed him) DB Trevon Diggs Plummer and Haener reportedly impressed during their workouts , but the Lions opted to sign veteran Josh Dobbs to fill the hole left by Teddy Bridgewater’s sudden retirement. Dobbs’ signing, as of Sunday evening, was still not yet official, but he’s agreed upon a one-year, $1.425 million deal, with $475,000 guaranteed, per reports . Hick and McCloud’s workout comes off the heels of veteran Cedrick Wilson Jr. missing Sunday’s practice. As of right now, Wilson’s absence is not yet explained, but the working out of two receivers could be a sign Detroit will need some reinforcements at the position. Hicks (6-foot-2, 201) went undrafted in 2024 and has yet to make an NFL appearance, while McCloud (5-foot-9, 190) is an eight-year veteran who last significant contributed in 2024, when he started 13 games for the Falcons and put up 686 yards. Burney and Eifler tried out, but it appears the Lions opted to go with Agbongbemiga, instead. We previously wrote a story about the signing of the special teams-heavy linebacker here . But the big name here is Diggs. The 27-year-old cornerback was an immediate hit with the Dallas Cowboys as a second-round pick. In his second season (2021), Diggs led the NFL in interceptions (11), was named to the Pro Bowl, and received First Team All-Pro honors. After a decent follow-up season (three interceptions, 14 passes defended, another Pro Bowl), it’s been a bit of a struggle for Diggs. He suffered a torn ACL two games into his 2023 season, didn’t quite look the same in a shortened 2024 season, and ended up being cut midseason last year. He lasted two games when the Packers picked him up, and he’s been a free agent since. Detroit has a need for some cornerback depth after waiving Terrion Arnold this offseason, but it remains to be seen whether they will actually sign Diggs or not.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 training camp observations, Day 9: Veteran rest opens door for reserves
summary: After four days in pads and a day off on Saturday, the Detroit Lions returned to the practice field on Sunday for a scaled-back practice that lasted just under two hours. While on the field, the team ran position drills, two team sessions, an extended special teams session, offensive line vs. defensive line one-on-ones, seven-on-sevens, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive back Nick Whiteside (38) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After four days in pads and a day off on Saturday, the Detroit Lions returned to the practice field on Sunday for a scaled-back practice that lasted just under two hours. While on the field, the team ran position drills, two team sessions, an extended special teams session, offensive line vs. defensive line one-on-ones, seven-on-sevens, and finished the day with a situational team drill. However, the team rested several of their marquee players, opening up opportunities for several reserves to stand out. Injury updates Jeremy Reisman wrote a full report on Sunday’s injury updates , with several heavy hitters getting some rest on Sunday: Penei Sewell, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Alim McNeill, DJ Wonnum, and Levi Onwuzurike all exited after warm-ups or individual work, while Jameson Williams’ practice came to a conclusion after the first set of team drills. Amongst the injured players we’ve previously been tracking, Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Moore, and Mekhi Wingo were seen working with trainers. Of the players returning to practice, Jahmyr Gibbs was back in full, Ben Bartch expanded his participation to team drills, and Tyler Conklin was taking part in everything except team drills. The “Replacements” With a lot of starters resting, here’s a quick rundown of who was replacing them in the lineup: No St. Brown and Williams meant a steady rotation of players around Isaac TeSlaa, the most notable being Greg Dortch and Tay Martin. With Conklin limited, both Jackson Meeks and Thomas Gordon got their chances in the TE3 spot. Larry Borom replaced Sewell at left tackle, with some Miles Frazier mixed in. With Juice Scruggs out, Bartch took reps at left guard on the second team, repping behind Christian Mahogany. When he rested, Michael Niese got some work in with the second team at guard. With Hutchinson and Wommun resting, along with Moore injured, that left Anthony Lucas as the next in line at the Rush End. No McNeill, Onwuzurike, or Wingo opened the door for Myles Adams to start at the 3-technique, but he ended up giving reps to Skyler Gill-Howard, who showed very well throughout the day. With Campbell resting and Jimmy Rolder injured, Joe Bachie took over starting MIKE duties and was backed up by Troy Reeder. No Malcolm Rodriguez or Damone Clark meant that Devin White started at WILL unchallenged and was backed up by Erick Hunter. No D.J. Reed meant another opportunity for Nick Whiteside to start opposite Rock Ya-Sin, and with few nickel packages on the agenda, that meant that Ennis Rakestraw was pushed to the second team. This decision to start Whiteside over Rakestraw could mean that either Ya-Sin has beaten him for the CB2 job, or that Rakestraw could be pushing inside on a more regular basis—he’s been the team’s starting nickel for the past few practices. We’ll see how this plays out as the week progresses. Situational team drill The Lions ran three series of team drills on Sunday. The first series featured some positive play from defensive linemen like Lacy and Gill-Howard. The second series was full of sloppy play from the offense (three false starts in 10 plays), with Tyleik Williams ending up stealing the show with a brilliant tackle for loss. The final team series featured an end-of-game situational drill that showed the most promise from the offense, but they ended up coming up short. The third series started with a Jack Fox punt that traveled the length of the field, with media estimates of the ball traveling 70-80 yards, setting up the offense to start at their own 20-yard line, down four points and just under one minute remaining on the clock . The first down play saw immediate pressure up the middle from Gill-Howard, forcing a throwaway. Second down saw an incomplete pass from Jared Goff targeting Dortch. Then, on third-and-10, Goff hit Gibbs on a modified slot-wheel route that went for 17 yards and a first down. The offense used their only timeout. Goff immediately went back to the air on first down, hitting Dortch on a seam route with Roger McCreary in coverage, gaining 31 yards. The offense rushed to the line and spiked the ball, setting up second-and-10. Goff went back to Dortch again, but overthrew him; however, a defensive penalty was called, and the offense was granted an automatic first down. Now at the opponent’s 28-yard line, Goff threw a quick out to Gibbs for a quick gain of five yards, followed by a spike on second down, setting up third and five from the 23 with around 11 seconds left on the clock. The defense deployed zone coverage and shut down the passing lanes on third down, and while Goff tried to push it to Isaac TeSlaa in the back of the end zone, the pass was too high. On fourth down, the offense needed to gain 23 yards to get into the end zone, and down four points, with just four seconds remaining on the clock, they needed to score a touchdown. Goff once again looked TeSlaa’s way, hoping to get the lengthy receiver at the front of the end zone, but with the defense in prevent, it was Nick Whiteside who jumped the route and secured the interception to get the win for the defense. One-on-ones; OL vs. DL All camp, I have made a point to talk to Lions legend Lomas Brown about these trench drills, and on Sunday, he cautioned me not to read too much into this drill without pads, as some players have a disadvantage in shells. With that in mind, I’ll focus on some of the highlights where there were clear winners. Cade Mays has often been impacted by Tyleik Williams’ power in these drills, initially getting pushed back before fighting to re-anchor. On Sunday, Mays was aggressive early in the rep, trapped Williams, and won both his reps. Miles Frazier continues to rep all over the line and took reps at left tackle, left guard, right guard, and right tackle, winning all five of his opportunities. Larry Borom looked solid, getting wins over Tayler Lacy (twice) and Lucas. Ahmed Hassanein deployed a wicked double-swipe on Blake Miller that caught the rookie off-guard and opened the edge for Hassanein to get by him. His aggression got the better of him vs. Frazier, leading to him getting off balance and slipping when bending the edge. Gill-Howard got a quick win over Tate Ratledge (a rare loss), a nice feather in his cap for the rookie. UDFA rookie Melvin Priestly showed off some nice power at guard, then shifted inside and took reps at center, beating Chris Smith and Ben Stille. The only defensive player who won more than one rep was UDFA Eric O’Neill, who secured wins over Miller and Colby Sorsdal It was a tough day for Blake Miller, who lost to Hassanein and O’Neill, but got the better of Tyre West, though he did show much better in team drills. These days happen for rookies. Special teamers beginning to separate In the competition for the Lions’ gunner roles, we’ve seen a few players consistently winning their one-on-ones, illustrating how they’re separating themselves from the pack. On Sunday, Khalil Dorsey, Christian Izien, and Ya-Sin won all their one-on-ones, both as gunners and blockers. When the team went to a live drill, it was Dorsey and Izien as the starting gunners, followed by Whiteside and Tay Martin with the second team. With Ya-Sin in pole position to win the CB2 job, it appears clear that Dorsey and Izien look like they have the lead for the team’s gunner roles.
