title: Detroit Lions training camp injury updates: Good news on D.J. Reed
summary: The Detroit Lions held a shorter practice on Sunday, but they opted to hold out a bunch of their best players after four days of padded practice last week. It appears to be precautionary with all of them, so don’t get too concerned with the names you see below. Plus, there is some good news […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 21: D.J. Reed #4 of the Detroit Lions takes the field prior to a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Ford Field on December 21, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions held a shorter practice on Sunday, but they opted to hold out a bunch of their best players after four days of padded practice last week. It appears to be precautionary with all of them, so don’t get too concerned with the names you see below. Plus, there is some good news to deliver when it comes to D.J. Reed, Derrick Moore, and Malcolm Rodriguez. Returned to practice: RB Jahmyr Gibbs (hold-in, back) TE Tyler Conklin (calf) G Ben Bartch (undisclosed) Gibbs and Conklin both got some team reps for the first time in training camp. They appear ready to start getting worked into the mix, but it wasn’t a full workload for either player. Bartch also got some team work, but a very small amount. Coach Dan Campbell said that he hasn’t suffered any setbacks, but he hasn’t quite recovered as expected. Now he needs to make up for some lost time. “I’d be lying to you if I said I wasn’t hopeful he would have been out there more than now, but I also know there’s no setbacks, anything like that and he’s a veteran guy,” Campbell said. “From what we know about him and the short time we’ve been around him, he’s a guy that, it means something to him. He’s smart, he’s conscientious, all those things. […] There’s a reason he’s here, we think he brings outstanding competition. He’s got a shot, but certainly he’s behind the mark. I mean, he’s missed some days.” Appeared to be limited: WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (undisclosed) WR Jameson Williams (undisclosed) OT Penei Sewell (undisclosed) LB Jack Campbell (undisclosed) DT Alim McNeill (undisclosed) DT Levi Onwuzurike (undisclosed) EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (undisclosed) EDGE DJ Wonnum (undisclosed) Now, before you panic about this list, it’s worth noting that Campbell said before practice that there were a bunch of “bumps and bruises” on the roster, so they were holding several out as a precaution. Hopefully, we’ll get some more specific answers on all of these players later in the week. All of these players were on the field for walkthrough and warmups, but with the exception of Jameson Williams, none appeared to participate in any team drills by our observations—and Williams only got a limited amount of team work. Working with trainers, not practicing: EDGE Derrick Moore (groin) DT Mekhi Wingo (groin) LB Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) It was certainly promising to see Moore back out there. Last we heard from Campbell, he was on a 7-10 day timeline of returning from injury and that was six days ago. Wingo and Rodriguez have only missed a couple practices, suggesting their injuries are not serious. Not practicing: QB Teddy Bridgewater (retired) RB Isiah Pacheco (undisclosed) RB Sione Vaki (eye, broken nose) WR Greg Dortch (undisclosed) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) G Juice Scruggs (undisclosed) EDGE Payton Turner (back) DT Aidan Keanaaina (undisclosed) LB Damone Clark (undisclosed) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) CB D.J. Reed (groin) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Dortch and Clark are two new additions to the absentee list. No update on their conditions was given. However, Campbell offered positive news on No. 1 cornerback D.J. Reed, who has been sidelined since Thursday. “That’s not a major issue. We feel good about that. When he’s ready, he’ll be ready to go,” Campbell said. The news wasn’t as promising for Turner, who hasn’t practiced since the very first day of training camp. “Yeah, nothing new really,” Campbell said. “I mean, he’s got a back (injury) that we’re just trying to get to calm down and that’s a day-to-day type thing.” Injured during practice EDGE Ahmed Hassanein Hassanein spent a couple minutes down on the ground while trainers attended to his left lower leg toward the end of practice. He walked off the field under his own power with tape around his left ankle. The team did not deem the injury significant enough to warrant a post-practice update, which is good news, but it’s something to watch moving forward.

title: Detroit Lions signing QB Josh Dobbs to replace Teddy Bridgewater
summary: The Detroit Lions are signing veteran quarterback Josh Dobbs, according to a report from NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. Dobbs comes into Detroit to help out their quarterback room following the sudden retirement of Teddy Bridgewater. Dobbs is a very natural fit to join the Lions for several reasons. For one, he’s no stranger to Detroit. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 12: Joshua Dobbs #11 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to the game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 12, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions are signing veteran quarterback Josh Dobbs, according to a report from NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. Dobbs comes into Detroit to help out their quarterback room following the sudden retirement of Teddy Bridgewater. Dobbs is a very natural fit to join the Lions for several reasons. For one, he’s no stranger to Detroit. He spent two weeks on the Lions’ practice squad in 2022 before he was poached by the Arizona Cardinals. That Cardinals team, of course, had Drew Petzing as their offensive coordinator at the time. Dobbs would end up starting eight games for the Cardinals in 2023 before Arizona traded him to the QB-needy Vikings midseason. Dobbs would start another four games that season in Minnesota. So Dobbs has experience with both Campbell and Petzing, which should give him a head start before joining the team in training camp shortly. In 15 career starts, Dobbs has completed 351-of-559 passes (62.8%) for 3,346 yards (6.0 Y/A), 17 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. Dobbs will now be in competition for the backup job with undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer. The 23-year-old former Illini quarterback has been accumulating a lot of reps over the past three practices with Bridgewater out, and the Lions have been impressed with his progress. “We like Luke, Luke is growing, Luke is getting better, he just needs reps,” coach Dan Campbell said Sunday. “I mean, he needs a million reps. But the reps that he has gotten to this point, he has improved.” Despite just joining the team, Dobbs is likely to come in and get some playing time in Detroit’s upcoming preseason debut on Thursday against the Cincinnati Bengals. Campbell has already said they don’t plan to play Jared Goff, and while they want to give Altmyer a lot of looks, giving him an entire game would be a big ask. “Certainly Altmyer’s going to take a heavy load and then anybody else we get, we’ll get them up to speed as fast as we can and give them some reps,” Campbell said. The Lions haven’t officially announced the move, so the corresponding transaction is currently unknown. Update: The Lions also reportedly worked out quarterbacks Jake Haener and Jack Plummer .

They officially placed Teddy Bridgewater on the reserve/retired list, signed cornerback Ryan Cooper and linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga, and waived tight end Nick Muse. Bridgewater’s move to the retirement list comes minutes after Dan Campbell announced the veteran quarterback is stepping […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 18: Amen Ogbongbemiga #45 of the Chicago Bears stands on the field during the fourth quarter of an NFL divisional playoff game against the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field on January 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced a flurry of roster moves ahead of Sunday’s training camp practice. They officially placed Teddy Bridgewater on the reserve/retired list, signed cornerback Ryan Cooper and linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga, and waived tight end Nick Muse. Bridgewater’s move to the retirement list comes minutes after Dan Campbell announced the veteran quarterback is stepping away. “I’ve known Teddy a long time, and, man, the human being is unbelievable,” Campbell said. “Certainly the player, everything he’s about, the teammate that he is, the way he prepares. Always played the game up here and had a huge heart. He’s going to be missed.” Campbell said the team intends to sign a veteran backup quarterback and hopes to do so by Monday. Cooper was one of three defenders who tried out for the Lions over the weekend . He last played football with the Birmingham Stallions of the UFL, posting 25 tackles, four pass breakups and an interception in nine games. At 5-foot-11, 184 pounds, Cooper has only made one game appearance at the NFL level, playing six special teams snaps for the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Detroit needed a little cornerback depth while D.J. Reed is sidelined with a minor groin injury and the Lions waived De’Shawn Rucker with an injury designation. Ogbongbemiga has been in the NFL for five seasons, appearing in 72 games and making three starts since 2021. He went undrafted in the NFL but was a first-round pick in the CFL in 2021. He opted to go the NFL route, making the Los Angeles Chargers 53-man roster as a rookie and appearing in 15 games. He lasted two more years with the Chargers, playing mostly on special teams—932 snaps on teams over three years. For the last two seasons, he’s been with the Bears. Again, he was a core special teamer for Chicago, logging 499 snaps before the team cut him earlier this offseason in February. Detroit has also been a bit shorthanded at linebacker with Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) and Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) dealing with injuries. In short: In: CB Ryan Cooper LB Amen Ogbongbemiga Out: QB Teddy Bridgewater (retired) TE Nick Muse (waived)

title: QB Teddy Bridgewater is leaving the Detroit Lions, team seeking vet backup
summary: The Detroit Lions will have a new backup quarterback for the 2026 season. Lions coach Dan Campbell announced on Sunday that Teddy Bridgewater is stepping away from the team. When asked if this was a retirement from Bridgewater, Campbell suggested that’s where things currently stand. “I think only he can truly answer that, but I […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 05: Teddy Bridgewater #12 of the Detroit Lions reacts after the Lions defeated the Minnesota Vikings, 31-9, at Ford Field on January 05, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions will have a new backup quarterback for the 2026 season. Lions coach Dan Campbell announced on Sunday that Teddy Bridgewater is stepping away from the team. When asked if this was a retirement from Bridgewater, Campbell suggested that’s where things currently stand. “I think only he can truly answer that, but I feel like this is where it’s at for sure right now,” Campbell said. “This is where it needs to be and where he felt.” That leaves the Lions a little precarious at the backup quarterback position, as the only other rostered quarterback beyond Jared Goff is undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer. Campbell said he intends to add a veteran quarterback to help the depth of the room, but they also like where Altmyer is currently at in his development. “We like Luke. Luke is growing,” Campbell said. “Luke is getting better. He just needs reps. I mean, he needs a million reps. With the reps that he has gotten at this point, he is improved. So, we like him, but we are going to add somebody, and we’d like to add a veteran quarterback. We’re hoping maybe something happens tomorrow.” As for Bridgewater, Campbell made sure to express his appreciation for his time together, both in Detroit and New Orleans. “I’ve known Teddy a long time, and, man, the human being is unbelievable,” Campbell said. “Certainly the player, everything he’s about, the teammate that he is, the way he prepares. Always played the game up here and had a huge heart. He’s going to be missed.” Campbell also noted that the veteran quarterback was concerned he was letting the team down. “His biggest worry was letting us down,” Campbell said. “That’s the type of guy he is.”

title: More Penei Sewell trick plays coming in 2026?
summary: Thus far, we’ve seen the Detroit Lions attempt to execute two trick plays involving offensive tackle Penei Sewell. The first came in a key game against the Minnesota Vikings in 2022 when Sewell made an athletic, game-clinching catch after being lined up as a tight end. The second was a far less successful attempt to […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 11: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions catches the ball in the fourth quarter of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on December 11, 2022 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thus far, we’ve seen the Detroit Lions attempt to execute two trick plays involving offensive tackle Penei Sewell. The first came in a key game against the Minnesota Vikings in 2022 when Sewell made an athletic, game-clinching catch after being lined up as a tight end . The second was a far less successful attempt to get Sewell to attempt a throw against the Bears in 2024 , which technically went down as a sack, but also involved an awesome stiff-arm. It’s quite possible there will be a trilogy of trick plays involving Sewell, and that third installment could come in 2026. During an interview with NFL Network on Friday, Lions coach Dan Campbell admitted that they plan on installing some plays involving Sewell as an offensive weapon . “Not yet, but we will,” Campbell told the NFL Network crew. “We will. Look, he’s a versatile—I’ve said this all along—he’s a weapon. He’s a weapon. He plays on the o-line, but there’s so much he can do.” What that trick play will look like remains a mystery, but we do know the Lions have an offensive coaching staff that is more than willing to throw out trick plays. Last year, Mike Kafka—now the Lions’ pass game coordinator, then the Giants’ interim head coach—dialed up a few successful trick plays for New York against the Lions. And while offensive coordinator Drew Petzing doesn’t have an extensive history of pulling out some trick plays, Campbell spoke about how impressed he’s been with him thus far. “I was always intrigued with Drew in crossover tape of some of the things he was able to do,” Campbell said. “Man, the run game, but also matchups in the pass game. I thought he did a lot with little (in Arizona). They didn’t have some of the pieces we’ve got here, and I thought he did a great job of finding those matchups and using them.” Could one of those new matchups involve Penei Sewell as a receiver? We’ll have to wait and see.

title: Jahmyr Gibbs contract details: New strategies from Detroit Lions
summary: The full contract details of Jahmyr Gibbs’ three-year extension are out, and it reveals a ton of interesting things about how the Detroit Lions approached this deal. Before I get into the nitty-gritty, here’s how the overall contract looks, including overall cap hits and “dead cap if cut.” [Note: This does not include the incentives […]
full_text: Jun 17, 2026; Detroit, MI, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs drills during the Detroit Lions veteran’s minicamp at the Allen Park Training Facility. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The full contract details of Jahmyr Gibbs’ three-year extension are out, and it reveals a ton of interesting things about how the Detroit Lions approached this deal. Before I get into the nitty-gritty, here’s how the overall contract looks, including overall cap hits and “dead cap if cut.” [Note: This does not include the incentives built into Gibbs’ contract. More on that later.] What’s different about Jahmyr Gibbs contract? It’s a pretty stark difference from how the Lions treated some of their recent extensions. For one, there is only one option bonus—a strategy Detroit has used annually on some of their most recent contracts. We broke down what option bonuses are in relation to Kerby Joseph’s contract here . Additionally, there is just one void year on the deal—but plenty of room to restructure and add void years, if desired. Those two things combined allow the Lions a little wiggle room toward the end of Gibbs’ contract. If they want to get out of the contract, the lack of prorated option bonuses leaves less guaranteed (dead) money to worry about, particularly in that final year. If they want to extend Gibbs or lower his cap hit, the high base salaries allow for simple restructures. But there is one caveat to all of this… Rolling guarantees make this contract harder to cut Jahmyr Gibbs This contract is loaded with rolling guarantees. What are rolling guarantees? Basically, it’s a way for a player to ensure some of their salary is guaranteed a year prior to the next season. For example, let’s take Gibbs’ 2028 salary. $8 million of it is already guaranteed. He’s getting that money—and the Lions are taking that cap hit—even if he’s cut before 2028. The remaining $2.25 million in 2028 salary becomes guaranteed if he’s still on the roster in March of 2027 . So, in essence, if the Lions were to cut Gibbs in 2028, they would still be on the hook for that entire salary, because it became fully guaranteed in March of 2027. Here are the other rolling guarantees in his contract: If on the roster in March 2028, $8 million of his 2029 salary is guaranteed If on the roster in March 2029, the $3.5 million of his 2029 salary is guaranteed So even if the Lions cut Gibbs before March of 2029, they will still have to take cap hits for: Two more remaining signing bonus prorations (2029, 2030): $3 million each Three more remaining option bonus prorations (2029, 2030, 2031): $2,006,600 each $8 million in 2029 salary that became guaranteed in March 2028: $8 million … for a total of $20,019,800 in dead cap—saving just under $7.5 million in cap space. While the Lions can get out of the contract in 2029, it’s much more costly than it looks at first glance. That said, Detroit could utilize the June 1 designation to cut that year, splitting the ~$20 million in dead cap over two years ($13 million in 2029, $7 million in 2030). But Detroit is getting early cap relief Gibbs’ 2026 cap hit did increase by $3 million (new signing bonus proration), because there was nothing they could do with his minimum salary (it was fully guaranteed). However, they will certainly feel some relief in 2027. After Detroit exercised Gibbs’ fifth-year option, they were staring down a $14.29 million fully guaranteed salary. His 2027 cap hit is now essentially $8 million less, giving Detroit some flexibility in next year’s free agency. Now, let’s say you didn’t want to extend Gibbs. You wanted him to play off that fifth-year option, and then franchise tag him in 2028. Three more years of Gibbs, then say goodbye. It’s hard to predict what his 2028 franchise tag would be, but OverTheCap projects the tag to be $15.065 million in 2027. Chances are it will be at least as expensive as Gibbs’ current 2028 cap hit of $15.5 million. So over the next three years—well within the Lions’ Super Bowl window—Gibbs would have actually cost at least $5 million more to the team’s salary cap than if they didn’t extend him. Incentives Interestingly, the Lions are offering incentives to Gibbs tied around receiving yards , suggesting they are very interested in increasing that part of his game. Here are the details of those: $562,500 for each season (2026-28) in which he earns at least 800 receiving yards [paid in 2029] $562,500 for each season (2026-28) in which he earns at least 800 receiving yards AND the team gets to the divisional round of the playoffs [paid in 2029] $421,875 for each season (2026-29)in which he earns at least 800 receiving yards [paid in 2030] $421,875 for each season (2026-29) in which he earns at least 800 receiving yards AND the team gets to the divisional round of the playoffs [paid in 2030] These incentives, if earned, will impact the salary cap when they are paid out.

title: Discussion: Who will be the next Detroit Lions inducted into the Hall of Fame?
summary: On Saturday, five people were officially inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame: Drew Brees, Roger Craig, Luke Kuechly, Larry Fitzgerald, and Adam Vinatieri. All of those players are more than deserving of the honors. It’s been a little bit since we’ve seen a Detroit Lion on stage accepting their induction. If we’re talking […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2018; Canton, OH, USA; Busts of enshrinees on display at the Pro Football of Hall of Fame. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports On Saturday, five people were officially inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame: Drew Brees, Roger Craig, Luke Kuechly, Larry Fitzgerald, and Adam Vinatieri. All of those players are more than deserving of the honors. It’s been a little bit since we’ve seen a Detroit Lion on stage accepting their induction. If we’re talking about players who are Lions more than any other NFL franchise, Calvin Johnson was the last to be inducted back in 2021. Technically , Dwight Freeney was the last one in 2024. Let’s use this space to talk about the Lions’ future in the Hall of Fame. Today’s Question of the Day is: Who will be the next Lions player inducted into the Hall of Fame? My answer: For simplicity’s sake, let’s just talk about players who spent a large portion of their career with the Lions. So not players like Anquan Boldin. The Lions have been trying to make a push for Lomas Brown , and he finally broke through to become a semifinalist for the 2026 class. It’s hard to imagine him getting further in the voting process after the 2026 push, but it’s quite possible he makes it in as a senior candidate after his last year of modern-era eligibility (2027). Beyond that, we should probably have the Matthew Stafford conversation. While Stafford did not have Hall of Fame credentials when he left Detroit in 2021, he is certainly a viable candidate now with a Super Bowl under his belt and an MVP award from last year. You can certainly squabble whether he should be considered a Ram or Lion upon induction, but it’s looking more and more like he’s headed for Canton—especially if this year’s Rams team meets expectations. If we want to limit the conversation to current Lions players, Penei Sewell feels like the safest candidate. He’s already a three-time First Team All-Pro player, and he’s just 25 years old. Amon-Ra St. Brown has a pretty good case, as well, with four Pro Bowls and two First Team All Pros at just 26 years old. Jared Goff deserves to at least be in the conversation, but I don’t think he has the resume yet to get in. If he, like Stafford, can add at least a Super Bowl ring and an MVP to his candidacy in the next few years, he’ll deserve to be considered. But he’s just not there yet. So, if we count Stafford, I think he’s next. If not, I’m guessing Sewell. Who do you think will be the next Lions player inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame? Which players do you think will eventually head there? Share your answers in the comment section.

title: Packers claim former HS All-American receiver Chris Hilton
summary: The Green Bay Packers worked out multiple receivers today and re-signed receiver Kisean Johnson after a tryout, following short-term injuries to receivers Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed. When the Packers announced their transactions after practice Sunday, which Johnson participated in, it was news that Green Bay waived two players, not one, while adding Johnson, giving […]
full_text: OXFORD, MS - SEPTEMBER 27: Chris Hilton Jr. #3 of the LSU Tigers in action against the Ole Miss Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on September 27, 2025 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) The Green Bay Packers worked out multiple receivers today and re-signed receiver Kisean Johnson after a tryout , following short-term injuries to receivers Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed . When the Packers announced their transactions after practice Sunday, which Johnson participated in, it was news that Green Bay waived two players, not one, while adding Johnson, giving the team an open roster spot on the 91-man roster. The players waived were cornerback Marlon Jones and safety Johnathan Baldwin , who both were given injury designations. They will revert to the Packers’ injured reserve if they pass through waivers unclaimed. From there, Green Bay can decide whether to end their seasons by keeping them on the injured reserve or pay them out an injury settlement, which would make them free agents while they are rehabbing their injuries. As I mentioned in The Feed when the news dropped that the Packers had an extra roster spot to fill , this seemed like a move that a team would make before they claimed someone on waivers themselves. It turns out that I was on the right path, as Green Bay was awarded another receiver, Chris Hilton Jr., off waivers today. He should make his Packers debut in Monday’s practice, which is open to the public. Hilton played five years at LSU before going undrafted in the 2026 class, despite participating in four different all-star games (Hula Bowl, American Bowl, East-West Shrine Bowl and Senior Bowl) and receiving a combine invite. At the combine this year, he measured in at 6’0”-flat and 188 pounds and recorded a 4.41-second 40-yard dash. The former high school All-American had 41 receptions for 780 yards and six touchdowns in his SEC career, but only registered 10 receptions for 122 yards as a redshirt senior, as the Tigers struggled in the passing game after quarterback Garrett Nussmeier injured his abs, which severely limited his play. Nussmeier, who had some first-round hype coming into the 2025 season, wound up getting drafted in the seventh round by the Kansas City Chiefs this spring. Chris Hilton has okay size for a WR and good speed. Explsoveness is neither a strength nor a weakness, but at his size those poor agility drills are likely to show up when facing NFL cornerbacks. Some things to work with, but some concerns. pic.twitter.com/GZ69HsueAG — RAS.football (@MathBomb) May 3, 2026 Hilton began his NFL career with the Washington Commanders, but he was let go yesterday, a day after the team signed receiver Stefon Diggs to a one-year, $12 million contract. When Hilton signed with Washington, he received $15,000 in guarantees, which was equal to or more than 6 of the Packers’ 11 initial UDFA signings this year: QB Kyron Drones RB Jaden Nixon TE RJ Maryland (waived with an injury designation) OL Dylan Barrett CB Marlon Jones (waived with an injury designation) S Murvin Kenion II Commanders signed Chris Hilton Jr from LSU. I coached him in the Hula Bowl. Kid can play! Nice pickup — Jay Gruden (@Coach_JayGruden) April 28, 2026 Hilton was The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s 50th-ranked receiver in the 2026 draft class and received a free agent grade from the draft analyst. Here’s his blurb on Hilton: Christopher “Chris” Hilton Jr. grew up north of Baton Rouge, La., with his parents (Chris Sr. and Cindy), who were both track athletes at Southern University. Hilton was a standout football and track star at Zachary High, where he won several state titles in sprints and jumps (personal best of 10.85 seconds in the 100-meter dash). A four-star recruit, he was the top-ranked receiver in LSU’s 2021 class (ahead of Malik Nabers and Brian Thomas Jr.). Multiple injuries sidetracked his early career, however, as he struggled to find a consistent role beyond being a deep threat. Hilton looks like a sprinter with his slender, lean-muscled frame and uses his speed to stretch the field. A limited snap count hindered his ability to develop as a route runner, and he was also up and down with his hands — his success rate nosedived when defenders crowded his air space. He has limited return experience but played more on special teams in 2025. For what it’s worth, the injuries he suffered in his career were: 2021 (redshirt season after playing four games): torn meniscus 2022: missed 10 games with shoulder surgery and a torn meniscus in his other knee 2023: healthy 2024: missed 7 games with a hairline fracture 2025: healthy In total, he started seven games for the Tigers over five years. His only return experience was as a kick returner during his true freshman and redshirt freshman seasons, when he returned two attempts for a total of 26 yards. The Packers also reported worked out Devin Voisin , a UDFA who was second-team All-Sun Belt with South Alabama last year, so it’s clear that the team was trying to add bodies to the receiver position this week. Voisin has yet to sign with an NFL team, despite being on the Senior Bowl roster this offseason. He was invited to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ rookie minicamp and has also worked out with the Tennessee Titans and Denver Broncos in the last two weeks.

full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Chris Brooks #30 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had a closed practice to the public, but open to the media, on Sunday, following the team’s Family Night practice at Lambeau Field on Friday. This practice was held in the Packers’ indoor facility, while Monday and Tuesday’s practices are scheduled to be open to the public at Ray Nitschke Field before the team has a travel day on Wednesday. Green Bay will open up its preseason slate in Pittsburgh on Thursday. Here’s everything you need to know about Sunday’s practice. Injuries Running back Chris Brooks (NFI, hamstring) and defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (PUP, knee) were both activated today and returned to practice for the first time in training camp. This leaves just tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), edge defender Micah Parsons (ACL), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) on the Packers’ physically unable to perform list. Parsons and Riley are expected to remain on the PUP list to start the regular season (which will mean they won’t count against the 53-man roster but will also mean that they won’t play at least the first four weeks of the season), while Orzech’s injury was called a short-term issue. Musgrave’s neck injury seems to be of the “tricky” variety, as the staff has been vague about his timeline to return to the field. Before practice, head coach Matt LaFleur said that there were no long-term injuries suffered on Family Night, even though four players were added to the non-participants list today: receivers Matthew Golden (toe), receiver Jayden Reed (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (neck) and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (foot). Linebacker Zaire Franklin was also a non-participant today, but that was due to Franklin traveling to Canton to watch his former teammate Adam Vinatieri be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame this weekend. Franklin’s absence was excused by the team. Golden, Reed, Whyle and Cooper joined running back Josh Jacobs (groin), cornerback Domani Jackson (undisclosed) and safety Johnathan Baldwin (knee) as active players who were held out of practice entirely on Sunday. Tight end Tucker Kraft, left guard Aaron Banks, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt and cornerback Kamal Hadden all returned to practice today after being held out of Family Night on Friday, as the team was conservative on that front. Because of the two new injuries at the receiver position, the Packers re-signed receiver Kisean Johnson , who originally joined Green Bay’s practice squad late in the 2025 season. To make room for Johnson, the team waived cornerback Marlon Jones with an injury designation. Offense Starters (lots of intrigue!!!) Love Lloyd and Moore in the backfield Dabney Melton – Watson Morgan – Burton – Ryan – Monk – ZBB!! LVN – Wyatt – Brooks – Sorrell Hopper – McDuffie Nixon – Bullard – Cisse Williams – X — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 9, 2026 Because Kraft isn’t in team drills and both Musgrave and Whyle are injured, Drake Dabney was the “starting” tight end today. The other healthy tight ends on the roster are Messiah Swinson, McCallan Castles (recently signed), Drew Biber (recently signed) and Thomas Yassmin, an international exemption player whose first practice with the Packers was on Family Night due to visa issues. Banks remains sidelined for team drills, but Bako-Bewele was involved in the team period for the first time in training camp today. The first look starting offensive line was Jordan Morgan, Jager Burton, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Bako-Bewele (left to right). Darian Kinnard, who has exclusively played tackle up to this point in camp, finally repped at guard on Sunday, a role he played with both Kansas City and Philadelphia before he joined the Packers last season. John Williams, who is playing all five positions in camp, is still getting in the lineup at tackle ahead of Travis Glover, who the team was high on before his season-ending shoulder injury in 2025. It was interesting that Bo Melton was the next man up at receiver with both Golden and Reed out, and that Skyy Moore got a snap in the backfield to open practice. Moore has mostly been playing the slot for the Packers, so there’s probably a package where Reed is in the backfield. 60 yard bomb from McCord to Savion Williams, who came free off the snap and gained a few steps on Kristian Welch in recovery mode for the defense — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 9, 2026 Savion with a 5th catch in team, as Love hits him on an in-breaker. Just missed a one-handed grab earlier too. — Mike Spofford (@mikespofford) August 9, 2026 While Melton got the nod over Savion Williams, that doesn’t mean that Williams didn’t show out on Sunday. LaFleur has said in the past that it’s difficult to rep four quarterbacks in practice (McCord and Drones split third-team reps on Family Night, for perspective), so if McCord is pulling away, maybe the team can move off Drones the next time they need to add a healthy body to the 91-man roster. Defense With both starting linebackers out of practice, the replacement starters today were Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper, which shouldn’t have been too surprising. title: Green Bay Packers re-sign WR Kisean Johnson
summary: Due to short-term injuries to receivers Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed, the Green Bay Packers looked to add a receiver on Sunday, as they reported worked out Kisean Johnson, Kobe Hudson and Cornell Powell between their Family Night practice on Friday and their media-open practice on Sunday. Apparently, Johnson was the receiver who impressed the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 08: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Kisean Johnson (83) during a NFL preseason football game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers on August 8, 2025, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Due to short-term injuries to receivers Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed , the Green Bay Packers looked to add a receiver on Sunday, as they reported worked out Kisean Johnson, Kobe Hudson and Cornell Powell between their Family Night practice on Friday and their media-open practice on Sunday. Apparently, Johnson was the receiver who impressed the most in the workout, as the Packers added him to the team’s 91-man roster. In a corresponding roster move to make space for the addition of Johnson, Green Bay let go of cornerback Marlon Jones, who was waived with an injured designation today. Jones was a rookie UDFA who signed with the Packers in mid-May . This is actually Johnson’s second stint with Green Bay, after he signed with the Packers’ practice squad on January 6th, leading up to the team’s postseason loss to the Chicago Bears. If you lost Johnson in the nearly 30-player shuffle in the final two weeks of Green Bay’s season, no one is going to blame you. Unlike most of the Packers’ practice squad, Johnson was not signed to a reserve/futures deal after the season, making him a free agent. At Alabama State, Kisean Johnson was an FCS All-American before transferring to Western Kentucky, where he had 75 receptions for 925 yards and seven touchdowns in his lone year at the FBS level. In 2025, he was originally signed as a UDFA with the Cleveland Browns before his stint with Green Bay. In the 2025 class, Johnson was The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s 124th-ranked receiver . He was given a true free agent grade after measuring in at about 6’0.5” and 216 pounds at WKU’s pro day. He ran a 4.63-second 40-yard dash and posted a 33” vertical jump during the pre-draft process.

title: Jonathan Gannon shows new defensive looks in Packers’ Family Night
summary: When Jonathan Gannon was hired to be the Green Bay Packers’ defensive coordinator, there was an assumption that the Packers’ defense would primarily be a 3-4 front in base defense and the squad would call quarters coverage significantly more than a typical NFL team, since his defenses have called Cover 4 more than any individual […]
full_text: Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon talks with head coach Matt LaFleur during practice on Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026, at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co When Jonathan Gannon was hired to be the Green Bay Packers’ defensive coordinator, there was an assumption that the Packers’ defense would primarily be a 3-4 front in base defense and the squad would call quarters coverage significantly more than a typical NFL team, since his defenses have called Cover 4 more than any individual NFL team since 2021 . The big question was how many exotic personnel packages Gannon would bring from Arizona, which he leaned on due to their lack of talent throughout his tenure, since the personnel in Green Bay is different. On Family Night, we got our first bird’s-eye view of the Packers’ defense, which helped us answer that question (at least partially). Generally, Jeff Hafley, Green Bay’s previous defensive coordinator, almost exclusively played his base 4-3 defense and a Nickel package. Beyond Gannon’s expected 3-4 base defense and Nickel package, the Packers showed three other looks on Family Night. Three-Safety Penny Three safety penny (McKinney so deep in the middle he's not on the screen) with Edgerrin Cooper playing on the edge (LVN out) pic.twitter.com/I1w8rLMs8D — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 8, 2026 Alright, this is the Packers’ often talked about three-safety defense. Yes, there are three safeties on the field when Green Bay plays their Nickel sets, since Javon Bullard plays in the slot, but this is a true three-safety look. Evan Williams and Javon Bullard are 10 yards off the ball here, and Xavier McKinney is so deep in the middle of the field that he doesn’t even appear on the screen. On this play, the Packers are playing a “Penny” front, which is essentially the same as a 3-4 defense on the line of scrimmage, with three interior defensive linemen jamming up the front. Penny is used to stop opposing offenses’ run games while allowing for five defensive backs to be on the field, like in a Nickel package. The trade-off here is that most teams usually put an off-ball linebacker on the bench to get a slot defender (compared to a 3-4 defense), but the Packers actually lost a “true” edge defender to bring on an extra safety when they played Penny on Family Night. Instead of Edgerrin Cooper going to the bench, which is what most teams would have done with their Will linebacker in Penny looks, they played Cooper on the edge (at the top of the screen) and swapped out an edge rusher for Javon Bullard. Same 3 penny look but the the slot is split from the formation. Cooper detaches from the edge. Very college football pic.twitter.com/UjYsLJplUL — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 8, 2026 Why are the Packers playing Cooper on the edge in these packages? Well, one way to hurt Penny defenses is by spreading them out. Either the defense has to declare that they’ll be rushing five by keeping the line of scrimmage together (teams usually throw quick game passes against this) or they have to detach an edge rusher into the slot (an obvious matchup that offenses want to take advantage of) if they’re showing a four-man rush. So instead of an edge rusher breaking out into the slot, it was Cooper who was separated from the offensive formation when the defense got that spread look on Family Night. Cooper is probably a better matchup in the slot than Preston Smith, the player that offenses picked on the last time Green Bay leaned heavily into the Penny formation under Joe Barry. You’re probably wondering: “Wait, we’re giving up the edge on this play?” The answer is yes, and it’s very common in college football right now (especially among programs that major in quarters systems). College coaches have learned a technique that they generally call Jimmy/Pony that allows linemen to slow-play the run game and allow for the ball to bounce outside slowly in a way that gets defenders who line up at depth to make plays in the alley. The video above is a clinic that former Alabama coach Karl Scott did, where he explains this technique. Scott is now the defensive backs coach/passing game coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks, who just won a Super Bowl with a quarters-based defense. My question moving forward for this package is whether or not the Packers’ pass-rush of three interior linemen and one true edge rusher is good enough to get home in this package when they’re spread out and rushing four, especially if that lone edge rusher isn’t Micah Parsons, but we probably won’t get an answer there until the regular season. Worth noting: Green Bay called this package on mixed downs, as both of the screenshots above came from second-and-medium looks. Here’s an overhead look of a Penny front, which Cooper would be playing the “W” for in this set: Basically a 5-1 alignment. It’s an Odd front with a Nickel. pic.twitter.com/pEj3bohNGR — Honest NFL (@TheHonestNFL) October 4, 2023 Cheetah Package Pressure nickel with LVN at DT. Sorrel to bench and Collin Oliver/Brenton Cox Jr. come off the bench pic.twitter.com/7PgOaWt0vo — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 8, 2026 This is your typical Nickel look, with the Packers playing a four-man front on the line of scrimmage and having a slot defender (Bullard) on the field. The one curveball here is that on obvious passing downs, Green Bay also plays an extra edge defender on the interior — in this case Lukas Van Ness on the side of the center — in place of a 300-plus-pounder. Jeff Hafley had this package too, which is how you got Micah Parsons standing up and roaming near the ball pre-snap on third downs. They called this the “Cheetah” package under Hafley. So far, edge defenders kicking into the interior have come out of three-point stances for Gannon, so maybe that’ll be a difference in 2026. For what it’s worth, it seems like the Packers prefer to use interior defensive linemen Karl Brooks and Warren Brinson on passing downs (remember that Devonte Wyatt and Javon Hargrave were both non-participants on Family Night) and edge rushers Brenton Cox Jr. and Collin Oliver on the outside in these situations. Barryn Sorrell was mostly a run-down edge defender (and did well on Family Night in that role), with Van Ness and Dani Dennis-Sutton being the top “kick inside” candidates on third downs. Mug Front Mug front pic.twitter.com/rswuYCPlnO — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 8, 2026 The final “exotic” front the Packers showed was a Mug front, another tool that Hafley also used in the past. This is another Nickel personnel formation, with the difference from true Nickel being that the typical off-ball linebackers are walked up to the line of scrimmage, forcing opposing offenses to allocate at least one non-offensive lineman to help chip the front; otherwise, an all-out blitz (of six line of scrimmage defenders) would leave a free man screaming to the quarterback. — At minimum, Green Bay has five defensive looks installed: Base 3-4 Nickel Normal Nickel Cheetah Package Mug Nickel 3-Safety Penny While the Nickel formations are similar to what Hafley did with the Packers, expect a lot more “Odd” fronts (3-4 base, 3-Safety Penny) in Green Bay under Gannon this year, as Hafley generally only played an Odd-numbered front on the line of scrimmage when the team played its 4-3 Under. In 4-3 Under looks, Hafley’s defense would walk down Sam linebacker Isaiah McDuffie to the line of scrimmage. So far, we’ve seen no three-linebacker (not outside linebackers, who are edge rushers) looks under Gannon, as the Packers appear to be majoring in two-linebacker sets in 2026. We also didn’t get any Dime (double slot, one linebacker) looks on Family Night, which was a staple for Gannon in Arizona. For perspective, the Cardinals ran 176 snaps of Dime last year (5th most in the NFL), while Green Bay ran just 2 (29th in the NFL). Both of those snaps came in end-of-half situations for the 2025…

title: Super Bowl Pressure Index: Where do the Houston Texans rank on this list
summary: There is always pressure to win in the NFL. This is not a revolutionary concept. Yet, some teams go into the upcoming season under more pressure than others to be the ones left standing after the Super Bowl. With that, here is a ranking of which teams are under the most pressure to win it […]
full_text: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 16: A view of the Vince Lombardi trophy at Fanatics Fest NYC 2026 at Jacob Javits Center on July 16, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Fanatics) | Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Fan There is always pressure to win in the NFL. This is not a revolutionary concept. Yet, some teams go into the upcoming season under more pressure than others to be the ones left standing after the Super Bowl. With that, here is a ranking of which teams are under the most pressure to win it all. These rankings are primarily subjective in nature and will be binned in sub-categories. While there will be likely correlation between pressure and projection to win, there are going to be some teams that will have a higher pressure ranking vs. preseason win projections. With that, on to the rankings: Pressure to not finish 0-17 (No particular order): Miami Dolphins New York Jets of New Jersey Arizona Cardinals Remember 2019 when the Texans gave Miami all of that draft capital for Laremy Tunsil? The final yield: 0-2 in the playoffs. There was a massive hurricane fire sale in Miami this offseason. They finished 1-15 in 2007. They might match that win total this year. The Jets likely will get at least one INT this season on defense…maybe. However, wins might be hard to come by, again. The Cardinals have to hope that Carson Beck’s performance in the Hall of Fame game does not constitute the highlight of the season. The Cleveland Browns: Cleveland Browns They have arguably too much talent to worry about 0-17. However, they are stuck in a tough division, have no surety about their QB situation and traded their best player to the Rams in the offseason. The Browns will likely suck again this year, but Watson’s contract comes off the books and they should have a chance for a good QB prospect in the 2027 Draft. Pressure to not totally suck (No particular order): Tennessee Titans Las Vegas Raiders New York Giants of New Jersey Cam Ward showed the Titans that perhaps there is something there. With a new coaching staff, the Titans will look to rise above the horridness of the last couple of seasons. With a few breaks, the Titans could possibly up the win totals. Mendoza hasn’t lost a game since 2024. That streak will end this season. While he is the main focus, the Raiders did significantly upgrade their talent, especially along the lines. Maybe not a playoff team, but likely won’t be in competition for the #1 overall pick either. The Giants have a new coach and provided their young stars can avoid needless injuries/stupid actions, should also not be front runners for the #1 overall pick again. NFC South (No particular order): Carolina Panthers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Atlanta Falcons New Orleans Saints Arguably the weakest division in the NFL, this division has four teams that can all be in the hunt for the division crown and a home playoff game and also be in the hunt for a top 10 draft pick. Carolina “won” the division with a losing record last year but also took the Rams down to the wire in their playoff matchup. Tampa Bay had been the reigning champion, but injury and questions about their QB which started in last season’s collapse are making things even more uncomfortable for Todd Bowles. Atlanta has been one of the biggest teases in the league in recent seasons, filled with talent, but somehow managing to be less than the sum of their parts. New Orleans seemed to finally embrace the long-delayed rebuild, but then Shough shows up to jolt the Big Easy fanbase. Likely the 4 seed in the NFC is going to the winner of this division, with a chance it is to at team with a winning record. Not championship pressure, but playoff pressure (No particular order): Indianapolis Colts Minnesota Vikings Washington Commanders Cincinnati Bengals Los Angeles Chargers The Colts watched all other AFC South teams win multiple division crowns since their last one in 2014. Much rides on the health of Daniel Jones. If he can return and play close to the form he showcased in last season’s 7-1 start, the Colts may have something to say about playoff seeding. Same with the Commanders, who hope the Jayden Daniels of 2024 is the one that shows up this season. The Vikings hope that either Murray or McCarthy can lead them back to the postseason. The Bengals need a) Joe Burrow to stay healthy and 2) Dexter Lawrence to lift the defense to average. If both happen, the Bengals are legit contenders. The Chargers think they are contenders, but they need to do something they haven’t done since they played in San Diego: Win a playoff game. Teams under pressure to win it all (in ascending order) 16) Jacksonville Jaguars Under Coen, the Jags won their first AFC South title since 2017. They had a sour coda with their loss to the Bills, but they set a foundation of success. Yet, the Glitter Kitties had a curiously quiet offseason. The pieces are there for them to make another run at their first Super Bowl, but they might also have to claw just to get back to the postseason. 15) Chicago Bears Ben Johnson was the hot shot/can’t miss hire last offseason. The Bears responded with a division crown and an overtime loss short of the conference championship game. Yet, there is pressure to hold off regression, as they relied on defensive turnovers and a myriad of 4th quarter comebacks to get to where they got as far as wins. Will their offseason moves be enough to mitigate those fears? 14) Kansas City Chiefs Quite the dynastic hangover season for the Chiefs. They finished 6-11 and Mahomes tore his ACL. Yet, the Chiefs expect to have Mahomes back under center to start the season and they retooled gaps in their running game and secondary. Eric Bienemy is back to guide an offense that has regressed since his previous tenure. That they’ve won three Super Bowls in the last six years lessens some of the pressure to win it this year. However, they want to show that last season was a painful footnote and not a trend. 13) New England Patriots QB Drake May, HC Mike Vrabel and DC Zak Kuhr leveraged the weakest schedule in decades and a hot defense to claim their 10th Super Bowl bid this century. Yes, the Seahawks blasted them in the Super Bowl, but the Pats can say they are back. The schedule is going to be more difficult, and New England won’t sneak up on anyone this year. Oh, and I don’t know if you heard, but Vrabel had a bit of a difficult offseason. As if the defending AFC Champion needed more challenges. 12) Seattle Seahawks The defending Super Bowl champions rode Sam Darnold of all QBs, along with the “Dark Side” defense to their 2nd Lombardi Trophy. They lost Kenneth Walker, but with most of their key stars returning, they figure to have a good chance to repeat. They won in the 49ers’ house last season. Seattle would surely relish the chance to win it in the Rams’ home this round. Of course, they have to weather being the defending champ and playing in the super brutal NFC West. 11) Denver Broncos If Bo Nix hadn’t broken his ankle in the AFC Divisional round? Denver had an awful lot go right for them last season as they ended up with the #1 seed in the AFC. They return a formidable defense and Nix is expected back to start the season. Yet, they must navigate a more dangerous AFC West and they can’t expect to rely on continued 4th quarter magic to bail them out again. 10) Philadelphia Eagles The 2025-26 started with their best defensive player getting ejected from a game before the first official snap. The season never really got much better. The Eagles became the first team in over 20 years to repeat as NFC East Champions. The reward: a humiliating loss to the 49ers at home. In theory, if the defense can continue its high standard of play, the offense only needs to be competent, something it definitely wasn’t last year. Philly fans aren’t noted for patience, so it is on HC Sirianni and new OC Sean Mannion to get the Eagles back in the Super Bowl mix. 9) Detroit Lions They finished last in the…

title: Colts’ Shane Steichen reveals preseason opener plan at QB
summary: According to head coach Shane Steichen, the Indianapolis Colts will rotate their two primary backup quarterbacks, Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard, during the team’s upcoming Thursday night preseason opener on the road against the New England Patriots (via The Athletic’s James Boyd): Rather unsurprisingly, Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones, who’s seemingly shown no signs of […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - JULY 29: Anthony Richardson #5 of the Indianapolis Colts fixes the shoulder pad of Riley Leonard #15 during the Indianapolis Colts Training Camp at Grand Park on July 29, 2025 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to head coach Shane Steichen, the Indianapolis Colts will rotate their two primary backup quarterbacks, Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard, during the team’s upcoming Thursday night preseason opener on the road against the New England Patriots (via The Athletic’s James Boyd): #Colts HC Shane Steichen said the plan is for QBs Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson Sr. to play in Thursday’s preseason opener against the #Patriots . Daniel Jones will only participate in Tuesday’s joint practice. (I’d be shocked if DJ plays in the preseason.) — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) August 9, 2026 Rather unsurprisingly, Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones, who’s seemingly shown no signs of his torn Achilles suffered last year so far during team training camp, will not play in the team’s Preseason Week 1 game— especially on newly installed turf that the Patriots field crew is rushing to get down in Gillette Stadium by Thursday night. Both Richardson and Leonard have shown inconsistency so far throughout training camp, with neither quarterback arguably clearly separating from the other competitor for the Colts’ QB2 job behind Jones. That means it could come down to their respective preseason performances, as well as their work behind-the-scenes, which is the key reason why Jones bested out Richardson for the Colts’ QB1 job last year after rather even on-the-field performances throughout last year’s training camp and preseason games. If Richardson doesn’t clearly separate himself through all three facets: training camp, preseason, and off-the-field work, then the default to me, would be Leonard ultimately winning the QB2 job for the Colts going forward. Richardson is a free agent at year-end, and clearly has no intentions of re-signing—having already requested a trade from Indianapolis by his representation earlier this offseason. Meanwhile, Leonard is under team control by the Colts on his rookie contract through the 2028 season. It’s nothing personal from that standpoint, it’s just good business that whatever practice reps are left over from Jones should go to Leonard throughout the season. The backup quarterback that will actually remain in Indianapolis beyond the 2026 campaign—if it’s even that long for Richardson.

title: Could Patriots ‘new’ turf pose preseason problem for Colts?
summary: According to ESPN NFL reporter Mike Reiss, the New England Patriots are ‘all hands on deck’ this week to replace the freshly installed World Cup turf at Gillette Stadium ahead of their Thursday night preseason opening game against the Indianapolis Colts: The post-World Cup field turf passed general tests, but failed separate laboratory testing protocols […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: A detail view of the New England Patriots logo painted on the field in Gillette Stadium prior to an NFL wild card playoff football game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN NFL reporter Mike Reiss, the New England Patriots are ‘all hands on deck’ this week to replace the freshly installed World Cup turf at Gillette Stadium ahead of their Thursday night preseason opening game against the Indianapolis Colts: Gillette Stadium is installing new artificial turf this week after the surface installed following the World Cup was deemed noncompliant by the NFL, per @MikeReiss . #Patriots COO Jim Nolan says the replacement will be the latest version of the turf used last season and should… pic.twitter.com/SMe1xk5Zsf — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) August 9, 2026 The post-World Cup field turf passed general tests, but failed separate laboratory testing protocols because it lacked a rubber shock pad (E-layer) that is apparently required under lab specifications for concrete bases—and apparently Gillette Stadium uses a stone-dust base. Reportedly, the replacement turf will be one that the Patriots used last for their Divisional Round win against the Colts’ AFC South rival Houston Texans on January 18th, 2026. At any rate, the Colts are no strangers to preseason turf issues, as the 2016 Hall of Fame game between the Colts and Green Bay Packers was infamously called off hours before the ‘kickoff to preseason’ game because the stadium crew accidentally applied the wrong type of paint during touchups, causing it to fail to dry properly. Specifically, the paint used on the midfield logo and end zones congealed and turned rubbery, creating slippery footing and unsafe conditions for potential participating players. The Colts have already had a number of hamstring injuries during this year’s training camp, and while it would be surprising if any of those players nursing such lingering injuries would play in Preseason Week 1, you also don’t want to see any new names join the injury practice report because of suspect turf conditions. Not saying that will be the case in New England by any means, but stranger things have happened.

title: NFL Insider wouldn’t be surprised if Colts QB Anthony Richardson has played last down in Indy
summary: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, he wouldn’t be surprised if Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson, who’s competing for the QB2 job behind starter Daniel Jones, has played his last down in Indy: It’s been a roller coaster ride for the 2023 4th overall pick of the Colts, who had a promising start to his […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - JULY 29: Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 of the Indianapolis Colts participates in training camp at Grand Park Sports Campus on July 29, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, he wouldn’t be surprised if Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson, who’s competing for the QB2 job behind starter Daniel Jones, has played his last down in Indy: From Inside Training Camp Live: Attempting to make sense of the future of #Colts QB Anthony Richardson… pic.twitter.com/kBMpF5fkji — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 9, 2026 It’s been a roller coaster ride for the 2023 4th overall pick of the Colts, who had a promising start to his pro career as a rookie in a limited 4 starts that same season, before being lost to a season-ending shoulder injury. Richardson endured a ‘sophomore slump’ a year later, where his maturity was questioned following his infamous in-game tap-out incident, and it’s been a myriad of injuries that have kept him off the field ever since—including a freak accident in Week 6 last season when a medical band snapped during pre-game work, which would cause him to miss the remaining 2025 season. The Colts could’ve certainly used Richardson after Jones went down with an Achilles tear during Week 14 of last year, but as mentioned, he wasn’t available himself as a backup. There’s been plenty of blame to go around for both sides. The Colts initially said he needed snaps and game day reps after drafting him, only to reverse course, and say he wasn’t ready—and should’ve sat to begin his pro career in retrospect. Indianapolis never surrounded him with a willing veteran mentor at quarterback either. Even overlooking the injuries, Richardson’s passing accuracy remains a critical deficiency for him to take the next step, and it’s a fair question of whether he was doing everything on and off the field to lead the team as their new QB1—and the fresh CEO of W. 56th Street team headquarters. At any rate, having already had trouble handling some snaps in training camp, it appears as though Richardson’s vision may not have fully recovered yet from the medical band incident. With his trade value already seemingly low, because let’s face it, if the Colts had gotten something meaningful in a trade offer in return, they probably already would’ve moved him, one has to wonder if the latest vision concerns only torpedos it downward further. For what it’s worth, there has been no status update per Richardson, on his earlier offseason trade request from both him and his representation, which still remains active—as he’s just looking to help a team, whether it’s the Colts or another NFL squad right now: Anthony Richardson addressed his trade request today in the midst battling for the backup QB role. "I haven't really talked to my agent about that recently. I haven't talked to (Chris) Ballard or anybody about that recently, so I'm not necessarily sure what's going on with… pic.twitter.com/wHM629FhuL — Angela Moryan (@AngelaMoryanTV) August 9, 2026 With Richardson, at best, having failed to separate himself so far from 2nd-year quarterback Riley Leonard in training camp, it makes the most sense for Indianapolis both now and going forward to have the latter as the QB2 behind Jones because Leonard is under contract through the 2028 season, whereas Richardson is a free agent at year-end—and it’s a foregone conclusion that he will not re-sign with the Colts. It would be one thing if Richardson was head-and-shoulders the better backup QB option over Leonard, who just has one career start under his belt, but that hasn’t been the case yet. Richardson definitely needs to pick it up.

title: Chiefs News: It’s time to key in on position battles for the preseason
summary: The latest The Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for a game this week, an exhibition against the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium; kickoff is scheduled for 3:00 p.m. Head coach Andy Reid seems to be strongly “leaning” toward Patrick Mahomes not playing, but there are plenty of other players he will be […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Emmett Johnson #10 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The latest The Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for a game this week, an exhibition against the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium; kickoff is scheduled for 3:00 p.m. Head coach Andy Reid seems to be strongly “leaning” toward Patrick Mahomes not playing, but there are plenty of other players he will be looking to see in live action. The lineups we’ve seen so far in training camp could change by the time Week 1 gets here, including the rotation in the backfield behind starting running back Kenneth Walker. The 4 Chiefs position battles we’re watching as the preseason opener approaches | The Kansas City Star Second running back: Emari Demercado, Brashard Smith, Emmett Johnson Other running backs also have looked strong, with Demercado and Smith getting most of the second-team reps in recent practices. Smith, the only Chiefs player in the group returning from last season, is the most versatile. “We’re moving him all over the place,” said Andy Reid, who also singled out Smith’s improved pass-blocking ability. Johnson, the fifth-round draft pick from Nebraska, also has been getting reps with the second team. The Chiefs should improve the number of explosive runs with this group and look to identify their top a short-yardage back. 2026 NFL Training Camp: Early Takeaways for all 32 teams | NFL.com I think it’s safe to declare Patrick Mahomes completely fine. Every report out of camp reads like he isn’t coming off a nasty knee injury, so why should we fret? Peter Woods looked the part when the pads came on. The first-round DT could be massive for K.C.’s defense. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson seems poised to swipe the starting right tackle job. This feels like it warrants more attention. Five Observations from Saturday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/8 | The Mothership 3. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes made a handful of classic throws. Mahomes showed off a handful of the off-balance throws for which he’s synonymous on Saturday, firing a pair of near identical passes across his body while on the run to a receiver in the middle of the field. Mahomes found Andrew Armstrong on the first instance, followed by a throw to Nikko Remigio a little bit later. The three-time Super Bowl MVP, who has participated in every 11-on-11 segment of training camp so far, spoke following practice about his progress as he continues to work his way back from last season’s knee injury. Three Chiefs Players With the Most to Lose in Preseason Opener vs Rams | Sports Illustrated 3. Garrett Nussmeier Now that he has an extended opportunity, Nussmeier’s performance could have massive implications for his chances of securing the QB3 job. It will be his first real opportunity to play with the rest of the squad, and it’s possible that he receives snaps with some of the first-team starters as well. While it’s highly unlikely that Chris Oladokun jumps him up the depth chart, K.C. is in a tricky situation with Nussmeier. If he plays poorly in the preseason, the Chiefs could decide to run with two quarterbacks on the active 53-man roster to open the campaign and leave Oladokun on the practice squad. Nussmeier cannot simply be placed on the practice squad like Oladokun as a drafted rookie, as he would first have to clear the NFL waiver wire. Patrick Mahomes supports hometown schools with T-Mobile | Chiefs Wire Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes returns for his second season alongside Rob Gronkowski to inspire fans and rally communities throughout T-Mobile’s Friday Night 5G Lights competition. Mahomes and Gronkowski are joined by standout college athletes Dante Moore, Ashlea Klam, CJ Carr, Rocco Becht and Kewan Lacy, representing divisions across the country and encouraging fans to support their hometown schools in the race for game-changing prizes. Chiefs Predicted to Part Ways With Fan-Favorite WR After Offseason Return | Heavy Sports “With the uncertainty at the top of the depth chart, it seems like the team needs to keep more than five receivers. There’s more to find out about Royals and Armstrong, but that’s more than can be said about Remigio. He has maximized his role in Kansas City, and the return job should be handed off to Brashard Smith. Allen has lined up and caught punts and kicks as well.” Remigio was an exclusive-rights free agent this winter, returning to the team with a new contract extension on the day the free agent market officially opened in March. Remigio made a strong impression in training camp in 2024, averaging 33.25 yards on kick returns and 21.0 yards on punts, though the numbers leveled off during the regular season. Around the NFL Commanders moving Brandon Coleman back to LT after Laremy Tunsil injury | The Athletic Only 72 hours after celebrating the signing of veteran receiver Stefon Diggs, the Washington Commanders lost five-time Pro Bowl left tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps, an injury that will keep him out for a good portion of the season, if not its entirety. Replacing a player of that caliber is a tall task, especially this late in the offseason. Washington may add to its offensive line — for depth, if not more — but for now, the plan is to turn to Brandon Coleman at left tackle, according to a team source who spoke on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly on the matter. Teddy Bridgewater leaves Lions to retire again, coach says | ESPN Head coach Dan Campbell said he believes that this retirement could stick for Bridgewater, who had previously retired after the 2023 season only to return to the Lions the next season. “I think he can only truly answer that, but I feel like this is where it’s at for sure right now. This is where it needs to be and where he felt,” Campbell said. “And his biggest worry was letting us down. That’s the type of guy he is, and he’s not. “That’s as far as it can get. He meant a lot.” Safety Plan: Defensive Back Brandon Jones fills in as Broncos kicker, makes three field goals in scrimmage | NFL.com Jones did not kick in high school or college. “I just have some history in playing soccer,” he said. “I don’t know how I even got to kick. Me and I guess, I can’t remember… I think I just was joking with ‘Riz’ like, ‘Yo, I can kick if you ever need an emergency-kicker-type of situation.’ Then he called my bluff and put me to the test one day, I think it was some time last year. I made an extra point. Apparently, there are a lot of guys on the team that can also kick, but I guess I just got the opportunity today. [I] went three-for-four, so not too bad.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs training camp: 5 observations from the second week of practices 3. R Mason Thomas should see more snaps as time goes on With second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte missing nearly all of the second week of camp with an injury, the primary workload for the first team went to Felix Anudike-Uzomah, while rookie R Mason Thomas mostly took snaps with the second team and a few rotational situations with the first team. The team appears to be willing to give Anudike-Uzomah every chance to earn playing time after struggling through the first three seasons of his career, but on Friday during the two-minute drill, it was Thomas who walked on to the field when the first-team defense took on the starting offense. The two-minute drill can be where games are won and lost, and the team did not hide the fact that the rookie is already one of the defense’s best pass-rush options. title: Chiefs training camp: Roster superlatives before preseason Week 1
summary: It has been a fun time getting to know this year’s Kansas City Chiefs at training camp up in St. Joseph, Missouri, so far this summer. Let’s keep the fun rolling with some superlatives, listing the extremes of the roster in order to get more familiar with the team ahead of a preseason Week 1 […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Omari Evans #7 catches a ball during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It has been a fun time getting to know this year’s Kansas City Chiefs at training camp up in St. Joseph, Missouri, so far this summer. Let’s keep the fun rolling with some superlatives, listing the extremes of the roster in order to get more familiar with the team ahead of a preseason Week 1 game against the Los Angeles Rams next Saturday, August 15th, at Arrowhead Stadium. Measurables were collected from players’ pre-draft process. Here we go: Tallest player Offensive tackle Ethan Driskell — 6 feet 8 3/8 inches tall The third-year offensive tackle from the University of Marshall has spent most of camp as the third-team right tackle. However, with starting right guard Trey Smith missing practice last week, Driskell got more reps as the second-team right tackle. Shortest player Wide receiver Jacob De Jesus — 5 feet 6 inches tall De Jesus, a receiver and return man from the University of California, has been the most impressive undrafted free agent among this year’s rookie class in camp so far. That doesn’t mean he will be lucky enough to make the roster. It’s a long shot, one special teams coordinator Dave Toub acknowledged after Saturday’s practice . “De Jesus is solid, great catcher, just not a real big guy,” Toub acknowledged. “He’s going to be exciting in the preseason games, for sure.” Heaviest player Defensive tackle Cole Brevard — 343 pounds The big nose tackle is an undrafted rookie from the University of Texas. He’ll be hoping his mass shows up in the preseason games, looking to find a spot on the practice squad as a reserve A-gap tackle. Longest arms Offensive lineman Matt Waletzko — 36 1/8 inches long A former Dallas Cowboys fifth-round draft pick, Waletzko appeared in 11 games for Dallas between the 2022 – 2024 seasons. He has spent most of camp on the third-team offensive line, lining up as both a tackle and a guard. Biggest hands Offensive tackle Jaylon Moore — 11-inch hand size The veteran tackle is battling for the right tackle position with rookie Kahlil Benson. Benson had a bigger pre-draft profile than Moore, but Moore has the biggest paws on the team, an underrated trait for holding up in the trenches. The 3 fastest players Wide receiver Xavier Worthy — 4.21 seconds in the 40-yard dash Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton — 4.28 seconds Wide receiver Omari Evans — 4.28 seconds We all know the fastest player on the team, but tied for second is undrafted rookie wideout Omari Evans from the University of Washington. He stands 6 feet tall and weighs 190 pounds, showing off explosiveness as well with a 41-inch vertical leap during this year’s pre-draft process. Quickest acceleration Wide receiver Jeff Caldwell — 1.48 seconds 10-yard split in the 40-yard dash Caldwell, a rare athlete from the University of Cincinnati, has been buried on the depth chart during camp, playing mostly with the third-team offense. The preseason would be an excellent time for Caldwell to show off that acceleration, along with the 42-inch vertical leap and a team-leading broad jump of 134 inches. Most recently a basketball player Tight end Mason Pline From Furman University, Pline found his way into the NFL in the 2024 NFL Draft cycle after one season of football for the Paladins. Before that, Pline played basketball and football at Ferris State University. He stands over 6 feet 6 inches tall and weighs 251 pounds. He has not seen work with the first team, but Pline has shown off his rebounding skills by reaching for passes down the field with the reserve teams so far in camp.
