title: Chiefs training camp: 5 observations from the second week of practices
summary: There have been ten practices through roughly two weeks of Kansas City Chiefs training camp. I was fortunate enough to attend for four days in St. Joe as the Chiefs got into the dog days of camp. This iteration of the team has many questions, but after watching in depth, things are starting to look […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: R Mason Thomas #51 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There have been ten practices through roughly two weeks of Kansas City Chiefs training camp. I was fortunate enough to attend for four days in St. Joe as the Chiefs got into the dog days of camp. This iteration of the team has many questions, but after watching in depth, things are starting to look a bit clearer. Here are five things I observed. 1. Peter Woods looks the part Training camp can often be a collage of sparks and hype, but since the pads have come on, first-round defensive lineman Peter Woods has more than looked the part. The first defensive tackle taken in the 2026 NFL Draft, Woods has shown a blend of explosion and power, making plays throughout camp so far. Woods giving Benson the business in inside run. pic.twitter.com/8jo9bju63B — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 After playing at a listed weight under 300 pounds during his final season at Clemson, Woods entered camp weighing roughly 308 to 313 pounds. He has showcased explosion and power this week in practice. KC trying to set up a draw, but Woods stands his ground and helps stuff the run. pic.twitter.com/ZmVFdaIE3W — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 He also showed off mobility that leaves the door wide open for what he can become as a player in defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s exotic looks. Great blitz pickup for KC. pic.twitter.com/K1aNcBZkk6 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 Woods has been by far the hottest name in camp since the pads came on during Monday’s sessions, and all eyes will continue to be on him through the remainder of the preseason. 2. The secondary could be a cause for concern There is plenty of time to right the ship, but the Chiefs’ secondary could be a cause for concern early on in the season. With cornerback Mansoor Delane’s status unclear, and Kristian Fulton and L’Jarius Sneed missing nearly the entire week, the Chiefs’ cornerback unit outside of Nohl Williams struggled. Veteran safeties Chammari Conner and Jaden Hicks also struggled. Justin Fields with a nice pass to Jeff Caldwell who had a step on Conner — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 6, 2026 The lone bright spots were safety Alohi Gillman, who made a few nice plays, and rookie slot defender Jadon Canady; the first-year player from Oregon earned more playing time with the first team as the week progressed. 3. R Mason Thomas should see more snaps as time goes on With second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte missing nearly all of the second week of camp with an injury, the primary workload for the first team went to Felix Anudike-Uzomah, while rookie R Mason Thomas mostly took snaps with the second team and a few rotational situations with the first team. The team appears to be willing to give Anudike-Uzomah every chance to earn playing time after struggling through the first three seasons of his career, but on Friday during the two-minute drill, it was Thomas who walked on to the field when the first-team defense took on the starting offense. The two-minute drill can be where games are won and lost, and the team did not hide the fact that the rookie is already one of the defense’s best pass-rush options. Thomas has looked sharp and has worked to shed the notion that he is an undersized speed-only player. R Mason Thomas lands the inside hands against Simmons and drives him back in 1v1. pic.twitter.com/RHQzRQTsGp — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 5, 2026 While the speed rush got him drafted, seeing him play with power has been nice as well and will open up more roles for him as he continues to progress. Looks like R Mason Thomas gets the better of Benson on this one. Would have been close to a sack. pic.twitter.com/hsCxW65v5P — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 5, 2026 It has been quite some time since the Chiefs have had a player with the combination of speed and bend off the edge that Thomas has, and there is a feeling the team could be trying to buy time for him to develop the other aspects of his game before deeming him a full-time starter. Thomas working on Moore pic.twitter.com/QtJaoZhWk1 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 8, 2026 Thomas still has a ways to go, but the ability is flashing, and it feels inevitable that his snap count will increase soon. 4. Kahlil Benson could be doing something remarkable The team believes in rookie-minicamp tryout signing Kahlil Benson, and that was never more apparent than after a week of playing nearly all right tackle, transitioning inside to right guard after Trey Smith missed Friday and Saturday with a hip injury. Good Pro by the Chiefs. Walker fighting to keep Thomas off of 15. pic.twitter.com/9uultcDT7d — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 After a week to evaluate his game, nothing was extremely overwhelming, other than he often found himself in the right place at the right time and played with just enough leverage to create movement in the ground game, along with quick enough feet to play tackle. Not the best camera work, but Woods and Benson working in 1v1 pass pro. pic.twitter.com/hDP4JVKGn0 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 The decision to slide him over to right guard once Smith was out speaks volumes to how the organization feels about him, and is adding to the likelihood every day that he will see the field frequently in 2026. 5. Kenneth Walker has a mean streak It’s been hard to miss the Chiefs’ newest free agent addition so far in camp, and on Saturday he was involved in one of the more viral plays camp has seen so far. Boys, I’m a K9 guy. pic.twitter.com/66WQpsfUsU — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 8, 2026 I have been traveling to St. Joe to watch the Chiefs practice for over a decade now, and I have never seen this. After further thought, I don’t think I have seen anything quite like this in a lifetime of attending football practices and games. Sure, this would evoke an ejection in a real game, but Walker appears to have had enough of the shenanigans presented by the defensive players, and after all, this is practice. Last season, the swagger and confidence many had become accustomed to the Chiefs playing with never showed up, and when it did, there was more of a sense of false bravado than anything. So far in camp, Walker has been a tone setter and is making his case to become one of the true alpha dogs on a team that is in no short supply of alpha dogs. Simmons helps free K9 pic.twitter.com/mIDbVmSRqr — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 8, 2026 Walker carried a large workload on Saturday — much like he did on Wednesday and Friday — and seems on track to be the Chiefs’ workhorse early in the season. Walker lead toss with Moore leading the way. pic.twitter.com/I8gyn1LrUU — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 The Chiefs finally got knocked down last year, but the new players clearly have a mindset and attitude to get them back on track to being the hunters once more.

title: Patrick Mahomes details final steps in pre-camp injury clearance
summary: As the Kansas City Chiefs left for training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, the team received some welcome news. Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes was cleared to practice after spending the offseason rehabbing from a season-ending knee injury suffered in December. Speaking after Saturday’s practice, Mahomes revealed the final hurdle he overcame […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 26: Quarterback Patrick Mahomes #15 participates during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Kansas City Chiefs left for training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, the team received some welcome news. Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes was cleared to practice after spending the offseason rehabbing from a season-ending knee injury suffered in December. Speaking after Saturday’s practice, Mahomes revealed the final hurdle he overcame before Dr. Dan Cooper — who repaired the quarterback’s ACL and LCL — would sign off on a return to full participation. Final clearance was not a given. “I had to pass a test that was pretty hard,” Mahomes recalled. “Then, they made me go out there and do a lot of cutting and jumping and all that different type of stuff. I’m a competitor. So, when it comes to a test of physical ability, I wanted to go out there and do it, but he wasn’t going to take it easy on me. He was going to push me to my limit and see what I got. “You’re nervous because you’re so close to camp and have to pass it kind of on that first time, but I was able to do that.” Receiving Cooper’s blessing has allowed Mahomes to have confidence in fully returning to practice. However, he knows that he remains under scrutiny as he tries to overcome a serious injury. “It wasn’t like he was just going to clear me to clear me,” Mahomes noted. “So, I knew that I could go out there and be myself. Now, it’s about proving to the coaches and the doctors as they watch all this stuff that I can go out there and do that in the regular season as well.” For his part, Mahomes has had no noticeable setback through two weeks of training camp. “It feels great,” he said of the knee. “I’m just pushing every single day. I’m trying to stack days together. I feel like when you’re tired, sometimes you don’t even think about it. I’m trying to protect it, but at the same time, I’m trying to push it and get myself ready to go for the season.” Mahomes has been seen adjusting his knee brace at times. Since the team has transitioned to padded practices with the knee completely covered, it has seemed to bother him less. Every OL knows this dance. It’s tight and hot and constricting having game pants on with a knee brace under but it beats adjusting and pulling on the brace after every play when you’re just wearing shorts. https://t.co/ZF0X3Rc2wI — Mitchell Schwartz (@MitchSchwartz71) August 8, 2026 “I forget about it sometimes,” he admitted. “I try to be smart, but you get through camp, and you’re trying to compete. Practices are long, and you want to win the rep. So, there are times when I do forget about it and just play football. Which is a good thing. I’ll have to do that again whenever we get to the regular season. It’s about just learning how to play with what I’ve got. I feel like I’m able to move and do the things that I can. We’re just going to keep pushing it and see where I can get it to so I can hopefully get that OK to go out there and play Week 1.” It would be an upset at this point if Mahomes does not play Week 1 against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football.” The preseason appears to be another matter. On Friday, head coach Andy Reid all but ruled Mahomes out of the first exhibition on August 15 against the Los Angeles Rams — and implied that Mahomes is uncertain to suit up at all in the early slate. Mahomes has not been told that he is not playing in the preseason, but the decision will not affect his preparation. “Whatever Coach says. I’m going to prepare to play,” he remarked. “He hasn’t told me anything. So, I’ll prepare to play and prepare to get myself ready. We’ll see where we go from there. If not, I’ll be as locked in as I am during the game and try to get myself ready to go for the game. It’s just a process of trying to make sure you’re ready for the season. Whatever Coach thinks is the best, I’ll do.” Whenever Mahomes retakes the field, he knows that he will have to battle being cautious with the aggressive style that made him the league’s most recognizable player. Great blitz pickup for KC. pic.twitter.com/K1aNcBZkk6 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 7, 2026 “I’m trying to hold back because I’m a competitor, and I like competing,” he explained. “All of a sudden, I’m running and cutting back and trying to pitch the ball. It’s trying to keep yourself from doing stuff like that, but when it’s fourth down, and you want to try to make a play happen, you try to make a play happen. I’m not going to lose who I am, but I’m going to try to keep myself smart and keep myself in position to be out there for my teammates.” While return from serious injury is new territory for him, Mahomes wants observers to know that he is up for the challenge. “I’ll be ready to play,” the three-time Super Bowl champion declared. “I know that. That’s just how you have to go about it. Whenever the opportunity comes to go out there and play football, you have to go out there and maximize it. If that’s the preseason, I’ll go out there and play. If that’s the regular season, I’ll go out there and play. Whenever I get that opportunity, I’ll be ready to step back on that football field and be myself.”

title: Trent McDuffie on joining the Rams: “It feels like home”
summary: Trent McDuffie bolstering the Los Angeles Rams secondary is one of the biggest positional upgrades for any team this NFL offseason. And the two-time All-Pro has taken to his new team quite quickly. “It feels like home,” McDuffie said this week in an interview with the Rams’ social media team. “When I put that Rams […]
full_text: Trent McDuffie bolstering the Los Angeles Rams secondary is one of the biggest positional upgrades for any team this NFL offseason. And the two-time All-Pro has taken to his new team quite quickly. “It feels like home,” McDuffie said this week in an interview with the Rams’ social media team. “When I put that Rams helmet on, it was like a feeling that I should be here, a feeling of almost community. The fans, I’ve known them forever, I grew up here … they’ve welcomed me into this team and this culture with open arms.” It’s hard to ask for more from a blockbuster acquisition than what McDuffie has already given this Rams franchise. Obviously, he’s a stud of a player, whether that means he’s playing in the slot or on the boundary. But the fact that he wants to be a part of this organization and has already embraced it is a welcome addition, too. Even with an interview segment that’s gone viral this week about being made about his trade away from the Kansas City Chiefs in the moment, McDuffie had previously admitted a desire to play for the Rams one day . Sometimes things work out exactly how they’re supposed to. And if you’re one who likes to buy in on vibes, McDuffie’s aforementioned interview is only going to further sell you on this group. “They’re so smart, and they just love ball,” McDuffie said, regarding his teammates. “Everybody’s out here working hard, no doubt, but they’re enjoying it, and that makes it a little bit more special when you come out here and enjoy playing football.” This is the time of year when everyone should be excited about their team. Training camp is the football equivalent of the old baseball axion that “hope springs eternal.” If you’re already feeling down about your situation, it’s probably not going to be a fun fall for your franchise. But for a team that has a target on its back and one, singular goal in mind this season, it’s not nothing that things feel so positive right now. Sports culture in this country lauds the “businesslike mentality” a great deal, but threading the needle of intense focus and giddy excitement can only be a positive. There’s no downside to boosting morale. How does all of that translate to the football field? The camaraderie, the energy, that positive feelings, that’s all coalescing with the best roster in football. And as played out as the phrase “iron sharpens iron” is, that’s something McDuffie and these Rasm are living by. “I’m going against the two best receivers in the league with Davante [Adams] and Puka [Nacua],” McDuffie said. “Each day that they come out on this field, they’re ready to work and you know you have to be at your best. And that’s what I love. If I have to come out here every day and be at my best, one, we’re going to raise the standard, two, I’m going to get them better, three, they’re going to get me better.” When a new team leader is bringing this kind of excitement and passion for the game, it’s hard not to buy all the way in.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Did a potential landing spot just open for Stetson Bennett?
summary: Teddy Bridgewater informed the Detroit Lions that he plans to step away from the team and will likely retire, according to a report from ESPN’s Ian Rapoport. This abrupt opening creates a void behind Jared Goff—one that is important and must be filled for a playoff hopeful. Could the Los Angeles Rams be a trade […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 31: Stetson Bennett #13 of the Los Angeles Rams calls out a play during the Los Angeles Rams Training Camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Teddy Bridgewater informed the Detroit Lions that he plans to step away from the team and will likely retire, according to a report from ESPN’s Ian Rapoport . This abrupt opening creates a void behind Jared Goff—one that is important and must be filled for a playoff hopeful. Could the Los Angeles Rams be a trade partner that could help Brad Holmes and the Lions patch things back together quickly? Stetson Bennett is battling with first-round rookie Ty Simpson to become the primary backup to Matthew Stafford. Reports from practice indicate that Bennett has taken a significant step forward in his fourth training camp, although the wheels have seemingly come off in recent days and turnovers have ratcheted up. We know that Simpson will play in the preseason . Whether Bennett takes the field remains to be seen. Sean McVay continues to mull over the decision. Not playing would be a ringing endorsement that Bennett has won the backup job; however, the fact that McVay does not find his decision easily made is also telling. The backup quarterback competition may still be in flux. Simpson has displayed his strong processing and decision-making skills. His arm is proving to be more talented than he received credit for over the draft process. The only advantage Bennett has over the rookie is time—and that competitive edge is soon to fade. So if McVay’s decision between the two players is even close at all, why not move Bennett in exchange for draft capital? The Rams are running low on future picks because of their recent veteran trade acquisitions. It’s a way to restock the cupboard and creating a path to playing time for a young player that has probably earned it. But Bennett does have value for the Rams. Simpson should not play until he’s absolutely ready. Bennett’s presence is a way to insulated the rookie from stepping onto the field too soon. A mid or late round draft pick is not worth the potential downside of playing Simpson prematurely and cratering his confidence. The Lions need another quarterback behind Jared Goff. The Rams are uniquely positioned to help them out, and the two teams have a history of collaboration through trade. These are dots worth connecting and keeping an eye on over the coming weeks. Could Stetson Bennett soon find himself in Detroit?
author: JB Scott

title: Fiske on Garrett: ‘Not all men are created equal’
summary: Braden Fiske doesn’t think the Los Angeles Rams necessarily traded for a normal man when they acquired Myles Garrett in the offseason. “Not all men are created equal,” said Fiske this week. Could Garrett’s presence help Fiske become the most man he’s ever been on the field? “Not all men are created equal, that’s for […]
full_text: Woodland Hills, - June 08:Rams Kobie Turner (91) and Braden Fiske (55) at Rams practice on Monday, June 8, 2026. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Braden Fiske doesn’t think the Los Angeles Rams necessarily traded for a normal man when they acquired Myles Garrett in the offseason. “Not all men are created equal,” said Fiske this week . Could Garrett’s presence help Fiske become the most man he’s ever been on the field? “Not all men are created equal, that’s for sure,” Fiske said of Garrett on Thursday, via the team website . “He’s a baller, no doubt. He’s getting a slide, there’s no doubt about that. Trying to work off him or vice versa, communicating. The biggest thing right now is working on our communication of how to rush together, how we’re going to attack certain looks. As all four, the certain looks that we’re going to get when he’s on the field, preparing for that and doing our best to work off each other. It’s been good so far though. I think we’re making strides.” While Aaron Donald’s potential return looms over Fiske’s immediate future, Garrett’s present presence could give L.A. the best defensive line in the NFL. Here are all the Rams links to know for Sunday. No Update on Aaron Donald ( oc register ) Sean McVay has nothing new to say about Donald. “I don’t know yet,” he said. “We’re (going to) see.” Early during the Rams’ two weeks spent at LMU for training camp, McVay stated that fans should not expect an update on Donald until the team returned to Woodland Hills . When asked Saturday if there’s any update on Donald, McVay said there is not. “No update on that as of right now,” McVay said. The next “no update” should happen on Sunday. Fiske sees AD return as chance to learn (oc register) Fiske would welcome Donald, but doesn’t think the team needs him right now. “I try to think of being impacted in the right way, in a healthy way of I can learn from him if he does choose (to return),” Fiske said. “And if he doesn’t, I love the group that we have, and we’re getting some really good work out here. But, if that’s what he chooses to do, we’re here, we’re going to get some work. And if he’s not, we’ll continue this train rolling and get this thing going.” McVay ready for Cowboys joint practice (oc register) Tuesday will be a joint practice between the Rams and Cowboys, who training camp at Oxnard. “I think when you go against each other as much as we’ve done up to this point, it’s good to be able to just kind of change it up and get a feel to go against different schemes and great players,” McVay said. “(I am) looking forward to being able to go against some different schemes in really all three phases is kind of the the best thing, and some really good personnel that they have.” Joint practice is more valuable to the Rams than preseason, although this year will be different in that regard. Stetson Bennett may not play in preseason ( AP News ) McVay is pleased with what he’s seen from Bennett and could rest him for the entire month, giving Ty Simpson more snaps to develop his game. We already posted that Simpson will play next week . “He’s just taking advantage of his reps,” McVay said. “He’s aggressive. He’s a playmaker. He’s going to be aggressive, but not reckless. He can make some things happen off-schedule. The way that we’re able to get in and out of the huddle in terms of his overall command has been significantly improved.” Don’t count out the veteran QB options though if McVay changes his mind. Myles Garrett eyes bigger NFL history ( Yahoo! Sports ) Garrett wants to continue chasing sacks in 2026. Including the most-ever through a player’s first 10 seasons. On that subject, Garrett appeared on ‘Inside Rams Camp’ on Thursday and revealed he is chasing some big history in 2026. “Break my own record. I mean, there’s a couple records on the way. You know, if I get 20, I have the most by year 10 of anyone, and that would be passing Reggie. And you know, I want to, you know, be up there and be his peer and surpass him, but I also want to, you know, break my own records in which I’ve created and go out there and get 24, 25,” Garrett said. Will get get 25 with the Rams this year? Andrew Whitworth HOF eligible in 2027 ( Yahoo! Sports ) Will Whit get into the Hall? Former Los Angeles Rams offensive tackle Andrew Whitworth is eligible for the NFL Hall of Fame class of 2027. AP In his 17-year career, he was known as one of the best left tackles in the league, as he was selected to 4 Pro Bowls and was a two-time first-team All-Pro in 2015 and 2017. Whitworth was a core player and fan favorite during his time with the Bengals, as he helped the team reach the playoffs six times during his tenure. In 2014, he had a perfect season for an offensive lineman, as he did not allow a single sack. I understand what’s special about Whitworth, but his particular type of resume hasn’t usually gotten players into the Hall of Fame. However, maybe in his case the Super Bowl at the end of his career will get him over the hump. Rams waive Drey Norwood ( RamsWire ) “Norwood, an undrafted rookie out of Missouri, played in 54 games during his collegiate career, starting in 30 of them.” Okay, there you have it. Comment of the Day On Saturday, I asked Rams fans if Steven Jackson should be in the Hall of Fame . Here’s what one of you said. ohramsfan: Yes, he persevered on horrid teams and produced every season. What do you think? Share your opinion in the comments and maybe tomorrow you’ll get comment of the day. Feed Post of the Day Jayden Daniels is too afraid to try no-look passes. Once again emphasizing just how special and unique of a quarterback Matthew Stafford continues to be.

title: Las Vegas Raiders Summer Scouting: CB Rankings
summary: I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some […]
full_text: SOUTH BEND, IN - NOVEMBER 22: Leonard Moore #15 of the University of Notre Dame concentrates before the snap during a game between Syracuse University and University of Notre Dame at Notre Dame Stadium on November 22, 2025 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some talent on the interior OL, and I’d expect Las Vegas to add more in 2027 as John Spytek does. These rankings are extremely early, and they will evolve over not only the summer but the next 8-10 months throughout the season, and into draft season. Some lists will feature 10, 15, 20, or more ranked prospects but I’ll include others on the list below to note. Leonard Moore, Notre Dame – 6’2/195, Jr Even as a Notre Dame fan, I promise I’m not being bias here there’s a very good chance that the Irish have the best CB, SAF, and linebacker in college football and arguably the best safety duo and cornerback trio. Leonard Moore is exceptional, and arguably a near generational cornerback. He’s physical, big, and smart and it shows with a career 80 tackles, 7 interceptions (including 5 in 2025), 19 PBU, and 3 FF while being a 2x All-American. Moore is long, he uses his length well, and he’s going to take away almost every contested catch situation allowing 4 in his career. Moore has elite awareness, a ton of lower body athleticism, and he’s an exceptional run defender as well. The true junior has a knack for the ball in space, will break off his routes, and in man coverage he’s sticky on the hip with elite contact balance. He’s a smart, highly physical, and highly talented cornerback who shows an ability to anchor a secondary for years. Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia – 6’0/180, R-So Georgia and Notre Dame have competed before for top players with Bowers/Mayer, then this year with their safety and corner battles. Robinson is smaller, but he’s a good player and paired with KJ Bolden makes an elite secondary duo. Robinson had 20 tackles, 4 interceptions, and 9 PBU in his frst season as a starter, largely due to his athleticism and ball skills. Robinson is best in zone coverage, he has a quick snappy first step, elite hip and foot speed, and he’ll drive on the ball quickly. Robinson baits quarterbacks, uses leverage to his advantage, and he’ll sink and drive on the ball exceptionally well to take away a route or take the ball away. Robinson is physical, he’ll fight defenders at the line, boxes out receivers in coverage, and he does a good job using the sideline to his advantage. Robinson stays low, plays with good foot speed, and he mirrors defenders well. There’s a lack of tackling, and his frame is concerning, but the ball skills are the best in the class with elite athleticism as well. Xavier Scott, Illinois – 5’11/190, Sr A safety/nickel hybrid, Scott had an injured year in 2025 but I expect a bounceback in 2026. Scott is undersized, but he plays similar to Devon Witherspoon. He’s shown elite hip flexibility, has smooth snappy hips, and his footspeed is exceptional. Additionally, Scott does a great job to mirror defenders, use his ball skills to fight the ball in the air, and he’ll be an elite nickel defender in the NFL. Scott doesn’t have the size, but he’s shown good strength to take on blocks, is able to jam defenders at the line of scrimmage, and he has above average length which allows him to get his hand into the catch point and knock the ball out. Scott is fluid athletically, and he’s shown good long speed. The NFL is valuing the nickel heavily & Scott should be a top 20 pick in April with a year similar to his 2024 season with 50 tackles, 4 INT, and 11 PBU. Ashton Hampton, Clemson – 6’2/200, R-So Hampton is a former WR moved CB and he’ll be asked to take on Avieon Terrell’s role in 2026. Hampton is big, but he’s able to move which is rare for a CB his size. He has decent foot speed, snappy hips, and he sinks into the route well which allows him to break onto the ball consistently. Hampton does have some moments he’s immediately beaten off the line but has good recovery speed. Additionally, he shows the best traits in man coverage to match and mirror defenders, play with a quick mind, and he is able to utilize his leverage and the sideline to push defenders routes. He’s physical, and will get flagged but Hampton enjoys to fight for the ball, though it can be a bailout for average first step speed and inconsistent long speed which cause him to lag behind at times. He’s a good athlete, moves well, and shows a ton of instincts and good man coverage skills. Kelley Jones, Mississippi State – 6’4/195, R-So Jones moves well, something rarely any 6’4 CB does. He hauled in 2 interceptions & 12 PBU in 2025 and his length is elite. Jones is able to reach into the receivers pocket, knock out the ball, and he’s able to use his length to close passing windows or smack the ball away at the catch point. Jones isn’t great in man coverage, he’s shown inconsistent long speed and his immediate burst is average as is his recovery speed. In zone, Jones moves well going forward with an elite first step, and his length helps to take away a variety of passing angles. Additionally, he’s smart & patient with an ability to sit on concepts, use the sideline, and drive on the ball well. He’s an average tackler, with good size, and physicality, but I’d like to see better angles and more physical nature. Zabien Brown, Alabama – 6’0/192, R-So Jayden Bellamy, UCF – 6’1/180, R-Jr Bellamy is a sleeper. H’s a zone coverage corner, and he’s extremely lean with good length. Additionally, Bellamy is exceptionally smart, with an ability to read and react immediately, preview route concepts, and he does a great job to drive on the ball and take away route concepts. Bellamy excels with his football IQ and while an average athlete, you can’t teach his instincts and ball skills. He does over commit at times, has some concerns when it comes to his tackling angles, but it’s hard to deny the instincts. Brice Pollock, Texas Tech – 6’0/195, R-Jr Vicari Swain, South Carolina – 6’0/185, Jr Swain made headlines as a returner, despite 28 tackles, 2 INT, and 7 PBU while adding 19 PR, 302 yards and 3 touchdowns. He will rise with a good season, and it’s off the pure athletic nature he possesses. Swain is quick footed, he has elite foot speed, and he does a great job in start stop situations as he sinks his hips well. Additionally, Swain does have elite quick feet in first step situations, long speed, and explosiveness. There’s likely no corner in the class more athletic, or faster, than Swain, but he needs to improve in the positional instincts, technique, and rely less on his athleticism. Swain shows good length, has elite balance, and there’s a lot of immediate reaction in his game which allows him to fly to the ball. There’s a high level upside for Swain, but a large floor also though he’ll succeeed in the NFL for his return ability. OJ Frederique Jr, Miami – 6’0/180, R-So Chris Peal, Syracuse – 6’1/200, R-So Eli Bowen, Oklahoma – 5’9/185, R-So Bowen the brother of fellow Oklahoma DB Peyton Bowen is kinda fascinating as a prospect. He’s a likely nickel in the NFL but plays physical enough to play the boundary with 2 TFL, 3 INT, and 11 PBU in his career. Additionally, Bowen has some snaps at FS though I think a nickel move is likely in his future. He’s twitchy in coverage, moves exceptionally well, and fires off the ball with good hip flexibility. Bowen shows good start/stop ability, he decelerates quickly and tracks the route concept incredibly well. In addition, Bowen is physical in the run game, he’ll play big works off blocks, and is a willing tackler with good form (10% career…

title: The Year 2 bar for Raiders cornerback Darien Porter
summary: Standing nearly 6-foot-3 and 195 pounds with blazing speed, Darien Porter was a prototype cornerback for the previous Las Vegas Raiders coaching staff — particularly head coach Pete Carroll. The Carroll architype is a tall, long-armed, and fast cornerback and with his height, 33 1/8-inch arms, and 4.30-second timed 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine, […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 09: Darien Porter #26 of the Las Vegas Raiders speaks to the media after the rookie minicamp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 09, 2025 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Standing nearly 6-foot-3 and 195 pounds with blazing speed, Darien Porter was a prototype cornerback for the previous Las Vegas Raiders coaching staff — particularly head coach Pete Carroll. The Carroll architype is a tall, long-armed, and fast cornerback and with his height, 33 1/8-inch arms, and 4.30-second timed 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine, Porter checked off all the boxes and general manager John Spytek made the Iowa State product the Raiders’ third-round pick (68th overall) in the 2025 NFL Draft. Now it’s offensive-minded Klint Kubiak, a rising star creative play caller at the helm of the Silver & Black as head coach and instead of Patrick Graham at defensive coordinator (he’s now with the Pittsburgh Steelers orchestrating their defense), it’s fellow rookie coach Rob Leonard running the defense in Las Vegas. And the 25-year-old cornerback is once again trying to make an impression and earn starting snaps once more — albeit against a restocked cornerback room that has more youth, promise, and — let’s face it — quantity and quality that Porter didn’t face in his rookie season in 2025. While he did play in all 17 games and notched 10 starts — playing 607 snaps on defense and 155 more on special teams — and garnered first-team reps in offseason practices and training camp, the fight for the outside starting gig opposite Eric Stokes is wide open. And that’s where the Year 2 bar starts for Porter: Securing the definitive CB2 spot. By The Numbers Darien Porter, Cornerback, 2nd Year 2025: 17 games (10 starts), 42 total tackles (29 solo), 3 pass deflections, fumble recovery Career: See above. Don't you Darien 🫵 #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/oD7NDIdhLM — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) August 8, 2026 The Competition Determined to not only get looks but turning those reps to showcase their better options, there are two 2026 draft picks and a resurgent 2024 selection vying for the CB2 job alongside Porter. Hezekiah Masses, the Raiders fifth-round pick in this past draft, is a standout story this offseason. The University of California product made the coaching staff notice and jumped right into the fray with first-team reps throughout the offseason and now in training camp. The 22-year-old brings good size at 6-foot-1 and 185 pounds. Fellow draft classmate Jermod McCoy, taken in the fourth round, is on a managed workload plan as he suffered an ACL injury in 2025. The 20-year-old Tennessee product had first-round talent with the ball skills to be a thief in the secondary. Working with the lower units, McCoy (6-foot and 193 pounds) is a wild card as his potential is tremendous, health permitting. Lastly, Decamerion Richardson is having a Raider revival. The 112th overall pick in the 2024 draft fit the Pete Carroll prototype at 6-foot-2 and 192-pound cornerback with his 32 3/8-inch arms and 4.34 speed. But he didn’t see a snap on defense last year. Displaying tight coverage in practices, the upward trend is good for the 24-year-old. Porter is no slouch in practice with his first-team reps. He’s as sticky and nuisance as his fellow cornerbacks and like Masses, Porter snared an interception in practices. That all said, it’s a wide open competition and Las Vegas is eager to see which cornerback showcases the grit and win the gig. There’s lots of competition among the #Raiders CBs this camp. Eric Stokes has one of the spots locked down but watch out for Hezekiah Masses, Darien Porter, and Jermod McCoy opposite him as camp rolls on one of them will emerge. pic.twitter.com/Vh2ryrOffP — Jesse Merrick – Silver & Black Sports Network (@JesseSBSN) July 31, 2026 “I was listening to Kirk Cousins talk about the quarterback competition,” Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard began when asked about having a young secondary. “It’s like they’re competing, but you’re not lined up out there against the other guy. So, in the room, it’s like you’re competing against yourself, the other guy, if he made a play, you want to make a play. They all are such different players in how they play corner. It’s nice to see the brotherhood in there and then watch them out here compete trying to help each other. ‘How do you see this?’ ‘How do you do that?’” Areas of Opportunity To separate himself from the rest of the hungry pack, Porter needs to not only showcase the ability to cover and take the ball away consistently, he must show improvement as a tackler. While he did rack up 42 total tackles in his rookie season (29 solo), Pro Football Reference charted the cornerback with five missed tackles and a 10.6 missed tackle percentage. Raiders safeties coach Matt Robinson’s time at the podium during a post practice press conference made the point of tackling very clear. “And especially as DBs, everybody thinks interceptions, picks, PBUs, but you’re going to be in a position to block destruction and tackling way more than you will be making true plays on the ball,” Robinson began, “You’re going to have more tackles than you are picks and PBUs. So, that messaging of style of play and being a physical defense and when you come out everybody’s expected to tackle, everybody’s expected go smash stuff, so I’m excited.” Of the aforementioned names above, Richardson and McCoy arrived to the NFL with reputations as sound tacklers in college. Masses showcased the physicality and willingness to mix it up but his slender and wiry frame is limiting. And then there’s Porter, the weakest in that area of the group. This is where wide receiver-turned-cornerback hurts Porter as his open-field tackling is amiss with poor angle and technique where the cornerback was either lunging or arm-tackling instead of wrapping up physically. Darien Porter enters year 2 in Las Vegas after logging over 600 snaps as a Rookie CB. He displayed the speed and athletic traits that made him a 3rd Round pick in '25, while battling some of the AFC West's most imposing X WR's. #Raiders #LasVegas pic.twitter.com/YZWV9xDLex — All 22 Films (@All_22_NFL_Cuts) May 27, 2026 Where converting from pass catcher to defender helps Porter though is in coverage. At his size, length, and speed he’s show glimpses of a sticky and smothering cornerback he can be on the perimeter. With the entire defense playing aggressive and fast like Leonard wants, it opens up opportunities for defensive backs to gamble and make plays on the ball — something that Robinson highlighted as the vital, too. “I think they’re just feeling the pressure of we got to play fast, we got to play aggressive, but we got to know what to do and be disciplined in the back end so the ball doesn’t go over our heads,” Robinson said. “But we got to be able to trust our eyes and then go make plays because this league is all about the ball. If you take the football away, one, you make yourself some money, and then you win games because of the turnover ratio.” The Bar Claiming the CB2 job opposite Stokes is the ultimate end goal for Porter. Competition breeds excellence and the fight for the role isn’t expected to temper soon. The secondary needs various starters to either ascend or maintain a higher level of play and perhaps competition breeds competence will suffice. Playing not only in all 17 regular season games but starting them is apt for Porter with 48 total tackles (34 solo), an interception, and 8 pass breakups is a reasonable Year 2 bar.

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 04: Caleb Rogers #76 of the Las Vegas Raiders celebrates as he runs off the field after the team's 14-12 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs at Allegiant Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have gone through nine days of training camp, and the camp battles are heating up. One of the main battles so far is for the right guard position with Caleb Rogers and Jackson Powers-Johnson. Powers-Johnson has taken the first snap with the first team so far in camp, but Rogers is right behind, getting plenty of snaps with the ones. It is a brutal competition, and Rogers got banged up on Saturday but was able to return quickly. He has made the competion neck and neck so far with his run blocking ability and knowledge in pass protection. On Saturday, Rogers talked to the media about the competition and how it is making everyone on the offensive line better. “I mean, again the standard of play is very high. Our job is to match that and to get the job done. It’s about being a part of the best five and pushing each other to figure out who that is. And it’s been an incredible process to be a part of, pushing each other every single day, coming in every single day with that mindset. It’s been incredible.” Fans are clamoring for the guards to be both Powers-Johnson and Rogers, but Spencer Burford is holding them off, causing a competition between the two. It will be interesting to see who comes out on top heading into Week 1. full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 04: De'von Achane #28 and Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins talk on the field during training camp practice at Baptist Health Training Complex on August 04, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following our discussion last night regarding the Miami Dolphins’ potential defensive MVP, we now turn our attention to the offensive side of the ball. Aside from the running backs room, the skill positions look significantly different this season. De’Von Achane remains the clear leader in the backfield, with a continued role in the passing game, while fans adjust to Malik Willis taking over at quarterback. At tight end, Greg Dulcich has emerged as the early favorite to lead in receptions. However, the wide receiver corps remains the biggest question mark following the departures of Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill. The team has revamped the unit by adding free agents Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell, drafting prospects like Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell, and leaning on returning players such as Malik Washington and Theo Wease. With 12 receivers currently on the roster, Miami will likely trim this group to roughly six for the 53-man squad, with a few more potentially landing on the practice squad. While reports suggest Malik Willis is building chemistry with Washington and Wease, and that Caleb Douglas looks like he was well worth his draft selection, the pecking order remains uncertain—particularly as we await Chris Bell’s return from injury to see how he competes once fully integrated into practice and game action. So this evening’s Phinsider Question Of The Day is: Who is your early choice to take the title of Miami Dolphins Offensive MVP for the 2026-2027 NFL season and why? Please share your thoughts and answers in the comments section below-

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: Reading The Tea Leaves Of The QB Competition
summary: The QB Competition is unavoidable. So far, the stats show Kyler Murray going 73-for-110 (66.3%) while pushing the ball more aggressively downfield, and J.J. McCarthy going 70-for-103 (67.9%) while playing more conservatively according to most reports. There has been some major differences though. Over the last four practices, Kyler Murray has out-snapped J.J. McCarthy 63 […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The QB Competition is unavoidable. So far, the stats show Kyler Murray going 73-for-110 (66.3%) while pushing the ball more aggressively downfield, and J.J. McCarthy going 70-for-103 (67.9%) while playing more conservatively according to most reports. There has been some major differences though. Over the last four practices, Kyler Murray has out-snapped J.J. McCarthy 63 to 33 with the first-team offense, effectively pulling away in what was publicly framed as an even battle. Overall, Murray has had 146 snaps to JJ’s 136. Both have had up and down days in practice with obvious nuance involved if you want to try and explain those days. Was it in full pads? Was it 7 on 7? Was it full speed? Etc. You will never be able to convince someone whose mind is already made up. Like mine. I do not know when a decision will be made nor do I know how KOC looks at these camp performances vs what beat writers and fans believe they are seeing. Why are we here and where will it lead to? Obviously, JJ being out all of year one led us to this moment. His injuries and play in year two forced the team into the decision to obtain Murray. The narrative that KOC did not simplify (dumb down) his offense soon enough for JJ is hogwash and just a lame excuse. Heading into year two the team did not bring in any real competition for JJ (why should they?) and he was handed the job. He lit up the New England Patriots in camp joint practices and thus, the team trusted that his year of mental reps had paid off and he was ready to run the entire offense. Once he got that high ankle sprain it cost him 5 games. When he return his mechanics were naturally a bit rusty but then he gets the concussion. When he came back from that he had the mechanics problem and processing issue. KOC cannot and should not alter an offense just because a QB has a bad outing or two especially one who is basically a rookie. KOC only had to change it up once it was not working for JJ. Simplifying your offense allows for opposing defenses to easily predict play calls and suffocate players like Jefferson and Addison. Eliminating the over the middle concepts destroyed the effectiveness of JJ and Addison. In his first 6 starts last year, JJ completed 54% of his passes with 8 TDs and 11 INTs and the team went 2 and 4. In his next 4 starts he completed 64% of his passes with 7 TDs and 3 INTs and the team went 4-0. This last stretch of games is where most supporters point to as evidence of his ability to play at a high level. By limiting McCarthy’s field of vision strictly to the boundaries and immediate checkdowns, his completion percentage surged to 64% and his turnovers plummeted to just 3 over the final stretch. While it managed to mask McCarthy’s flaws in the short term, it completely capped the offense’s ceiling—severely impacting the production of elite players down the stretch. The worst part of it was that the team played bottom-tier, unmotivated opponents, including the Commanders (who ranked dead last in defense and had fired their coaches) and a Giants team with an interim defensive coordinator. The Lions sat stars like Aidan Hutchinson, and the Packers completely rested Jordan Love and 15 other starters for the finale. Over those last four games, McCarthy only averaged 161 passing yards per game, completing 61-for-91 passes for 5 touchdowns to 2 picks while the running backs did the heavy lifting with 421 rushing yards. Star targets were totally neutralized—Justin Jefferson didn’t even cross 100 yards once, averaging a frustrating 54.5 yards per game (19 catches for 218 yards), while Addison, Nailor, and Hockenson were reduced to boundary decoys. The real engine was Brian Flores’ defense, which practically won those games alone by forcing 10 turnovers, logging 18 sacks, and allowing a tiny 6.5 points per game against a depleted schedule. All in all, it was a tough season for JJ due to injury. These stats are not overly concerning to me for a young inexperienced QB. It is just provided to here to give a little more context to those games. Ultimately, he did what he had to do and did not turn it over which led to the wins. Heading into the offseason, the team fired Kwesi and named Rob Brezinski interim GM. At the combine, Brez said this: “We need to have a baseline quarterback play to be successful. Every organization does.” Brzezinski paired that quote with public praise for McCarthy, calling him a “great person” who “works really hard”. But in the NFL, when management starts praising your personality while stating they are “looking under every stone” for options, the writing is on the wall. This caught my attention because it made me wonder who told him to say that or gave him the idea of the plan of action? I believe it came from the Wilfs who saw a $140 million investment in Justin Jefferson being wasted on a 54% completion rate, empty stadium seats in December, and a damaged team brand. Did they give the executive order that the 2026 season must be competitive? Me thinks so. KOC likely played a role in just giving his opinion of where JJ was at in his NFL QB Journey. So they get Murray and begin this “competition”. I am of the opinion that because KOC was a backup QB in the NFL and made that famous quote “teams fail QBs before QBs fail the team” (something like that), he is actually trying to bring JJ along in his journey. I believe KOC truly feels he spoke the truth with that quote, but if he has a mandate to win, how can he not do what is best for the team? So what happens if the team decided to name Murray the starter? Will they hang onto to JJ? Nolan Teasley has no ties to JJ. Will the team want to have a circus environment every time Murray throws a pick, has a bad game, or the team loses? 2026 Vikings Training Camp Full Schedule https://www.vikings.com/schedule/vikings-events/training-camp/schedule DATE : TIME : PRACTICE Saturday, Aug. 1 : Noon- 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Monday, Aug. 3 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Tuesday, Aug. 4 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Wednesday, Aug. 5 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Friday, Aug. 7 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Saturday, Aug. 8 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Sunday, Aug. 9 : 5 – 11 p.m. : 7 p.m. Tuesday, Aug. 11 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Wednesday, Aug. 12 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Thursday, Aug. 13 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Monday, Aug. 17 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Wednesday, Aug. 19 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. : Joint Practice with Baltimore Ravens Thursday, Aug. 20 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. : Joint Practice with Baltimore Ravens The Minnesota Vikings 2026 preseason schedule features three matchups Week 1: Saturday, August 15 at New York Giants (1:00 PM ET) Week 2: Saturday, August 22 vs. Baltimore Ravens (12:00 PM ET) Week 3: Friday, August 28 at Denver Broncos (Time TBD) Minnesota Vikings News and Links Vikings QB Announcement Coming Soon? https://www.minnesotasportsfan.com/minnesota-vikings/starting-qb-announcement-coming-soon-reports/ The Minnesota Vikings have a lot going on at 2026 training camp. But until the quarterback competition is OFFICIALLY decided between Kyler Murray and JJ McCarthy, nothing else really matters. In fact, after McCarthy had his best day of camp so far on Friday, there’s a loud segment of fans on social media — and undoubtedly some national media members — who still believe the QB “battle” in Minnesota is far from over. … “JJ McCarthy had a really nice training camp practice Friday for the Vikings. He had a deep out route that he completed to Dontae Fleming, had three touchdown passes in a four-play red zone drill a little bit later on, and overall just a really nice day, maybe his best day of the summer. But that would be more important if there already wasn’t a big gap between him…

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - JANUARY 4: Kevin O'Connell head coach of the Minnesota Vikings looks on from the sideline against the Green Bay Packers in the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time to take a look at the results of our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week about our Minnesota Vikings, and this week’s results were a lot closer than I thought they were going to be, honestly. Our question for this week was whether or not you thought the job of head coach Kevin O’Connell should be in jeopardy if the purple do not make the playoffs in 2026. After the votes were tallied, the fans appear to be split just about right down the middle on this one. Of those who responded to our poll, 49% believe that O’Connell’s employment status is going to be in trouble if the Vikings miss the playoffs for a second consecutive season in 2026. Heading into this year, the consensus among the Really Smart Football People™ seems to be that the Vikings are the fourth team in a four-team NFC North race. That was the case last year as well, and the Vikings wound up in third place courtesy of tiebreakers and on the outside looking in when it came to the playoff picture. They loaded up on defense in the 2026 NFL Draft, and everything on that side of the ball appears to be solid once again, but the quarterback situation is still in flux. If the Vikings can get things figured out at the game’s most important position, then there’s no reason that they shouldn’t be able to find themselves fighting for a playoff spot all the way to the end of the season, at the very least. If they can’t? Well. . .then O’Connell is probably going to have to spend some time updating his LinkedIn profile, at the very least, particularly given the fact that the Vikings now have a new General Manager in place. Those are the results of our SB Nation Reacts poll for this week, ladies and gentlemen. title: Vikings 2026 Training Camp: A QB Crisis, Camp Stars & a Comp Pick Twist
summary: Minnesota Vikings training camp 2026 has one burning question on every fan’s mind: do the Vikings have a quarterback who can win in the NFC North? After nine practices, Two Old Bloggers — Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano on Vikings 1st & SKOL — are sounding the alarm. The honest answer, delivered with trademark candor, […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Minnesota Vikings training camp 2026 has one burning question on every fan’s mind: do the Vikings have a quarterback who can win in the NFC North? After nine practices, Two Old Bloggers — Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano on Vikings 1st & SKOL — are sounding the alarm. The honest answer, delivered with trademark candor, is unsettling: both Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy have been, in the words of reporter Tyler Forness, “just fine.” And fine may not be enough to beat Jordan Love, Jared Goff, or Caleb Williams. The quarterback competition has dominated Vikings coverage, and for good reason. Murray has received roughly twice the first-team reps as McCarthy, raising legitimate questions about whether Kevin O’Connell has already decided the outcome. But rep count aside, neither signal-caller has seized the moment. As Darren put it bluntly: “The second worst outcome is what we have right now — both guys are so-so. Nobody’s really running away with it.” Dave echoed the concern, noting that a viral tweet framed it perfectly: Kyler should be proving he’s light years ahead of J.J., not the other way around. A Mike Sando survey of 50 NFL coaches and executives reinforced the worry — Murray ranked 23rd overall (Tier 3), McCarthy 34th (Tier 4), and every NFC North rival QB ranked ahead of them. Beyond the QB room, however, genuine reasons for optimism are emerging — and Two Old Bloggers covered them all. Key Points from This Episode: Charles Demmings (CB, 5th round) is making plays daily against Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings — the Vikings haven’t drafted and developed a quality corner since Xavier Rhodes in 2013 Caleb Banks (DT, #18 overall) is fully participating with no reported foot issues — a massive win after multiple surgeries; he’s being worked in gradually alongside Levi Drake Rodriguez, Jaylen Redmond, and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins Jake Golday (LB) is earning snaps with the ones under Brian Flores, showing he can already contribute at inside and outside linebacker — a potential immediate contributor Gavin Bartholomew (TE) is producing big catches daily, potentially following a Tyler Conklin-style development arc with T.J. Hockenson’s free agency looming after 2026 Jeshaun Jones (WR) leads camp in buzz but faces a brutal roster bubble — at 26, he’s six months younger than Justin Jefferson, with Tai Felton, Jauan Jennings, and Myles Price ahead of him Jamal Adams has switched to number 32 and is working at safety again under Flores — a potential Josh Metellus-style joker role could be in play Jordan Addison’s extension is the offseason’s next big business storyline; Zay Flowers’ 4-year/$140M Ravens deal is driving receiver market prices skyward, but Darren believes the Vikings have leverage through Jennings, Tai Felton’s development, and Addison’s trade value Compensatory pick alert: If Kyler Murray starts, plays well, and signs a big deal elsewhere, the Vikings could be in line for a 2028 third-round comp pick — similar to what they received for Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold The silver lining? Sam Darnold looked shaky at this same point in 2024 training camp and turned into an MVP-caliber performer. There’s still time. Joint practices against the Baltimore Ravens and the first preseason game against the Giants are the next big proving grounds for this Vikings roster. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Two Old Bloggers brings exactly the kind of unfiltered, experience-backed Minnesota Vikings analysis that cuts through the noise — every week on Vikings 1st & SKOL, part of the Bleav Network. Whether you’re optimistic or bracing for impact, Darren and Dave will help you make sense of it all with humor, history, and just enough existential dread to feel right at home. Don’t miss a single episode — subscribe, rate, and ring the bell wherever you get your podcasts. Fan With Us! We have your Minnesota Vikings talk amongst the Two Old Bloggers , Darren @KickassblogVike and Dave @Luft_Krigare . Join the conversation! title: Mike Vrabel gives insight into Terrell Williams’ new role with Patriots
summary: To close out their five-day practice block last Friday, the New England Patriots held a scrimmage. Besides splitting the roster in half, they also did the same with the coaching staff. On one side, you had the Blue Team led by running backs coach Tony Dews; on the other, the White Team was led by […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots assistant head coach Terrell Williams walks to the practice field during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images To close out their five-day practice block last Friday, the New England Patriots held a scrimmage. Besides splitting the roster in half, they also did the same with the coaching staff. On one side, you had the Blue Team led by running backs coach Tony Dews; on the other, the White Team was led by Terrell Williams. For Williams, it was a return to the spotlight after a disrupted 2025 season and subsequent role change within the organization. Originally arriving as defensive coordinator alongside Mike Vrabel last year, he was named assistant head coach this offseason. Before Friday’s scrimmage, Vrabel gave insight into what Williams’ new role entails. “He’s really taken control of that front seven,” the Patriots’ second-year head coach explained. “It’s something that’s critical to our defense, the way that we want to play, the style that we want to play and making sure when we pressure, when we run games, when we’re in different fronts. “That’s kind of really being able to bring Clint [McMillan]’s guys and [Mike Smith]’s guys together so that everybody’s seeing it the same way and that we’re coordinating how we want to rush and the way that we want to rush. So, that’s one way, still continuing to support Zak [Kuhr] and the defensive staff.” Williams’ one-year tenure as defensive coordinator was marked by medical challenges. After already missing time during the offseason because of what he later called a “health scare,” he was diagnosed with prostate cancer following New England’s regular season opener against the Raiders. With the now-52-year-old taking a leave of absence, inside linebackers coach Zak Kuhr took over play-caller duties. Kuhr, with behind-the-scenes support from Williams, coordinated a defense that helped the Patriots get all the way to the Super Bowl. His eventual promotion to full-time DC was therefore a logical step — as was Williams moving to assistant HC, especially with a focus on the defensive line. Before joining the Patriots in 2025, after all, Williams had spent his entire 27-year coaching career from college to the NFL along the D-line. Among his stops were the Titans, for whom he coached the position group throughout Vrabel’s six-year tenure as head coach. In 2023, their final season in Tennessee, he also supported Vrabel as assistant head coach. “I’ve always said he’s got a really special quality of being able to reach a lot of different players, whether that’s on defense or offense,” Vrabel said about Williams. “He’s already made bonds with guys like Caleb Lomu and Eli [Raridon]. He’s seen a lot of football in this league and been around a lot of different players. I see him spend a lot of time with guys. I always like that — when guys that have experience on one side of the ball and they have the capability of doing it, of reaching players on the other side of the ball that maybe his position goes against, and they can tell him the things that they’re doing well or any things to be able to encourage them.”

title: Patriots 53-man roster projection before preseason opener vs. Colts
summary: With joint practices and the preseason opener versus the Indianapolis Colts on the horizon, now is as good a time as ever for another 53-man roster projection. The New England Patriots are a solid team coming off a berth in the Super Bowl, but as you will see, there are some questions that lead to […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - July 26: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins at training camp on July 26, 2026. (Photo by Jessica Rinaldi/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images With joint practices and the preseason opener versus the Indianapolis Colts on the horizon, now is as good a time as ever for another 53-man roster projection. The New England Patriots are a solid team coming off a berth in the Super Bowl, but as you will see, there are some questions that lead to interesting choices especially toward the end of the roster. If you want to compare to Matt St. Jean’s pre-camp roster projection, please click here . And with that said, let’s get into it. Quarterback In (2): Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito Out (1): Behren Morton Behren Morton has surprised me with how good he has looked in camp, but Tommy DeVito has looked better as Drake Maye’s primary backup, and knows the system. I would expect Morton to make it back to the practice squad. Running back In (3): Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson, Jam Miller Out (3): Terrell Jennings, Lan Larison, Myles Montgomery Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson are roster locks, meaning that the real battle is for the RB3 spot. Lan Larison and Jam Miller have both looked good, and the Patriots liked Terrell Jennings enough last year to bring him back for his second year. The Patriots seem to want a more bruising back as their third option, which is why I chose to keep Miller over Larison. I can see Larison making it instead, or even Jennings again, especially after the latter took extensive RB3 reps following his return from the non-football injury list. I like what I’ve seen from Miller, however, so he’s the one I’m keeping in this projection. Fullback In (1): Reggie Gilliam Out: N/A Reggie Gilliam doesn’t have any competition now that Brock Lampe was cut and Jack Westover effectively moved back to tight end, so this is an easy one. The only thing that could prevent him from making the team is if the Patriots prefer keeping an extra tight end and having him play fullback, which seems incredibly unlikely. Wide receiver In (6): A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams Out (6): Efton Chism III, Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon, Nick DeGennaro, Kobe Prentice, Tejhaun Palmer IR (2): Jimmy Kibble, Jeremiah Webb Wide receiver is the position that everyone has been talking about all camp. Will the Patriots keep seven? Will they keep six? Will they trade Kayshon Boutte? Will they trade DeMario Douglas? Will Kyle Williams make the team? All good questions, but the last one in particular was answered pretty emphatically by Mike Vrabel on Friday, so any projection should have Williams on it. As for Douglas and Boutte, they both seem to be a big part of what the Patriots would like to do. It is hard to see their potential trade value outweigh their importance to New England’s receiver group and offensive operation as a whole: Douglas has been the best wide receiver in camp, with Boutte showing consistent chemistry with Drake Maye. As for the final question, I have them keeping only six, with Chism on the outside looking in. He’s shown that he’s clearly better than the second-stringers, and looks like a real NFL player, but there are other positions of need on the team, so I have them only keeping six receivers. Lastly, in regards to the UDFA guys, Cameron Dorner had been coming on in camp but didn’t practice all of last week. I wonder if he maybe ends up on IR and gets another shot next year when there’s possibly less competition at the position. Tight end In (3): Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon, Tanner Arkin Out (3): C.J. Dippre, Jack Westover, Mitch Van Vooren IR (1): Julian Hill Just like the running back position, the top two spots here are locks, but it’s the third one that is up for grabs. Undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin has been the clear TE3 all camp, and has gotten reps at fullback as well; based on his summer so far, he is the clear frontrunner for the final roster spot at the position. C.J. Dippre has just started practicing after getting activated off of PUP, and I thought that he would have a chance to be the third tight end this year. Unfortunately, he has a huge cast on his hand, which makes him unable to catch the ball and in turn unlikely to make the roster from the current point of view. Jack Westover made the team last year, but, if camp is any indication, that won’t be the case this year. Offensive tackle In (4): Will Campbell, Morgan Moses, Caleb Lomu, Marcus Bryant Out (3): James Hudson III , Dametrious Crownover, Lorenz Metz (exempt) The top three tackles are roster locks. The depth is the question here, and I have them keeping Marcus Bryant as OT44. With Will Campbell out last week, Bryant filled in for him at left tackle , and the Patriots seem to like what they have in the second-year player. Hudson has been working at guard to try to make the roster, but he hasn’t looked great. Crownover and Metz seem to have a long way to go to crack an NFL roster, with the latter a candidate to be brought back via the practice squad through this international exemption. Interior offensive line In (5): Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu, Ben Brown, Andrew Rupcich Out (4): Mehki Butler, Caedan Wallace , Jacob Rizy, JonDarius Morgan The depth on the interior hasn’t looked great, which is why the Patriots recently brought in veteran Greg Van Roten for a workout . There’s a chance that he gets signed, and then ends up making the roster as the last guy on this list. Right now, I have Andrew Rupcich because he’s a veteran who Vrabel has experience with. I am somewhat concerned about this position, though, especially considering Vera-Tucker’s injury history, and Ben Brown struggling in camp so far. Hopefully, the starters stay healthy here, because, if the Patriots are forced to rely on their depth — especially for an extended period — they could be in trouble. Defensive tackle In (5): Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden, Joshua Farmer, Isaiah Iton Out (4): Leonard Taylor III, Eric Gregory, Jeremiah Pharms Jr, Casey Rogers This is such a deep position group for the Patriots, and I had a hard time figuring out who to cut. Ultimately, I chose to keep Isaiah Iton as the last guy because I really liked what I saw from him last year and what I have seen from him in camp so far this summer. Leonard Taylor and Casey Rogers seem to have the best chance to take the final spot, but I like the upside of Iton a little bit more, which is why he remains on the team. I also have loved what I’ve seen from Joshua Farmer in camp, and think that the top three — Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden — are going to be incredibly strong. Defensive edge In (6): Dre’Mont Jones, Harold Landry III, Gabe Jacas, Elijah Ponder, Bradyn Swinson, Xavier Holmes Out (2): Quintayvious Hutchins, Jesse Luketa Similar to wide receiver, this also is a group that has a lot of question marks. When will Harold Landry return? Will Gabe Jacas be able to contribute right away? Can Elijah Ponder do what he did at the end of last season for a whole year? While there is a lot of uncertainty, there also is a lot of potential. I love what I’ve seen from Xavier Holmes in camp, and think that he deserves a spot on this projection. He was a camp invite, not even a true UDFA, but he has shown some real flash and has been wreaking havoc on the Patriots backup offensive line. Also, if Bradyn Swinson can live up to his potential as well, the team could end up with a deep group of edge rushers. Of course, there is also a chance that Landry is never quite the same and the young guys can’t live up to their potential, and this group ultimately turns out to be a weakness. Let’s look on the bright side here, though, and be a little more optimistic than that. Linebacker In (4): Robert Spillane, Christian Elliss, Chad Muma, Khalil Jacobs Out (4): K.J. Britt, Namdi Obiazor, Amari…
