title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Under-the-radar players starting to emerge in training camp
summary: The dog days of summer have arrived in Foxborough. The New England Patriots took the practice fields on five straight days between Monday and Friday, including four times in full pads. The rhythm of this year’s training camp is going to change next week, with a joint practice and first game on the schedule. For […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots linebacker Khalil Jacobs (59) participate in drills during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The dog days of summer have arrived in Foxborough. The New England Patriots took the practice fields on five straight days between Monday and Friday, including four times in full pads. The rhythm of this year’s training camp is going to change next week, with a joint practice and first game on the schedule. For now, however, let’s put a wrap on the week that was. Welcome to the latest addition of our Sunday Patriots Notes . Under-the-radar players starting to emerge in training camp Training camp is not just the time for a team to forge its identity before the regular season, it also is an opportunity for players to make a name for themselves regardless of their background. The Patriots have seen multiple of those starting to emerge over the last few days. The obvious one is Tanner Arkin, an undrafted rookie who looks like the Patriots’ best blocking tight end and is on track to making the roster. Other notables are edge defender Xavier Holmes, who has had some flashes of disruptive play, as well as well as cornerbacks Karon Prunty and Channing Canada; both of the rookies are in contention for the fifth and sixth spots on the depth chart. Among the more veteran players, Marcus Bryant emerging as the top backup left tackle was a surprising development considering the presence of first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu. The same can be said for third-year man Terrell Jennings immediately resuming the RB3 role upon his return from the non-football injury list. The most notable development relative to his starting point, however, might belong to Khalil Jacobs. The undrafted rookie, who wasn’t even part of the first wave of signings, appears well-positioned to make the roster as a fourth off-ball linebacker. “He loves football,” said head coach Mike Vrabel about the 22-year-old. “He’s here a lot. He was here in the offseason, through the minicamps, early, staying late. He stays late. I see him here all the time.” Besides his work ethic, Jacobs also caught the eye due to his speed — a topic of discussion going all the way back to his pre-draft visit with the club. “When you get to the team periods, you notice his play speed, and I think that’s a great thing to say,” Vrabel added. “He came here on a visit, and I was trying to just give him a hard time about his 40, and he was like, ‘Oh, that was the timing.’ I’m like, ‘Thirty-two teams timed your 40 wrong?’ Just giving him a hard time. But to his credit, he plays a lot faster than whatever his 40 was. … He has a play speed about him, and sometimes he knows where he’s going, and sometimes he doesn’t, but he still kind of goes pretty quick wherever he decides to go.” For Jacobs, the speed element is important regardless of the 4.77-seconds he posted in the 40-yard dash during the draft process. “The math wasn’t mathing,” he said. “We play football, we’re not track runners. I have tremendous game speed, so I won’t allow 40 times and things like that determine the kind of player I am. … I play extremely fast. Once I see ball, get ball. I try not to think so much, allowing myself to go make plays, and try to make myself be in positions where I can make those plays.” So far this training camp, Jacobs has made his fair share of plays. It has allowed him to establish himself as a fourth linebacker behind Robert Spillane, Christian Elliss and Chad Muma. And if his journey so far is any indication, he is not intent on giving it up. “When my opportunity came, I just made the most of it,” he said. “I didn’t look back.” Upward trajectory Even though he has missed reps due to an apparent left arm injury, Will Campbell was off to a strong start this summer. His teammates noticed it too. “Will has definitely gotten better from the last time I played him last year,” said offseason signing Dre’Mont Jones. “He’s definitely watched a lot of film and honed in his technique even more. It’s fun to watch and it’s fun to compete against him every day.” “He just gets it,” added quarterback Drake Maye. “He gets how to practice, having to come here and show up every day because there are no days off. In practice and in this league, when you’re blocking guys in 1-on-1s, and you’ve got team next, and then we have two-minute. It’s constant, and I think that’s what Will is understanding: how it’s different from college. It’s constant, and you’ve got to train your body and train your mind to be out here each and every day, and treat it like, ‘Man, I’ve got to try to get better today.’ I think he’s learned that really fast, and I think he’s taking it head on, and I’m looking forward to seeing him this year do his thing.” Mike Vrabel indicated on Friday that Campbell should be able to up his workload this coming week. Summer camp vibes When the Patriots drafted teams for their scrimmage on Friday, there were only two rules. The first was that Drake Maye and Jared Wilson had to stay together, an unsurprising decision considering the importance of the quarterback-center relationship. The second was that Mack Hollins and Efton Chism also needed to be on the same team, an unsurprising decision considering the importance of bromance. “It’s unbelievable. You come in there, and they’re in the pool, the rehab pool, and they’re playing like pool games,” said Mike Vrabel about Hollins and Chism. “It’s like summer camp. They’re throwing stuff and got goggles on, and they swim down and pick up things on the bottom of the pool. They study all the time. They work out. They train. They compete. They push each other.” Hollins and Chism both arrived in New England last offseason. The former joined the team as a veteran free agency signing, the latter as an undrafted rookie. “It’s a really cool thing to see,” added Vrabel. “A guy that had been in this league a long time, played with a couple different teams and a kid from Western Washington, a small school, and they come together, and I think they both help each other.” List of 2023 first-round pick extensions keeps growing While the Patriots and Christian Gonzalez still await a conclusion to their own contract extension saga, multiple other 2023 first-round draft picks have signed new deals of their own. Including Titans guard Peter Skoronski, who just signed a reported four-year, $100 million extension before the weekend, the list now looks like this: ED Will Anderson Jr. (1-3): 3 years, $150M RB Bijan Robinson (1-8): 3 years, $66.75M DT Jalen Carter (1-9): 4 years, $152M OT Darnell Wright (1-10): 4 years, $116M (reported) OL Peter Skoronski (1-11): 4 years, $100M (reported) RB Jahmyr Gibbs (1-12): 3 years, $67.5M LB Jack Campbell (1-18): 4 years, $81M WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (1-20): 4 years, $168.6M WR Zay Flowers (1-22): 4 years, $140M What stands out is that none of the four cornerbacks selected in the first round in 2023, including Gonzalez, have been extended. The big name to watch in that regard is Seattle’s Devon Witherspoon, drafted fifth overall. He very well could become the first domino to drop. Versatility is key The competition for the third safety spot is seemingly down to incumbent Dell Pettus and free agency signing Mike Brown, with both getting starer reps throughout the summer. For Pettus, who appears to have taken a slight lead over the last week, the secret to winning is simply being able to do whatever is asked of him. “I’m just trying to continue to be consistent and continue to prove to the staff that I can wear many hats and also do one as equally as the other,” he explained. “Playing safety the same way, playing nickel, dime. Wherever they put me, I’m going to play it to my fullest potential no matter what. I just want them to be able to trust me and build confidence that no matter where they put me at, that I will…

Although Dillon’s injury will keep him off the field this season, there is no doubt his aid and presence will be felt elsewhere.

title: Will the Giants run more or pass more under John Harbaugh?
summary: Sixty-six years as a Giants fan has taught me never to predict anything about my team’s prospects for the upcoming season. When I do, I usually get it wrong. This season, though, with newly installed John Harbaugh at the helm, it’s tempting to predict something about what the team is going to look like on […]
full_text: Lamar Jackson and John Harbaugh before a 2025 pre-season game | Getty Images Sixty-six years as a Giants fan has taught me never to predict anything about my team’s prospects for the upcoming season. When I do, I usually get it wrong. This season, though, with newly installed John Harbaugh at the helm, it’s tempting to predict something about what the team is going to look like on the field in 2026. Headlines like that of Giants Wire’s John Fennelly the other day summed it up: “John Harbaugh’s run-heavy vision has Giants RBs licking their chops.” We all agree on this, right? You don’t bring Patrick Ricard with you from Baltimore if you’re not going to run the ball a lot. You don’t spend the No. 10 pick on a player you intend to put at right guard if you’re not going to run the ball. You don’t hire Greg Roman as a coach if you’re not going to run the ball. League-wide statistics from the 2025 NFL season bear this out. The NFL, thanks in part to rules changes early in the century that benefited offenses and especially quarterbacks and in part to the spread offense that the New England Patriots introduced in the 2007 season and that Tom Brady ran to near perfection, left its 3-yards-and-a-cloud-of-dust heritage in the rear view mirror and became a pass-first league. That has changed a bit in the past few years as defensive masterminds like Vic Fangio have utilized two-high safety looks with post-snap rotation to confuse quarterbacks and limit big passing plays. Still, the NFL remains first and foremost a passing league (data from Pro Football Reference ): Not a single NFL team rushed for more yards than they passed for in the 2025 season. The 2025 Giants under pass-happy Brian Daboll and Mike Kafka were right in the middle of the pack in that respect, with 3474 yards passing vs. only 2195 yards rushing. Harbaugh’s Ravens, though, were closer to the 1:1 line than any other NFL team; only the Jets, who had big quarterback problems last season, came close. So we know what to expect from Harbaugh’s Giants in 2026…or do we? Here is Harbaugh’s season-by-season pass-rush breakdown during his tenure as Ravens head coach: We can see that Harbaugh’s 2025 Ravens pass-rush balance was actually a bit of an outlier relative to his previous history. His first year as Ravens head coach, with rookie Joe Flacco as his QB, had a good pass-run balance, similar to what the Ravens did in 2025. After that, though, as Flacco grew as a QB, the Ravens became a pass-happy offense just like the rest of the NFL did to try to keep up with the Patriots. Flacco was injured and missed the last 6 games of the 2015 season, though, and after one more good season, began to decline, though he has continued to start at least a few games in every season since. In 2018 Baltimore traded back into the first round to draft Lamar Jackson. Jackson started the last seven games but was very limited as a passer while being extremely dangerous as a runner. He was actually the Ravens’ leading rusher for 5 consecutive seasons. You can see the trend of the Ravens becoming an almost equal pass-rush offense in 2018-2020. The last few seasons, though, as Jackson matured as a passer and the front office tried to provide him with weapons, the Ravens once again became a pass-first offense, similar to the Flacco peak seasons. It wasn’t for a lack of talent at running back – Derrick Henry became a Raven in 2024 and rushed for 1,921 yards that season. Jackson himself had seasons of 767, 764, 821, and 915 rushing yards from 2021-2024. Only last season, when Jackson again had injury problems and the offense showed signs of aging, did the Ravens show a pass-rush balance similar to Jackson’s early years. So will the Giants run more this season because Harbaugh is the head coach? Based on the chart above, it’s not obvious. It probably depends more on whether Jaxson Dart further develops as a passer and whether the Giants’ offensive line becomes better at run blocking than on any perceived preference by Harbaugh for the run over the pass.
author: Anthony Del Genio

title: Ed’s excellent West Virginia adventure: A different way of life
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants’ time at The Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia is over. So is mine. This was an amazing trip in many ways to a beautiful part of the country where life is much different than it is in New York or New Jersey. Yes, that includes upstate […]
full_text: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants’ time at The Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia is over. So is mine. This was an amazing trip in many ways to a beautiful part of the country where life is much different than it is in New York or New Jersey. Yes, that includes upstate New York, where I reside. I hope this post gives a little flavor of the trip. I will try to touch on what the area is like, what training camp itself offered, The Greenbrier, the experience for myself and other media members, and more. I hope you enjoy this stroll through my ‘excellent West Virginia adventure’. Monday, July 27 The truth of this story is that it begins long before I hopped in the car to make the 586-mile, 10-hour drive to the cottage I had rented in Covington, Va., about 14 miles outside of White Sulpher Springs. My trip to The Greenbrier was approved back in March. I knew I was going to drive from my upstate New York home to West Virginia, and knew my beloved 2014 Honda Pilot — with 190,000 miles on it — was not the right vehicle for the trip. As much as I did not want to, I parted with the Pilot and purchased a 2023 Subaru Ascent with less than 25,000 miles on the odometer. I put more than 1,600 miles on the Ascent during the trip, so that was a good decision. The 586-mile drive from my home to Covington was uneventful. Not like the storm-filled drive several of my media cohorts had on Tuesday. Or, my interesting drive home. Not in New York anymore This is a lesson I learned shortly after arriving at my home away from home for 12 days. It was between 6 and 7 p.m. ET, and I was hungry. I really wanted to settle in, and get a bit of work done. I did not want to drive all over the place looking for food in an unfamiliar, remote, place. So, what does a Northeasterner do? Order delivery. Only, I first had to find a place that would deliver. That by itself wasn’t simple. I ended up ordering pizza from a nearby Domino’s, only to receive a call back that I would have to meet the driver at a store a few miles down the road because I was outside the delivery zone. Welcome to remote Virginia! Tuesday, July 28 One of the benefits of being on site a day early, or what I hoped would be a benefit, was the potential to play tourist for a day. The city of Lewisburg was said to be the best place to walk around and shop, so that afternon I jumped in my car and made the roughly 22-mile drive in an effort to check it out. Problem was, the weather decided not to cooperate. The further I drove the more my GPS was issuing warnings of severe storms that might render some of the roads impassable. By the time I got to downtown Lewisburg, which looked like a quaint town that would be fun to walk around, the sky was incredibly dark and the volume of warnings had increased. I drove through, turned around, and went back to Covington. Of course, by the time I got there the storms had passed and the weather was good for the remainder of the day. So, that was strikeout number one in Lewisburg. Wednesday, July 29 I like to be early for things. I’m the guy who will sit in the airport for 2½ hours waiting for a flight. I feel like I am late if I don’t reach the press box three hours before a Giants game. We had been told that we would not be able to access the Sports Performance Center until two hours before practice. So, of course I showed up for Wednesday’s opening practice, scheduled for 1:30 p.m., at 11:05. I was told to leave and drive around White Sulphur Springs until 11:30. So, yeah, they were serious about the two-hour rule. Choo, choo! One of the annoying things about the Quest Diagnostics Training Center has always been that most pre- and post-practice pressers are held outside, with planes from Teterboro Airport flying overhead and making it difficult to hear. Well, having a railroad train chug just below the podium where you are trying to do an interview is not easy, either. Cool to watch, not fun to work through. I will miss watching the train chug by the Greenbrier Sports Performance Center practice field. One of the area's unique experiences. — Ed Valentine (@edvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-08-09T12:26:09.433Z Thursday, July 30 Hi, guys! I was hoping to meet a few BBV readers at practices open to fans. Larry Jamieson and ‘Pataroons’ introduced themselves in Thursday. I think it was the next day I met ‘Tiki’sBarber.‘ If you made it to The Greenbrier for any of the practices, I hope you enjoyed it. I did a few ‘In-5 trivia’ videos with fans while in West Virginia. I hope you enjoyed them. I was, honestly, a bit taken aback by fans’ inability to identify Jeff Hostetler. View this post on Instagram A different kind of dinner Life moves at a different, slower, pace in West Virginia than in the New Yorl/New Jersey area. An outdoor dinner with Steve Serby of the New York Post and Evan Barnes of Newsday at a restaurant called Max on Main proved that. One of my two sons works as a restaurant manager in the Albany area. He has told me that when they give wait times to customers, they usually project a longer time than they expect. In other words, if they expect 10 minutes they will tell customers 15. On this gorgeous evening, we discovered that 15 minutes has a different meaning in West Virginia. We were told 15 minutes, not because the place was full but because of that night’s staffing. Well, 15 minutes was really about an hour. We seated ourselves, and eventually had to run down our own waitress and insist on at least getting menus and placing drink orders. The food was good. The weather was great. The company was entertaining. The service? That was on its own schedule. Just remember that if you go out to eat in West Virginia, don’t be surprised if you are there for a while. Technologically impaired There was a time when I managed a newspaper’s computer network, and wrote a technology column. That was a long time ago. This was a tough day for me when it came to technology. First, I thought I had a great video of Malik Nabers working through drills, only to discover that I had my phone set on “photo” and didn’t take any video at all. Then, after practice I posted a recap video to YouTube without any sound. Apparently, the microphone needs to be on. Sheesh! Friday, July 31 Slammin’ Sammy’s As a ‘thank-you’ to media members who made the trip to West Virginia, the Giants — mostly the PR staff — hosted us for dinner Friday evening at ‘Slammin Sammy’s,‘ one of the many restaurants on The Greenbrier grounds. Since I drove my own car to West Virginia, I brought one set of dress clothes with me — even if I did forget the shoes! Pretty much everywhere you go around The Greenbrier, there is a strictly-adhered to dress code. While I was prepared, even without the dress shoes, some of my cohorts were not. One even had to find a Wal-Mart and buy a collared shirt before dinner. This was a fun event. GM Joe Schoen showed up, and we chatted for a bit. Dawn Aponte, senior VP of football operations and strategy, was also there. This was the first time most of us had met her. Saturday, August 1 Gustard’s Bistro in White Sulphur Springs is the one “must-eat” place not on the grounds of The Greenbrier itself that had been recommended to me. Apparently, others had been told the same. Saturday evening, Serby, Stapleton, Barnes, Charlotte Carroll of The Athletic, Steve Whyno of the Associated Press, Ryan Duynleavy of the New York Post, and I ended up in a private room at Gustard’s for a fantastic, fun meal. Good enough that I went back on my final night in West Virginia. Between the end of practice and the time of our dinner reservation, there were a couple of hours to kill. I parked in downtown White Sulphur Springs, walked around The Greenbrier property for a while, then went inside, took pictures, and had a pre-dinner ice cream at Draper’s in the resort. Below, some of the photos I took. Apologies in advance for the scary selfie! Sunday, August 2 Souvenirs? What souvenirs? This was the only off day…

title: NY Giants 53-man roster projection, Week 2 update: Locks, bubble players, long shots
summary: How much did the New York Giants time in West Virginia change the team’s potential season-opening roster? Let’s take a look. Below is an updated position-by-position look at who I consider to be locks to make the 53-man roster, bubble players, and long shots after the first two weeks of practice. The intent is to […]
full_text: Will Braxton Berrios (87) make the 53-man roster? | Getty Images How much did the New York Giants time in West Virginia change the team’s potential season-opening roster? Let’s take a look. Below is an updated position-by-position look at who I consider to be locks to make the 53-man roster, bubble players, and long shots after the first two weeks of practice. The intent is to look at where the most interesting competitions are, and the chances of individual players. Quarterback Locks (2) — Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston Bubble players (0) — None Long shot (1) — Brandon Allen [No change] I would think we will see a lot of Allen in Saturday’s preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings. Running back Locks (4) — Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary, Patrick Ricard Bubble players (1) — Dante Miller Long shots (2) — Eric Gray, Damon Bankston, Grant Finley (FB) [ Change: Finley added to roster] When the Giants have monitored Skattebo’s reps, it has been Miller who has benefitted by getting chances to work with Dart. I still don’t think Miller makes the team, but right now he would be RB4 with Ricard as a fullback/blocking tight end. Tight end Locks (3) — Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson, Chris Manhertz Bubble players (1) — Tanner Conner Long shot (1) — Thomas Fidone [No change] Conner, formerly with the Miami Dolphins, has made plenty of plays this summer. I don’t see, though, how he knocks Manhertz off the roster. Unless the Giants are willing to use Patrick Ricard regularly as an inline tight end. Wide receiver Locks (5) — Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields Bubble players (5) — Odell Beckham Jr., JuJu Smith-Schuster, Braxton Berrios, Dalen Cambre, Jalin Hyatt Long shots (3) — Ryan Miller, Xavier Gipson, Isaiah Hodgins [ Changes: Beaux Collins cut; Jalin Hyatt moved from long shot to bubble] Hyatt has made a career of flashing during training camp, and he is doing it again. Interestingly, the Giants are taking a look at Hyatt as a potential punt gunner. He has the speed for it. Does he have the physicality to get off blocks, especially double teams, and the willingness/ability to tackle? Those are questions we don’t have the answer to. One player who has gotten little attention in camp is Mooney, the veteran receiver signed in free agency during the offseason. I have even heard speculation that Mooney, who has $3 million in guaranteed money, could be on the roster bubble. After what I watched during the week of padded practices in West Virginia, and heard from players, I am not buying. Mooney has consistently repped with Dart. During Friday’s practice, Mooney caught several passes. One was an impressive 15-yard, top-tapping, deep out during the full-field drive at the end of practice. That same day, Mooney smoked Paulson Adebo for a deep sideline catch during 7-on-7 work. One of my favorite questions to ask new, veteran Giants is which player or players they knew nothing about they have been impressed by. When I had a chance to speak with defensive back Ar’Darius Washington, I put the question to him. “I knew Mooney was nice,” Washington said. “I knew he was good. But I didn’t know he was that good.” Anything can happen, but I have a hard time believing Mooney won’t be part of the 53-man roster. Offensive line Locks (7) — Andrew Thomas, Jon Runyan, John Michael Schmitz, Francis Mauigoa, Jermaine Eluemunor, Marcus Mbow, Daniel Faalele Bubble players (5) — J.C. Davis, Lucas Patrick, Bryan Hudson, Josh Ezeudu, Aaron Stinnie Long shots (5) — Evan Neal, Ryan Schernecke, Jake Kubas, Jarrod Gray (International Exemption), Brendan Jaimes [ Change: Jaimes added to roster] Patrick is making the team as the backup center … if he is healthy. The Giants have been managing the veteran lineman’s snaps. If he isn’t healthy, maybe that opens the door for Hudson … or even Kubas, who has worked at center in the past. Defensive line Locks (4) — D.J. Reader, Darius Alexander, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston Bubble players (5) — Bobby Jamison-Travis, Leki Fotu, Zacch Pickens, Sam Roberts, Josh Tupou Long shots (2) — Anquin Barnes Jr., Marlon Davidson [No change] If I had to guess right now, I would say Jamison-Travis and Fotu make the roster. That, though, is purely a guess. Off-ball linebacker Locks (4) — Arvell Reese, Tremaine Edmunds, Micah McFadden, Jack Kelly Bubble players (2) — Darius Muasau, Zaire Barnes Long shots (1) — Anfernee Orji [ Change: Kelly moved from bubble to lock] Kelly, one of the Giants’ three sixth-round picks, has been impressive going both forward and backward. He aligns next to McFadden with the second team during every practice. I will be very surprised if he is not on the season-opening roster. Edge defender Locks (3) — Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux Bubble players (1) — Khalid Kareem Long shots (2) — Trace Ford, Caleb Murphy [No change] I still see only the three edge defenders making the 53-man roster. Cornerback Locks (5) — Paulson Adebo, Greg Newsome II, Colton Hood, Dru Phillips, Deonte Banks Bubble players (3) — Art Green, Nic Jones, Korie Black Long shots (2) — David Long, D.J. James [ Change: Long, James added to roster; Jarrick Bernard-Converse waived/injured] The Giants are a little thin at cornerback right now, even after signing Long and James. Dru Phillips’ knee injury is said to be minor, but the Giants might still need to add one more player here. As for the competition for starting spots at cornerback, scoff at the idea Deonte Banks could be a starter if you want … but he could be a starter. He has been getting considerable snaps with the first team, and is legitimately in competition with Greg Newsome and Colton Hood. Newsome even said a few days ago that Banks has been “amazing” this summer. As a side note, Adebo took some second-team reps late in the week. I’m not sure how much significance to attach to that. As I said recently on New York Post Sports Plus , though, John Harbaugh is not going to be beholden to players who were here when he was hired. I still think Adebo is a starter, but his second-team work was noteworthy after he had struggled the previous day. Safety Locks (3) — Jevon Holland, Tyler Nubin, Ar’Darius Washington Bubble players (2) — Elijah Campbell, Jason Pinnock Long shots (2) — Beau Brade, Raheem Layne [No change] The more I watch practice, the more I believe Washington is going to play a lot. Also, I am not ready to do it yet, but I might have to put Pinnock in the “lock” category. It is important to remember how well Pinnock played for the Giants in Wink Martindale’s defense, and that Dennard Wilson will ask defensive backs to play aggressively. That suits Pinnock. Special teams Locks (1) — Jordan Stout (punter) Bubble players (2) — Dominic Zvada (placekicker), Ben Mann (long-snapper) Long shot (1) — Ben Sauls (placekicker) [No change] Mann had the first off-target snap I have seen from him all spring and summer on Friday, with a high snap contributing to a 45-yard miss by Sauls. Totals Locks: 41 Bubble players: 27 Long shots: 23 NOTE: The Giants have 91 players since they are carrying one player (Gray) with an International Exemption

title: Eagles work out 3 free agents
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles hosted three free agents on visits at the Jefferson Health Training Complex earlier today, according to the NFL’s official personnel notice. The names: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. DAVID BLAY First of all, big fan of this guy’s street magic. Blay, 23, has some local ties. He attended […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - MAY 09: Ja'Quinden Jackson #38 of the Jacksonville Jaguars goes through workout drills during Rookie Mini Camp at Miller Electric Center on May 9, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles hosted three free agents on visits at the Jefferson Health Training Complex earlier today, according to the NFL’s official personnel notice. The names: DT David Blay RB Ja’Quinden Jackson EDGE Tarron Jackson Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. DAVID BLAY First of all, big fan of this guy’s street magic . Blay, 23, has some local ties. He attended Harry S Truman High School in Levittown, Pennsylvania (shout out Bucks County) before initially enrolling at West Chester from 2021-2022. Blay then transferred to Louisiana for 2023-2024 and then again to The U in 2025. Blay did not get selected in the 2026 NFL Draft; he signed with the New England Patriots as an undrafted rookie free agent. But then the Pats waived him on August 7. Here’s a pre-draft scouting report on the 6’2”, 292 pounder: Blay is a slightly undersized nose tackle who climbed from Division II to Conference USA and finally to Miami, where he played for a national title. He takes on single blocks with adequate power to press and separate, but he can be wiped out by double-teams or angle pressure. He’s quick to close the distance on quarterbacks when he gets some breathing room but lacks early explosion and hand work to quickly open doors. Blay’s path to a roster might come as an undrafted free agent. And here’s what Pats Pulpit recently had to say about Blay: […] given that he did not make any noticeable contributions in training camp so far, the writing very much remained on the wall. The Eagles could be looking at Blay for the sake of more defensive tackle depth ahead of their first preseason game, which takes place in less than a week (August 15). JA’QUINDEN JACKSON Jackson, who turns 25 next month, finished his college football career at Arkansas before joining the Jacksonville Jaguars as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2025. The Jags kept him on their practice squad last season but then waived him back in May. With both Dameon Pierce and Elijah Mitchell leaving practice early on Saturday , the Eagles seemingly have interest in adding more running back depth, which makes sense. They could use the extra body for practice and preseason reps. Pre-drafting scouting report : A big back with an imposing frame, Jackson is a one-speed runner lacking burst and juice in the open field. He reacts to traffic once he gets into the run but isn’t proactive enough in his early reads to set up linebackers and unlock the lane. He’s too slow getting in and out of cuts, allowing defenses to rally and tackle quickly. He plays with adequate lane choice and can add yards after contact with his size and leg drive. Jackson’s size and strength will appeal to teams but a lack of functional speed and third-down value limit his ceiling. His spider graph reveals he’s a big back with long arms: TARRON JACKSON Oh, hey! Here’s someone we know. The Eagles originally selected Jackson with a sixth-round pick (No. 191 overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft. He appeared in 22 games with Philly from 2021-2023 until the Birds cut him in August 2024. Jackson then spent a brief stint with the Carolina Panthers before returning to the Eagles in November. But then they cut him again a month later, so, he wasn’t actually with the team when they won Super Bowl LIX. Tough. Jackson signed with the San Francisco 49ers in 2025 but suffered a neck injury that ended his season in late July. Now presumably healthy again, Jackson could have a third stint in Philly.

title: Eagles 53-man roster prediction: Training camp updates
summary: There’s no Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice today; players have off for just the second time since the summer sessions began on July 29. Now that we have a break in the action after watching eight practices, it feels like a good time to take stock of the team in the form of an updated […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Darius Cooper #80 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There’s no Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice today; players have off for just the second time since the summer sessions began on July 29. Now that we have a break in the action after watching eight practices, it feels like a good time to take stock of the team in the form of an updated 53-man roster prediction. We’ll continue to issue updated projections as we learn more from practices (including two upcoming joint days with A.J. Brown’s New England Patriots) and three preseason games. ( To see how things have changed, take a look at my last 53-man roster projection from 11 days ago .) OFFENSE QUARTERBACK: Jalen Hurts, Andy Dalton, Cole Payton (3) [3] Hurts has had an encouraging camp; he really seems to be embracing the new offensive direction under Sean Mannion. The QB2 battle is very much ongoing based on how the Eagles are rotating Dalton and Tanner McKee with the second-team offense. Dalton has been the better player since camp began but McKee previously outshined him in spring practices … so, it’s a close call. We could see some more separation in the preseason games. For now, I’ll say the Eagles trade McKee to a team that’s desperate for quarterback help, whether that’s needing a backup or otherwise. Dalton’s lacking arm strength is concerning but he does look comfortable in the offense. Payton has thrown a lot of interceptions in training camp but he’s shown enough promise to deter the Eagles from exposing him to waivers. RUNNING BACK (3): Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley (3) [6] Barkley looks as good as ever. Bigsby’s had an awesome offseason; the Eagles absolutely must find a way to get him more involved than he was last year . Shipley should be in danger based on merit but I tend to think the coaching staff will value him more than fans do. Dameon Pierce has flashed as both a runner, pass-catcher, and kick returner. He might be able to push for the RB3 role, assuming the injury he suffered on Saturday isn’t serious. Pierce has shown enough to at least make the practice squad. Elijah Mitchell and Carson Steele haven’t looked bad but they’re both fighting an uphill battle. Then again, the Eagles did keep four running backs for a good portion of last year (Barkley, Bigsby, Shipley, and AJ Dillon). WIDE RECEIVER: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Johnny Wilson (6) [12] Smitty has missed most of training camp with a hamstring injury but he looked good as ever prior to getting hurt. Zero concerns with him. Smith’s absence has opened up more opportunities for Wicks, who has fully taken advantage of them by making a lot of catches. It’s clear that Hurts trusts Wicks, which is huge. Cooper makes plays every day. He’s already done enough to make the roster. The question is: will he actually get playing time? He deserves it. Lemon’s had a disappointing offseason; the 2026 first-round pick missed at least four of the Eagles’ eight spring practices and he’s missed five of their eight training camp practices so far. Even prior to getting hurt, Lemon wasn’t doing much to impress. It’s just hard to know what to expect from him at the moment. Brown has been outshined by others … but the Eagles gave him $5 million guaranteed, which impacted their compensatory pick formula. So, it’s not ea sy to see them cutting him. Maybe they can move off Hollywood in a trade? Wilson has had a good camp as a pass-catcher and he obviously brings value to the table as a big blocking receiver. Elijah Moore was a really tough cut here; he deserves to make the team and he’s been getting first-team reps. But he also doesn’t have special teams experience (19 career snaps there) and he’s not subject to waivers. Maybe the Eagles can get him to agree to be on the practice squad early in the season before eventually adding him to the roster once a spot frees up. Britain Covey saw a lot of targets early in camp but he’s been dealing with a hamstring injury and the team can probably keep him on the practice squad if they want him to be in the punt returner mix. Quez Watkins is also in practice squad contention. TIGHT END: Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Cam Latu, Eli Stowers (4) [16] Goedert’s had a solid-to-good camp. Mundt is clearly TE2; he’s the second tight end in the Eagles’ 12 personnel sets. Latu is a stud special teams player and he can block. Stowers had his best two days recently … but it was a very low bar to clear since he’s had a quiet offseason. I tend to think the rookie tight end is in jeopardy of being a healthy scratch, at least early in the year. E.J. Jenkins is on the bubble here, probably a good bet to make the practice squad. Still think Dae’Quan Wright might come alive in the preseason games. OFFENSIVE LINE: Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin, Myles Hinton, Cameron Williams, Micah Morris (11) [27] The starters are in place. The Eagles have been load managing Dickerson and Jurgens left practice early the past two days, so, that’s something to monitor. Johnson returned to the team after some time away and announced he’s probably going to retire after the 2026 season . The backup situation here feels fluid. Bell is taking the bulk of first-team right tackle reps when Johnson isn’t in there. It seems like he could beat out Fred Johnson, who I left off this list. Big Fred obviously brings a lot of experience to the table … but he hasn’t had a good summer. Maybe the Eagles can trade him for a small return. Kendall is contending to be the Eagles’ top interior backup offensive lineman. Lampkin is small but mighty; he’s making his case to be on the roster to give the Eagles even more interior depth. Hinton, Williams, and Morris are hardly locks to stick around but the Eagles could look to retain their young developmental options with Lane heading out the door and Dickerson’s long-term outlook up in the air. John Ojukwu is a sleeper option to make the team. Jake Majors gets a lot of reps but he hasn’t looked good. DEFENSE EDGE DEFENDER: Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith , Arnold Ebiketie, A.J. Epenesa (5) [32] Greenard is expected to be activated from the active/PUP list in time to play in Week 1. Not ideal that he’s missing a big portion of camp but he could still have a good season, assuming his pectoral strain is not a lingering injury. Hunt’s had a very strong camp; he looks poised to make another big developmental leap in Year 3. Vic Fangio noted that Smith entered the Eagles’ offseason program heavier than they wanted him to be but he’s back down to his proper weight now. Smith hasn’t had a bad camp but he’s not had the same kind of summer than Hunt has had. Ebiketie and Epenesa have both flashed enough to lead one to believe they’ll be quality rotational edge rushers. Doesn’t seem like bringing Brandon Graham back is in the cards. Keyshawn James-Newby has missed time due to injury. Joshua Weru has shown some intriguing movement skills but the undrafted rookie who’s never played in a football game before clearly isn’t ready to play in 2026. DEFENSIVE TACKLE: Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young, Ty Robinson (5) [37] Carter looks poised for a monster year; he’s been dominant in camp after getting paid. Davis also looks like he’s ready to be really productive in 2026. Ojomo is on the Milton Williams trajectory in terms of balling out this season before getting a big contract from another team in free agency (March 2027). Fangio likes Young and he’s been the best defensive tackle outside of the top three. I like Gabe Hall more than Robinson but I’m not sure that Howie Roseman is ready to cut bait…

title: Philadelphia Eagles 2026 schedule and scores

title: Eagles News: Willie Lampkin impressing teammates as he pushes for a roster spot
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … This undersized ‘beast’ is pushing to make the Eagles’ roster – NJ.com The Eagles’ smallest offensive lineman is making a big impression during training camp. And he’s pushing for a spot on the 53-man roster, too. Willie Lampkin, the 5-foot-11 interior offensive lineman, has been one […]
full_text: Jun 9, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles center Willie Lampkin (61) and guard Micah Morris (76) drill during minicamp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … This undersized ‘beast’ is pushing to make the Eagles’ roster – NJ.com The Eagles’ smallest offensive lineman is making a big impression during training camp. And he’s pushing for a spot on the 53-man roster, too. Willie Lampkin, the 5-foot-11 interior offensive lineman, has been one of the standouts through seven camp practices. The second-year pro has been turning heads (and moving bodies) at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. And the work that the 290-pounder has put in has been impossible to miss. “Willie’s been killing it,” rookie quarterback Cole Payton said. “Every day we have a team meeting after practice, and there’s always ‘good effort’ clips. Willie’s always on the ‘good effort’ clips. He’s playing his ass off, and I’m super happy for him.” “Willie’s a beast,” interior offensive lineman Drew Kendall added. “He’s had a great camp.” Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: A ton of observations from the longest practice of the summer – BGN Lampkin notably took reps at second-team right guard in addition to third-team center. The Eagles seem to be taking a long look at him, as they should be. I think Lampkin is going to crush the preseason and win a roster spot, small stature be damned. Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 8: Jalyx Hunt is a beast – PhillyVoice The catch of the day was made by… oh hey… Darius Cooper again. Cooper was running toward the sideline, and when he ran out of real estate, he planted both feet on the ground and made a catch while falling to the ground. Great catch. He is clearly going to make the team, and I’m beginning to wonder if he might be the WR3. Eagles practice observations: Lane Johnson’s heir apparent; Jihaad Campbell pops; Moro Ojomo’s pressures – Inquirer Jihaad Campbell popped off the screen in the early portion of the scrimmage. The linebacker completely knocked Jurgens on his rear on an early run play. Later, Campbell fended off Steen at the second level and touched up running back Saquon Barkley. On the next play, he two-hand touched tight end Dallas Goedert after a sliding catch. I counted three more run plays in which Campbell was involved during the set. He did get washed out by Jurgens at one point. And in the “backed-up” period, he hesitated on a run blitz, and Barkley simply cut to the left and ran through the vacated gap. Zack Baun was equally impressive. He made the stop on Barkley’s first tote. He often teamed up with Campbell on other run stops. Baun also intercepted quarterback Jalen Hurts on a deflected pass in a two-minute drill. He correctly anticipated a later throw and nearly had another pick, but receiver Elijah Moore somehow escaped with the catch. Eagles star Lane Johnson deserves the farewell tour he’s about to embark on – The Athletic Lane Johnson announced to the world that 2026 is “probably” the final season of his storied career, and one of his closest confidants announced to the world a long-held belief within the locker room and team facility for the past decade. “Best tackle in the NFL,” Dom DiSandro, security chief and senior adviser to the general manager, uttered while Johnson walked by, and that view is part of why Saturday was so significant and the next six months so meaningful. The unscheduled announcement came after Johnson was excused for six days for a personal reason. It mattered that it came at all. He could have played out this season with the question lingering, as they did last year. The franchise knows how to throw a spring retirement ceremony; they’ve done it for franchise icons such as Jason Kelce (who watched from the back as Johnson spoke Saturday), Brandon Graham and Fletcher Cox. By declaring his plans on a sweltering August Saturday morning, however, Johnson allowed for the type of farewell tour he deserves. Cole Payton not lacking for confidence despite training camp INTs – NBCSP Cole Payton isn’t afraid to let it rip. The Eagles’ fifth-round quarterback out of North Dakota State has a live arm and the confidence to try some throws on the practice field … even when he probably shouldn’t. “I’ve got a lot of confidence in throwing the football,” Payton said. “But in the NFL, these windows are a lot tighter and so I’ve got to take care of the football. I’ve thrown a few picks. But there’s that balance of knowing when to strike and knowing when to take the check-downs. Going through those growing pains but taking the ups and the downs.” Through eight training camp practices, Payton has shown some encouraging signs, but he has also thrown five interceptions despite a limited workload. Why Fresh Start For Elijah Moore With Eagles May Lead To Roster Spot – SI The idea that the NFL is a meritocracy ignores some rather obvious exceptions like pedigree and money. As the 34th overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, Eagles’ receiver Elijah Moore was once on the right side of the personnel equation. Set to enter Year 6 of his NFL career after signing a one-year contract with Philadelphia in March, Moore, 26, is now swimming upstream against projection and larger contracts in an effort to make the 33-man roster. Through seven practices this summer, Moore has unquestionably been one of the better Eagles’ receivers, but the odds remain against the Ole Miss product. Fantasy Football ‘Do Not Draft’ list: Giants’ young trio among players being overvalued – ESPN On an offense that struggled at times, especially in throwing downfield, Eagles starter Dallas Goedert caught 11 of the team’s 26 TD throws. The 31-year-old caught 12 touchdowns during the prior four seasons combined, with some of that time lost to injuries. That’s another point. Goedert isn’t durable, and he likely isn’t coming close to double-digit TDs again. Spadaro: Tank Bigsby is ready for whatever opportunities come his way – PhiladelphiaEagles.com More than anything, when you are watching Tank Bigsby on the football field, you see the energy. You see the all-out, not-gonna-stop, relentlessness. You see the fun he’s having. “I just enjoy every opportunity I have out there,” said Bigsby, part of a loaded Eagles running back room in his second season and first Training Camp in Philadelphia. “That’s just the way I am. Go out there and do something you love to do. Every opportunity, it’s like you’ve just got to take advantage of it, like it’s your last opportunity. You can’t play around with it, you know what I’m saying? But at the end of the day, you just got to go out there and have fun, and that’s what I lean on.” As much as Bigsby loves the game, the game loves him right back. He embraces physicality, steps up to all the challenges, enjoys the nuances that separate players at the highest levels. Cowboys fans expect big things from Caleb Downs this year – Blogging The Boys Is it possible we’re hyping Caleb Downs up too much? It is a legitimate question considering how absolutely giddy Dallas Cowboys fans have been about getting Downs in the draft. It felt mostly like a pipe dream before the draft, but now we are living in the reality. Downs has been called the best defensive player in the draft, one of the highest football IQ rookies in a long time, and various other accolades, even the lofty ‘generational player’. That’s a lot to heap upon a rookie. But we’re going to heap some more. We asked you where Downs would end up in the Defensive Rookie of the Year vote at the end of 2026. A majority of Cowboys fans (53%) think he will outright win it! Another 25% thought he would finish somewhere between third and fifth. title: Aaron Rodgers’ advice to Drew Allar already paying off
summary: It’s been an explosive first training camp for Pittsburgh Steelers rookie quarterback Drew Allar. The Penn State product has routinely made throws that raise the eyebrows of media and coaches alike over the course of the last two weeks, and he unleashed a pair of deep throws during Saturday’s annual night practice at Latrobe Memorial. […]
full_text: Jun 9, 2026; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Drew Allar (16) participates in drills during Minicamp at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s been an explosive first training camp for Pittsburgh Steelers rookie quarterback Drew Allar. The Penn State product has routinely made throws that raise the eyebrows of media and coaches alike over the course of the last two weeks, and he unleashed a pair of deep throws during Saturday’s annual night practice at Latrobe Memorial. Allar spoke to the media after practice and was asked about fine-tuning the touch on his deep ball, to which he credited help from Aaron Rodgers. “It felt really good [to let loose on deep balls],” Allar said via Brendan Howe . “It’s been something I’m working on in terms of the trajectory to the throw. I kind of picked Aaron’s brain on it like a week ago. So to be able to finally get the chance to do it in a live setting… against live DBs in tight coverage felt really good.” This past Thursday, I asked head coach Mike McCarthy about Allar’s progression from rookie minicamp up until now. “He’s doing what you want from a young player,” McCarthy said . “These are tough practices because you’re not just repeating concepts… there hasn’t been a day where he hasn’t made a throw that makes you say, ‘Okay, that’s a young man taking a step.‘” Offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio echoed those sentiments. “Been impressed,” Angelichio told the media. “His poise, his ability to retain information. When you correct him on something, his ability to immediately go back in there and get it right – that’s important. He’s like a sponge in that QB room.” Allar and the Steelers will take the field for the first time in live-game action this Thursday when Pittsburgh hosts the Green Bay Packers. full_text: May 4, 2021; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth (88) practices at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex during rookie minicamp, Friday, May 14, 2021 in Pittsburgh, PA. Mandatory Credit: Karl Roster/Handout Photo via USA TODAY Sports The Steelers are looking to find even more ways to utilize tight end Pat Freiermuth. Offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio said the Steelers will continue to “push the envelope” with Freiermuth’s usage, especially when the coaching staff recognizes opportunities to isolate him one-on-one against opposing defenders. “Pat’s done a great job of controlling the middle of the field,” Angelichio said. Steelers OC Brian Angelichio says they'll keep 'pushing the envelope' with Pat Freiermuth's usage in the MOF, especially when they see him in a one-on-one. "Pat's done a great job of controlling the middle of the field." — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) August 8, 2026 Freiermuth has established himself as one of Pittsburgh’s most reliable receiving options since entering the NFL, and the Steelers appear intent on taking advantage of his combination of size, hands and route-running ability. His presence in the middle can create matchup problems against linebackers while also forcing safeties to account for him, potentially opening opportunities elsewhere in the passing game. Last year he only hauled in 41 passes for 486 yards, as former OC Arthur Smith seemed to favor both Jonnu Smith and Darnell Washington. That versatility could become increasingly important as the Steelers look to develop a more aggressive and diverse offensive attack under Mike McCarthy. Freiermuth has also shown the ability to contribute in multiple areas, making him difficult for defenses to ignore. If Pittsburgh can consistently create isolated opportunities for him between the numbers, he could become an even bigger component of the passing game. Angelichio’s comments suggest the Steelers aren’t satisfied with simply maintaining Freiermuth’s existing role. They want to keep expanding it—and make opposing defenses pay when they leave him alone in the middle of the field. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers training camp: DK Metcalf circus catch highlights Saturday night lights
summary: LATROBE – A crowd of 8,499 Steelers fans packed Latrobe Memorial Stadium to welcome the Pittsburgh Steelers on one of the most unique training camp traditions in the National Football League. The practice gave us no shortage of fireworks and big plays all around. Here are the biggest takeaways from the Steelers’ ninth training camp […]
full_text: Jul 25, 2025; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf (4) participates in drills during training camp at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE – A crowd of 8,499 Steelers fans packed Latrobe Memorial Stadium to welcome the Pittsburgh Steelers on one of the most unique training camp traditions in the National Football League. The practice gave us no shortage of fireworks and big plays all around. Here are the biggest takeaways from the Steelers’ ninth training camp practice of 2026. DK Metcalf makes the catch of camp During team period, Rodgers looked through his progressions for a moment before firing a ball down the right sideline. DK Metcalf was running down the field, but Asante Samuel Jr., who is having arguably the best camp of any player on the Steelers, was running stride for stride with him. It was great coverage by Samuel Jr., but a perfectly placed ball by Rodgers. Metcalf juggled with Samuel for a moment, but as they both fell to the ground, Metcalf came down with it with one hand. The play got a huge rise from the crowd and was arguably the best catch we have seen all camp. Rodgers and Metcalf seem to be more in rhythm this season, and that can only bode well for the Steelers offense. Have a day, Broderick Jones It was a shock to many that offensive tackle Broderick Jones was cleared in time to participate in training camp. After a few weeks of practice, Jones looks to be making serious strides after putting together a great practice today. In one-on-one blocking drills, Jones had a rep where he knocked freshly extended edge rusher Nick Herbig on his backside immediately. Jones was listed as the backup left tackle on the team’s initial depth chart. He will be a player to watch throughout camp to see how he is continuing to progress from his injury and earn a role on the team. Jamel Dean’s pick-six During seven-on-seven, Aaron Rodgers stepped back for his first throw of practice with a defense in front of him and was targeting Roman Wilson on an out route. The throw seemed to be a bit behind Wilson, leading to it being jumped and intercepted by Jamel Dean. Dean then took the interception all the way to the other end zone for what would have been a pick-six in a game. Dean has been thrusted into being the teams top corner in camp with Joey Porter Jr. and Jalen Ramsey both still on the physically unable to perform list. It was a huge play for Dean, who figures to be a key piece on the Steelers defense this season. The Drew Allar experience is real The project that is Drew Allar showed some flashes tonight. First was a downfield throw along the sideline to tight end Robert Tonyan. Allar hit Tonyan in stride for what would have been a 50-yard touchdown. The very next play, Allar uncorked a ball downfield as wide receiver Brandon Smith made a diving catch on the goal line. Allar displayed his ability not only to push the ball down the field, but to do it consistently in 11-on-11 situations. Allar also had issues with his short accuracy tonight and seemed to be unsettled when under pressure. I have seen more “wow” throws from Allar than any other Steelers QB this camp short of perhaps Aaron Rodgers, but the simple stuff is still very much a work in progress. Other notes: WR Michael Pittman Jr. left practice after being seen with a trainer looking at his left leg. Keep an eye out for any update on that in the coming days. Jaquan Brisker did not practice. It is not believed to be any sort of injury but rather a veterans day off. TE Robert Tonyan had several quality chunk plays over the middle. For what it’s worth, Tonyan was listed as the third tight end on the Steelers’ initial roster. Look for him to be a guy that makes the team given his familiarity with Rodgers and his quality of play this camp. After a rough go earlier in the week, tackle Troy Fautanu had a dominant practice. He stood out in one-on-one blocking drills and continues to show he is a player on the rise. Rico Dowdle looks very fast. Keep in mind they aren’t fully tackling, but there was a rep tonight where the running back exploded in between the tackles and would have had a huge gain even if they were tackling. title: Seahawks host cornerback Terrion Arnold amid felony robbery, kidnapping case
summary: The Seattle Seahawks and general manager John Schneider have a history of treading cautiously with players who have troubled pasts, but sometimes the the possibility of adding a promising young talent is too good not to explore. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Sunday that the Seahawks hosted former Detroit Lions first-round pick Terrion Arnold […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Terrion Arnold #6 of the Detroit Lions runs onto the field prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks and general manager John Schneider have a history of treading cautiously with players who have troubled pasts, but sometimes the the possibility of adding a promising young talent is too good not to explore. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Sunday that the Seahawks hosted former Detroit Lions first-round pick Terrion Arnold for a visit on Sunday. Arnold, who was drafted 24th overall in 2024, was released by the Lions on June 29 after he was arrested on eight total felony counts ranging from kidnapping to armed robbery. Here’s a summary from the last time Arnold’s name was linked to the Seahawks : Authorities accused Arnold of orchestrating the abduction and beating of three men whom prosecutors believe were wrongly suspected of stealing luxury goods and $100,000 in cash from Arnold’s AirBnB rental in Florida. Prosecutors further claim that although Arnold was not present at the time of the abduction and beating, he directed his associates to hold, beat, and pistol-whip the victims. Arnold posted bond and is eligible to sign with any team. He previously visited the Houston Texans in early July. The visit comes during third-round pick Julian Neal’s ongoing absence as he navigates through a leg injury. Although head coach Mike Macdonald said Neal is not expected to be sidelined long-term, the team’s interest in another cornerback indicates Neal’s status is definitely something to monitor in the coming days. Across two seasons with Detroit, Arnold was an inconsistent performer, but showed promise. He struggled heavily with penalties at the beginning of his rookie campaign, before showing signs of progression in the back half of the season. But, he failed to build off the strong second half in his sophomore year, where he regressed both in coverage and stopping the run. He recorded 70 combined tackles, one interception and 18 passes deflected across 22 career starts, having missed half of 2025 due to injury. Arnold is scheduled for an arraignment hearing in a Tampa court on Aug. 13, two days before the Seahawks’ preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys.

title: ‘Hard Knocks’ showed us Mike Macdonald’s team culture diagram
summary: The first episode of “Hard Knocks” featuring our own Seattle Seahawks was full of highlights. One of the most intriguing things to me was a scene where Mike Macdonald was addressing the team and explaining how the 90’s Chicago Bulls finally turned the corner, becoming a dynasty.  Specifically, at 1:25 in the clip above we […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - FEBRUARY 11: Head coach Mike McDonald of the Seattle Seahawks and his wife Stephanie MCDonald celebrate with fans during the Seattle Seahawks Super Bowl LX victory celebration and parade at Lumen Field on February 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first episode of “Hard Knocks” featuring our own Seattle Seahawks was full of highlights. One of the most intriguing things to me was a scene where Mike Macdonald was addressing the team and explaining how the 90’s Chicago Bulls finally turned the corner, becoming a dynasty. Mike Macdonald gave the Seahawks a history lesson on the 90s Bulls 🏀 Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks premieres tonight at 9pm ET on @HBOMax pic.twitter.com/o3aAeQwFio — NFL (@NFL) August 5, 2026 Specifically, at 1:25 in the clip above we get a glimpse at Macdonald’s entire vision for the Seahawks culture brought together in a single graphic. I went ahead and took a screenshot, so we can focus on it. Enhance… This diagram contains the core tenets of Macdonald’s football ethos, and by extension, his version of the Seahawks. We’ve heard him say all of these at some point, and this one graphic pulls them all together. Mike is extremely intentional in how he phrases things. I’m guessing that the layout of this diagram is also intentional. One of my majors in college was Management. I’ve been through multiple versions of leadership training, and I’m also a teacher and coach so these kinds of things really strike my fancy. Please indulge me as we break this down a little more! Our eyes are immediately drawn to the “12 As One” right in the center. This is at the core of the Seahawks’ philosophy, underscoring the importance of playing as a team and including the fans as part of that. Those words are shown in the largest font size and also circled by 12 (very intentional) of the green feather accents from the jerseys. The next large print showcases “Chasing Edges”, a very early Mike Macdonald-ism about always being on a constant quest to improve, no matter how small. Those two words surround the “12 As One” within the arrow (which we’ll get to in a bit). The font size is just as large as “12 As One”, and is also centered which highlights the significance of that phrase. At the end of the arrow, we have the next largest text featuring the three words “Decisive, Relentless, and Shocking.” This is how Macdonald wants his Seahawks teams to play. He also talks about the “tip of the spear,” and having these words at the point of the arrow could symbolize how these three characteristics allow the team to move forward. Speaking of moving forward, notice which way the arrow is pointing? Yeah, I believe having that arrow in there is absolutely intentional and represents “running it forward,” the newest Mike Macdonald saying for continued evolution of the Seahawks. Finally, we have the phrases on the outline of the arrow with “Thru, Not Around”, “Stack W.I.N.S”, “Old School Principles, New School Methods”, and “A Style Nobody Wants To Play.” These are all in a slightly smaller font than the rest, but still make up essential parts of Mike’s messaging. They make up the border of the arrow, tying the entire diagram together. Maybe I’m just nerding out, but I love things like this. Every leadership program has its own version of a graphic like this, summarizing everything in a single, digestible picture. All of these facets of Seahawks culture contributed to last season’s Super Bowl run, and I really enjoy seeing them all in one, cohesive representation. Mike Macdonald is a heck of a leader, and I’m confident in how he’ll use this diagram to continue to evolve the team going forward!

title: Live from Lumen Field: What we learned after watching Seahawks Football Fest 2026
summary: The Seattle Seahawks welcomed fans into Lumen Field for the first time since, well, the Super Bowl parade, as thousands upon thousands packed the lower bowl for a family day out at Football Fest. Marshawn Lynch and Cliff Avril were there and the fans loved it, many footballs and t-shirts were given away, and plenty […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks welcomed fans into Lumen Field for the first time since, well, the Super Bowl parade , as thousands upon thousands packed the lower bowl for a family day out at Football Fest. Marshawn Lynch and Cliff Avril were there and the fans loved it, many footballs and t-shirts were given away, and plenty of kids got to see their favorite players up close and get their autographs. It’s the Seahawks’ penultimate public training camp for the year, exactly a week out from their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Exactly a month from now is when the season starts and Seahawks fans will get to witness their second Lombardi Trophy banner unveiled . Field Gulls completed its week at Seahawks training camp by watching from the top of Section 136. ‘Hard Knocks’ was filming on the field, while we were not allowed to even have our phones out for any sort of use, filming or otherwise, during the team portion of practice. I’m once again emptying my embarrassingly illegible notebook with my observations (with credited observations to Seahawks Forever’s Dan Viens, as well as The Hawks Eye and Field Gulls’ Bryce Coutts and Josh Hite). The running game showed some explosiveness No Jadarian Price? No problem. Emanuel Wilson, George Holani, and even Velus Jones Jr all had at least one explosive run on the day. Wilson has really stood out for good camp performances this week, and while I’ve been resistant to the idea of Jones having much of a roster chance, there may yet be some hope as a gadget WR/RB hybrid. In our post-game recap video , Josh Hite likened Jones to JD McKissic and I think that’s a decent Seahawks comparison. While we did see some shotgun and pistol looks in the run game, under center ruled the day. I didn’t really think too much about the Wilson signing as being impactful, but Wilson’s ability to just get north whether he has exceptional speed or not is a plus. Elijah Arroyo showcased his skills The second-year tight end wasn’t all that impactful as a rookie, plus the injuries slowed down his progress. Under Brian Fleury, Arroyo could thrive. We’ve seen him split out wide several times like he’s a traditional X receiver, and his blocking has looked noticeably improved. This touchdown grab in the back corner of the end zone against Julian Love was an exquisite play between him and Sam Darnold. Go get it 😤 @elijah_arroyo pic.twitter.com/uljWljZczC — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 9, 2026 Arroyo’s training camp performances come at a time when A.J. Barner has been practicing but doesn’t seem 100 percent. Mike Macdonald all but indicated that Barner is still recovering from offseason surgeries, and on Saturday Barner did not catch a pass and uncharacteristically lost out on a couple of pass protection blocks. A.J. Finley had the most feel-good moment of Football Fest When A.J. Finley tore his ACL at last year’s Seahawks Football Fest, I had full view of the unfortunate end to his season. In the “simulated overtime” session that marked the start of 11-on-11 practice, Finley seized on Sam Darnold’s ill-advised throw to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and picked off the pass. Andre Fuller had coverage underneath and Finley was there over the top to make the grab, which was an awesome moment for someone who’s been with the second-team long enough that he has played his way into the conversation of making the roster. See ball. Get ball. @AJFinley1 pic.twitter.com/dNezWqIl0E — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 9, 2026 The defense had the slight edge over the offense Sam Darnold wasn’t bad but he wasn’t at his complete sharpest. Leaving aside the interception that was against the second-team defense, Darnold was fortunate not to have an out route throw to JSN picked by Josh Jobe, who undercut the route and broke up the pass. He also dropped a snap that resulted in an aborted play and had a pass batted down at the line by Brandon Pili. During the red zone challenge, Darnold did have a high of that aforementioned TD to Elijah Arroyo, but the right side of the Seahawks offensive line gave up “sacks” on consecutive plays to turn a red zone “possession” unto 4th and 24. Byron Murphy II and Uchenna Nwosu had the sacks that derailed the series. The defensive twos similarly did well against Drew Lock and company, although I’d say that was a little more even. Rashid Shaheed got some run with the twos in a mix-and-match and feasted on a blown coverage for an easy TD, while Lock stared down Tory Horton on a dig route and threw a bad interception to safety Rodney Thomas II. Bud Clark also blitzed and “sacked” Lock in the red zone, although I believe they never blew the whistle on Clark and Rylie Mills just chased him out of bounds anyway. Jalan Gaines was notably working with the twos as part of his impressive camp, while Tyrice Knight once again had several reps as an edge. The third-team defense did not produce a turnover, but we did see some positive play from Chazz Surratt in run support and Aidan Hubbard through pressuring Milroe into a goal line throwaway. Brian Fleury’s offense will not be Klint Kubiak’s offense copy-and-pasted …And frankly, nor should it be. Fleury is his own OC, he’s calling the plays, he’s designing the offense, and his ties to Kyle Shanahan run a fair bit deeper than Klint Kubiak. Based on what I saw on Saturday and at camp on Wednesday and Friday, we should see more condensed formations (even if it’s 11 personnel), motioning of tight ends, and dual running back sets. The concepts of this offense will more closely resemble Shanahan, and I still think a fullback will be a part of this offense, whether it’s Robbie Ouzts (no update on him despite us seeing him on the sideline, by the way), Brady Russell (likely too small for a FB role), or Brock Lampe (he did practice and had some nice reps). Rylie Mills had another big day It’s hard not to gush about Mills. When you see him winning pass rush reps against Abe Lucas and then getting in on a TFL run stop on the opposite side, you wonder what his ceiling truly is. Mills is strong as hell and wins with his hands so violently, plus he’s shown off a wicked swim move. It seems inevitable that Mills is going to be a major part of the defensive line rotation this season. We’ve discussed Mills to death but forgive me if I’m buying into the hype that Seattle got a second-round talent at a fifth-round price due to his ACL injury at Notre Dame. Jalen Milroe got the ‘1-on-1’ work Milroe had his highlights playing with the third-team offense, including a long, lofted 45+ yard touchdown to Montorie Foster Jr (who continues his excellent camp) in 11-on-11. I cannot say that D’Anthony Bell played that particularly well, but Milroe and Foster made it work. Milroe also flashed his speed on a 25-yard scramble later on in practice. What is noteworthy from the 1-on-1 battles, which mixed OL vs. DL in a blocking rep, RBs vs. LBs on throws in the flat, and WRs/TEs vs. DBs on downfield passing plays, is how Milroe had most (if not all) of the passing responsibilities. That means seeing Milroe throw to Elijah Arroyo, who got low near the goal line for a catch against rookie Bud Clark, as well as a lovely back-shoulder throw to Emmanuel Henderson Jr against Michael Dansby. Slowly but surely, Milroe is developing. Keep an eye on Mason Richman, Logan Brown, and Chris Paul Jr Three Seahawks unfortunately left practice a little banged up. Bryce noted that Mason Richman appeared to tweak something during a 1-on-1 rep, was looked at by trainers on the sideline, and did not return for any 11-on-11 work. He’s been getting some run at center and guard throughout camp and has been typically with either the twos or threes. Brown was holding his right arm after the final play from scrimmage, while simultaneously Chris Paul Jr appeared to injure the lower part of his leg. I think he got rolled up on but we only got one replay and I couldn’t quite make out what happened. Either way, Paul and Brown were both down for a bit…

full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JULY 25: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on July 25, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have been without first-round running back Jadarian Price over the past two days due to a “lower body soreness” issue , which naturally created cause for concern given he’d otherwise practiced all camp. Seattle has also dealt with the likes of high draft pick running backs Rashaad Penny and Kenneth Walker III missing parts of camp and/or preseason games due to injury as rookies. Head coach Mike Macdonald’s latest update on Price is still not that specific, but at least the timeline should calm any worried fans down. “We are going with a lower body soreness,” Macdonald said after Saturday’s Football Fest at Lumen Field. “Somewhere between the upper leg and lower body soreness. I’m not making light of it. It’s a minor issue right now. It’s a matter of days, so he will be back soon.” The Seahawks, meanwhile, signed running back Justin Jones presumably to just take some carries in upcoming practices while Price looks to return soon. The former Notre Dame back was on the sidelines at Football Fest after not being at Friday’s practice at all. With Price out, the bulk of the work at practice has gone to the trio of Emanuel Wilson, George Holani, and Velus Jones Jr. With Jacardia Wright also out injured, T.J. Harden has also taken some reps at the position. Seattle has an off-day on Monday before resuming practice on Tuesday for their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys.

title: Kyle Shanahan: Ricky Pearsall was not a factor in bringing Deebo Samuel back
summary: Kyle Shanahan says the injury to Ricky Pearsall had nothing to do with Deebo Samuel’s return. full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 12: San Francisco 49ers Deebo Samuel Sr. (right) and Ricky Pearsall watch the Golden State Warriors play against the Dallas Mavericks at Chase Center on November 12, 2024 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kyle Shanahan says the injury to Ricky Pearsall had nothing to do with Deebo Samuel’s return. When taking the podium for the first time at San Francisco 49ers training camp, the head coach denied that Ricky Pearsall’s loss for the season influenced the decision. “They’re just two just two completely different types of players,” Shanahan said. “Deebo was someone that we were hoping it would work out.” The 49ers signed Samuel on a one-year, $7 million contract the same day Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve. The 49ers and Samuel were talking for week s, per a report; players like Kyle Juszczyk and George Kittle were on social media offering up their guest houses for Samuel. In the weeks leading up to his signing, Pearsall had symptoms from his 2025 PCL injury. The decision was made to get surgery. While Samuel and Pearsall are different players and Shanahan may have wanted the former back before the latter went down with injury, Samuel’s return is more crucial given the situation. What once was a crowded wide receiver room with rookie De’Zhaun Stribling, Christian Kirk, Jacob Cowing and others is now a bit banged up, with small injuries keeping players out of practice. Samuel says he has a few years left . Samuel was drafted by the 49ers in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft. He was traded to the Washington Commanders in 2025—one year ago and not re-signed at season’s end. While a one-year, $7 million contract (loaded with incentives) with the 49ers is nothing to sneeze at, Samuel obviously wanted to see what was available in the market first before committing. Shanahan noted they hoped it worked out depending on the opportunities Samuel had. It might have been more Samuel finding the right deal than the 49ers trying to get their wide receiver room figured out. Kyle Shanahan just wanted his wide-back back. “The Ricky thing changed nothing”
