full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Detroit Lions camp is taking place in Allen Park, Mich., and Lions reporter Eric Woodyard has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Lions camp. We will update this file often. Can Dan Campbell & Co. get Detroit back in the playoffs in 2026? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Lions camp 
 
 Lions make Jahmyr Gibbs highest-paid running back in NFL history 
 Ex-All Pro LB Devin White joins Lions on 1-year deal 
 Campbell: Robinson deal won't 'hurt' contract talks with Gibbs 
 
 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff , and most of the starters, will not play in the preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals this week but could see some action against Washington on Aug. 22, according to head coach Dan Campbell. Undrafted rookie QB Lions  Luke Altmyer will now continue in the QB2 role behind Goff and is expected to take heavy snaps on Thursday, but Detroit will likely be adding another veteran QB for depth purposes as early as this week after Teddy Bridgewater decided to step away from the team. Altmyer says he's "excited" for the opportunity ahead.

 "I've played at a high level with the Big Ten and I've played in football games but it's a different level and I think that's the challenge is can you maintain emotions because it can get you really high and really excited," Altmyer said after Sunday's practice. "But, trusting my abilities, trusting my preparation, trusting my teammates. I think that's the word trust."

 Other observations:  

 
 Lions veteran QB Teddy Bridgewater has decided to step away from the team amid training camp and was officially placed on the reserved/retired list ahead of Sunday's practice. Campbell says he will be "missed" but this retirement could be for good. 
 Lions HC Dan Campbell and his wife Holly attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Canton to support legendary New Orleans Saints QB Drew Brees on Saturday on an off day. Campbell was an assistant/tight ends coach in New Orleans from 2016-20 and signed with the Saints as a player in 2009. "It was a reminder. It was refreshing just to be able to stand in the presence of greatness with those guys," Campbell said. 
 The Lions signed CB Ryan Cooper and LB Amen Ogbongbemiga and waived TE Nick Muse . 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 The connection between Jared Goff and  Amon-Ra St. Brown  was on display as St. Brown scored a touchdown in Friday's scrimmage off a slant at the goal line through tight coverage. St. Brown had a two-point conversion while also converting multiple fourth downs on a monster day in which his playmaking was consistently on display. WRs coach Scottie Montgomery credits Goff and St. Brown's friendship as the driving force of their on-field chemistry.

 "These guys, their timing is correct, but their off-the-field relationship also gives us an opportunity that a lot of people don't have," Montgomery said. "The communication between the two of them is probably what makes them as consistent as they are. There's certain things and there's nonverbal communication that happened between them now because of where we are in the offense, where they are in their relationship away from the building."

 More observations: 

 
 After signing a record three-year extension on Thursday, RB Jahmyr Gibbs was on the field and in uniform for the second straight day of practice but didn't participate in full team drills. "This process has been extremely stressful. I just wanted to play ball," Gibbs said. "I missed being out there with my teammates and coaches and it's just fun being out there now with my pads and stuff on. It just feels a lot better." 
 Detroit rapper Sada Baby and popular comedian Haha Davis were both in attendance for Friday's practice, sharing their excitement for the upcoming season while mingling with fans. "When you go 15-2 and reach the NFC Championship, at some point it has to go down and this is the year," Haha Davis said. "I really believe that." 
 The Lions are signing veteran DT Ben Stille to a one-year deal, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. 
 Detroit has waived injured CB  De'Shawn Rucker .﻿ 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Lions held a 2 ½-hour practice session in humid conditions. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell wasn't pleased with the performance of the defense during red-zone drills and was brutally honest in his assessment. He also took accountability for his "fair share of mess ups" as they're looking to improve to reach their standard ahead of Week 1.

 "Not very good. I'll be completely honest with you," Campbell said. "What caused it? I feel like there's obviously communication and technique. It's really simple. Like football is simple, but it's hard to do. It's easy to talk about and hard to do."

 Campbell feels they will continue to get better.

 More conversation:  

 
 Running back  Jahmyr Gibbs returned to practice, taking part in the walkthrough portion and stretches for the first time all training camp, before working on the side with a team trainer. However, he didn't participate in any individual drills during the session as he seeks a new deal. A crowd of media members swarmed Gibbs as he strolled off the practice field to enter the locker room after signing autographs, but he carefully avoided reporters and flashed a thumbs-up sign to the group after being asked if he was close to reaching a contract extension soon. 
 CB De'Shawn Rucker (ankle) and DT Mekhi Wingo (groin) left practice early to be evaluated for potential injuries. Several other players were limited due to cramping from the heat on a humid day. 
 The Lions placed TE Miles Kitselman on reserve/injured and signed WR Tarik Black . 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Tuesday marked Day 2 of padded practices and veteran LB Devin White continued to get acclimated to the defense alongside guys like All-Pro Jack Campbell . White was signed as a free agent on Aug. 1 to add depth after rookie linebacker  Jimmy Rolder went down with a hamstring injury earlier in camp. He has received limited reps in practices so far but has been doing additional conditioning drills on the side with trainers to keep in shape. "Right now, they've got a plan for me and I'm trusting in the plan," White said. "So, whenever they're ready for me to stop doing reps on the side, running and getting more reps in the team period, I'm going to be ready for it."

 More observations: 

 
 Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs missed his sixth straight practice as his hold-in for a contract extension continues but was on the field watching. Ahead of Tuesday's practice, the Atlanta Falcons reached a record-setting three-year extension with RB Bijan Robinson worth up to $75 million, which now likely sets the stage for Gibbs to reach an extension soon. Campbell feels it's "certainly not gonna hurt" with the process of negotiating. "It's not gonna hurt. But we'll see. Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there," Campbell said. "Every day that goes by, that's another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But there again, it'll get done when it gets done." 
 LB Malcolm Rodriguez left practice early to be evaluated for an ankle injury.

title: Do NFL superteams usually win the Super Bowl? Will the Rams?
summary: The Rams are loaded this season, and basically everyone is picking them to win the Super Bowl. But preseason darlings of the past 35 years haven't always met expectations.
full_text:
The 2026 Rams are the closest thing we've had to a preseason superteam in several years. Sean McVay's group was already a popular pick to win Super Bowl LXI before the offseason began. But then L.A. traded for Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson , shoring up the secondary at the expense of a potential Super Bowl opponent in the Chiefs. The move to draft Ty Simpson as Matthew Stafford 's successor struck a curious tone, but general manager Les Snead responded with the mother of all high-stakes moves, trading Jared Verse and three picks to the Browns for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 Unsurprisingly, the Rams have become prohibitive favorites to win the Super Bowl after their aggressive moves this offseason. Picking any other team to win the Lombardi Trophy at this point would almost require coming up with some sort of explanation for what happened to the Rams along the way.

 And yet, we have to look back only one year to remind ourselves how NFL seasons can play out entirely differently once players get on the field. In 2025, 68 ESPN personalities picked  their AFC and NFC champions, along with an eventual Super Bowl winner, before the season kicked off. Not a single person picked the Seahawks or Patriots. I predicted the  Chiefs and Packers , who combined for exactly zero playoff wins. Preseason darlings like the Chiefs, Lions and Commanders each missed the playoffs altogether.

 Was 2025 just a weird year? And how often do heavily favorited superteams such as the 2026 Rams actually win the Super Bowl? I decided to take a more comprehensive look through history to get a sense of how confident we can be that Los Angeles will be the last team standing come Feb. 14 .

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 To do so, I'm going to look at the 15 largest preseason favorites since 1990 and see how their seasons played out. I'll be using the preseason odds compiled at Pro Football Reference from 1990 to 2025 and compare them with the odds posted for this season's Super Bowl at  DraftKings . The Rams have odds of +550 at DraftKings to win the Super Bowl, while nobody else in the league is shorter than +1000. After we adjust for the vigorish and convert the betting lines into probabilities, the Rams have an implied 12.5% chance of winning this season's Super Bowl, putting them 5.1 percentage points ahead of the second-placed Bills and Ravens.

 While the absolute number might be a better sense of how the market views a particular team, I'm going to use the latter figure to sort through our top 15 teams (well, 16, if we're including the 2026 Rams). There were plenty of seasons in the 1990s where two or three superteams -- such as the 49ers and Cowboys -- were seen as significantly better than the rest of the competition. I want to get a sense of what it was like for the teams that truly separated from the pack before the season began, as appears to be the case for this Rams squad.

 Did those teams hold up to their preseason expectations? Was the market overconfident about their chances? Let's go team by team before using the lessons from those 15 earlier cases to talk about what it means for the 2026 Rams and their chances of winning McVay and Stafford their second title.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 2026 Rams | 2021 Chiefs | 2019 Patriots 
 2018 Patriots | 2017 Patriots | 2009 Patriots 
 2008 Patriots | 2007 Patriots | 2002 Rams 
 2001 Rams | 1998 Packers | 1997 Packers 
 1996 49ers | 1995 49ers | 1994 49ers | 1990 49ers 
 Can this season's Rams win the Super Bowl? 

 
 

 

 2017 New England Patriots 
 Implied odds: 19.8% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL: 11.5% 
 Result: Lost Super Bowl LII to the Eagles, 41-33 

 I wouldn't have guessed that the 2017 Patriots stood out in terms of Super Bowl odds more than any other New England team from the Tom Brady-Bill Belichick era, but let's contextualize this. The Pats were coming off that legendary 34-28 win over the Falcons in Super Bowl LI . Brady was getting Rob Gronkowski back from injury after the star tight end missed the playoff run with a back ailment , while Belichick added a new star receiver to the mix in Brandin Cooks . After a 14-2 season and with Brady motivated by the four-game suspension he took for the Deflategate scandal, you could understand why the Patriots were heavy favorites to repeat as champs.

 

 Some things went as expected. Brady won the league MVP award. Cooks and Gronkowski each topped 1,000 yards. The Pats went 13-3 and took home the top seed in the AFC.

 Others did not. Belichick's team started 2-2 and needed a last-minute comeback win over a 4-12 Texans team to avoid opening the season 1-3. The Pats righted the ship quickly, but they were trailing by 10 points in the fourth quarter of the AFC title game and were down nearly three scores to the Jaguars, only for Myles Jack 's fumble recovery touchdown to be overturned. Two late touchdown passes to Danny Amendola controversially pushed the Pats into the Super Bowl.

 There, well, nothing went as planned. The Patriots defense had quietly been a mess all year, finishing the regular season ranked 31st in DVOA. The offense covered up the weakness by holding on to the ball and getting out to early leads. The Eagles were heavy underdogs with backup quarterback Nick Foles in for the injured Carson Wentz , and you know what happened next. Brady threw for 505 yards and three touchdowns, still the record for an NFL quarterback in a losing effort, but the defense couldn't stop Foles & Co. The Pats fell 41-33.

 

 
 

 2007 New England Patriots 
 Implied odds: 20.9% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL:  10.5% 
 Result: Lost Super Bowl XLII to the Giants, 17-14 

 Are you sensing a trend? This was another Patriots team that rode offseason optimism about its offensive additions to high hopes before falling short in the Super Bowl. The 2006 Pats had blown a 21-3 lead to the Colts in the AFC Championship Game , but they also weren't far removed from winning three titles between 2001 and 2004. Brady had improved as a quarterback over that time, and during the offseason, Belichick had rebuilt the offense by trading for Randy Moss and Wes Welker and signing Donte' Stallworth.

 What happened next is one of the more notable seasons in NFL history. The Pats were caught spying on the Jets during a 38-14 blowout victory in Week 1, turning a team that had been the underdog favorites during their win over the Rams in 2001 into the villains of the NFL. On the field, the Patriots blew defenses away with their spread attack, as Brady produced arguably the greatest season in league history under center. The Patriots went 16-0 in the regular season, winning their average game by nearly 20 points.

 By the time the postseason came around, though, the cracks were beginning to show. Brady threw three picks in the AFC title game , but with Philip Rivers playing through a torn ACL and LaDainian Tomlinson limited by injury to three touches, the Chargers couldn't take advantage in a 21-12 defeat. And in the Super Bowl, again as heavy favorites, the Patriots were upset by a Giants team that was able to control Brady in the pocket with its pass rush.

 

 

 
 

 1996 San Francisco 49ers 
 Implied odds: 19.2% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL:  9.6% 
 Result: Lost in divisional round to the Packers, 35-14 

 The 49ers were the preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl in 1994, 1995 and 1996. Their status as the third team on this list might have more to do with a lack of competition in the AFC than anything else. The Bills were among the Super Bowl favorites earlier in the decade, but after a 7-9 season in 1994 and a 10-6 campaign in 1995, they had fallen back to the pack. The Steelers had advanced to the Super Bowl the prior season, but starting quarterback Neil O'Donnell had signed with the Jets in free agency, turning things over to 34-year-old Mike Tomczak as the team's starter. title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 If the Packers were looking for someone to emerge behind their top three receivers, then perhaps Sunday's practice will help. 
With Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle) out, Christian Watson was the only available starting receiver. 
Enter Savion Williams , the second-year receiver who had just 10 catches for 78 yards and a touchdown in limited opportunities as a rookie. In fact, last season Williams had more rushes (11) on jet sweeps and end arounds than he did receptions. 
Williams got things rolling Sunday when he caught a 60-yard bomb from third-string quarterback Kyle McCord early in practice. Williams took advantage of having linebacker  Kristian Welch  on him in coverage. But Williams didn't just show his skills with and against the backups. 
He caught four more passes -- all from starting quarterback Jordan Love  -- including another touchdown in the red zone and two more catches for first downs. 
"His measurables are off the charts in terms of his size, speed and strength," coach Matt LaFleur said recently. "And then he's just a young player that's still learning and he's got a long way to go, but I think he's showcased a lot of great traits, and that's why we drafted him and that's why we loved him coming out." 
Williams, a third-round pick, is in competition with the likes of Bo Melton , Skyy Moore , Isaiah Neyor and J. Michael Sturdivant for the backup receiver spots.

 Other observations: 

 
 Zach Bako-Bewele 's return to team drills for the first time since last season's knee injury might have cleared up the right guard situation. Instead of Anthony Belton going back to right guard, where he was a starter last season, the Packers instead went with Jacob Monk . Belton took mostly backup snaps at right tackle. Jager Burton took left guard snaps with Aaron Banks (knee) still limited to individual drills. 
 For the first time in camp, cornerback Keisean Nixon took reps with the No. 2 defense. It might not have been a full-fledged demotion because Nixon still got some first-team reps, but there were periods in which Brandon Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste were at the corners with the starting defense. 
 Defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt (ankle/leg) took 11-on-11 snaps for the first time in camp. Previously, he had done only individual drills. 
 Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (knee) and running back Chris Brooks (hamstring) were activated off PUP and NFI, respectively, and did individual drills. Hargrave said his knee issue was something that lingered from the offseason program, while Brooks said his injury happened during the break between minicamp in June and the start of training camp. 
 Rookie Trey Smack went 2-for-3 on field goals, missing from 48 yards off the right upright. He's now 16-of-23 in camp. 
 Not only did the Packers have an extended period at the end of practice that featured end-of-half/end-of-game special scenarios, but LaFleur was the one who directed each drill. It was another sign that LaFleur is focused on improving the way they finish games after blowing several leads last year. 
 Both starting inside linebackers,  Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin , missed practice. Cooper has a foot injury, and Franklin had just returned from the Pro Football Hall of Fame inductions. He attended the induction of former Colts teammate Adam Vinatieri . Tight end Josh Whyle (neck) also sat out. 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 Nothing like a deep-ball touchdown to cover up an offense's warts. That's what  Matthew Golden 's 52-yard touchdown catch from Jordan Love did on Friday night, when the annual Family Night crowd at Lambeau Field otherwise didn't have much to get excited about when it came to the Packers' offense.

 Everyone, however, probably left the stadium with visions of what Love and Golden can do in their second year together. Now, it's possible that edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr . could have blown up the whole play if tackling was allowed because he appeared to be closing in on Love, but everything else about it was picture-perfect. From the throw that sailed through the air to the over-the-shoulder catch by Golden, who got safety Javon Bullard turned around, it was the kind of play that Golden didn't make much last season as a rookie. He's expected to have a much bigger role in the offense this season.

 

 "I feel real confident just taking it day by day and just building chemistry with Jordan, being on the same page with him, communicating as much as I can," Golden said. "I feel like each and every day we go out there in practice, I feel like the chemistry between us is growing for sure."

 
 Trey Smack might have taken some of the pressure off himself after a solid showing. The rookie kicker, who came in 8-for-13 on field goals so far in camp, went 6-for-7 on Friday night. His lone miss was a 51-yarder wide left. Instead of kicking one after another like he had been doing in practice, the coaches gave Smack just a single rep at the end of each team period, making it more game-like. "Definitely, built a little bit of confidence up tonight," Smack said. "But we can always kick better." He will get only one more chance to kick in Lambeau in front of fans before the season because the Packers have just one home preseason game this year. 
 For a defense that wants to increase its takeaways from last year, there sure were some missed opportunities. Both Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney dropped potential interceptions during the team periods. The Packers had only 13 takeaways on defense last season after getting 29 in 2024. 
 Brandon Cisse , Bo Melton , Jacob Monk and  Chris McClellan  all dropped out of practice. Cisse, the rookie second-round pick who was at right cornerback with the No. 1 offense, said he was cramping and needed to hydrate better. McClellan, the rookie defensive lineman, who made a few tackles got rolled up on but said he was fine. Coach Matt LaFleur did not know what happened to Monk, who was the starter at right guard. 
 LaFleur said one of the best parts of Family Night -- besides the post-practice fireworks show and a near-packed stadium -- was having referee Shawn Hochuli and his crew officiate the practice. The Packers have local officials work training camp, but this was the first visit by an NFL crew this summer. "In terms of how they call defensive holding there was a number of those, there was a couple offensive holdings," LaFleur said. "So I think that was really good for our guys to get exposed to that." 
 A local high school football player tied Golden and Will Sheppard by catching five punts off the Jugs machine while having to hold each ball as he caught the next. With four in his arms and one between his knees, he couldn't hold onto No. 6. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 It…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Indianapolis Colts ' camp is taking place in Grand Park Sports Campus, Westfield, Indiana, and Colts reporter Stephen Holder has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Colts camp. We will update this file often. Will quarterback  Daniel Jones return to early-2025 form after a serious injury? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Colts stories 
 
 Tons at stake as Colts' Daniel Jones enters proving ground 
 Colts won't give Richardson away 
 Colts extend Jonathan Taylor for 2 years, $44 million 
 
 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 One year after being in contention to be the Colts' starting quarterback, Anthony Richardson Sr . now finds himself in a fight for the Colts' No. 2 quarterback spot behind Daniel Jones . 
Sunday was another day of evaluation for the Colts, with Richardson displaying some ups and downs throughout the workout before finishing with an impressive 2-minute drill that led to a touchdown. Meanwhile, Riley Leonard , his competition, has had a strong couple of days after battling his own inconsistency. 
Richardson requested a trade in February and was granted permission to speak with other clubs to see if a deal might materialize. Nothing did, so Richardson is back trying to re-establish himself with the organization. Richardson on Sunday said his accuracy needs to be more consistent. 
"I feel like I can improve a lot of things," Richardson said. "My decision making, I feel like I'm on point with the ball and I feel like I'm [throwing] to the right spot. Sometimes I don't throw the best ball, but I feel like my decision making is pretty good so far." 
Richardson and Leonard will split preseason snaps.

 Other observations:

 
 Receiver Josh Downs (groin) could potentially return to the lineup in Tuesday's joint practice at New England, coach Shane Steichen said. 
 Jones had his second and third interceptions of camp on Sunday, but both came on passes that appeared catchable. Receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine saw one pass go off his fingertips to safety A.J. Haulcy . Later, running back Jonathan Taylor had a pass go through his hands, landing squarely in the hands of safety Cam Bynum . 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Colts are still working to identify their best lineup at linebacker, and it's beginning to look like they might not have the luxury of settling in with a consistent starting group.

 Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo left open the possibility that the Colts might use a rotation of players at the position, with situations dictating who plays when. The issues are being currently exacerbated by the absence of projected starting middle linebacker CJ Allen (hamstring), the team's second-round pick.

 "At the end of the day, I think we're going to have a lot of guys in that room that play for us this year in different types of roles," Anarumo said.

 Having two rookies -- Allen and Bryce Boettcher -- among the leading candidates to start, is a factor, Anarumo said. Streamlining young players' responsibilities can allow for faster growth.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Receiver Josh Downs missed practice with a groin injury, leaving the Colts without their top two wideouts. Alec Pierce remains sidelined after offseason ankle surgery, and the Colts have provided no specific timeline for his return. 
 Riley Leonard was the second-team quarterback behind Daniel Jones , with Anthony Richardson Sr . playing with the third team. 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Starting quarterback Daniel Jones had one of his best days in Thursday's evening practice, connecting on a number of aggressive, downfield throws. But the same could not be said of the quarterbacks behind him on the depth chart.

 Anthony Richardson Sr . and Riley Leonard , locked in a battle for the backup job, have yet to establish the consistency that coach Shane Steichen is seeking. That continued on Thursday, when Leonard threw an interception to linebacker Austin Ajiake and Richardson was inefficient in his time under center.

 "The guy that's most consistent is going to win that job," Steichen said. "Those guys are battling. It's back and forth right now." He added, "There's been flashes, but yeah, there's work to done for sure."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 One week into camp and perhaps the biggest question is not a question at all.

 Quarterback Daniel Jones has not missed a single snap with the first-team offense and has not taken any days off from practice. This comes in spite of him only recently being fully cleared to practice in full-team drills following his Achilles tendon tear in December. If there were any uncertainties entering this camp, Jones has put them to rest.

 "I've felt good through the whole camp so far," Jones said. "I knew I would. You try to push yourself in the rehab in preparation for camp, knowing what to expect. I felt really good and I stay on the recovery part of it to make sure I'm available and out here every day."

 The Colts are five practices in and there are no known plans to pull back on Jones' workload.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward have been making life difficult for the team's wide receivers so far in camp, much to the Colts' contentment.

 Gardner and Ward are expected to be among the best cornerback combos in the league this season if they can both remain on the field. That was not the case last season, when they spent just one full game on the field together because of respective injuries.

 The length of both players has been especially challenging for the receivers, a group that is trying to find its way with the No. 3 spot still up for grabs.

 "When you can go up against two of the best in the league in practice every day, it's going to make everybody better," coach Shane Steichen said.

 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Colts spent most of Saturday's workout focused on red zone play, with the offense and defense more or less playing to a draw in terms of success. Among the highlights was tight end Tyler Warren 's leaping catch in the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Daniel Jones . Another impressive completion came when Jones delivered a strike to receiver Josh Downs in the corner of the end zone.

 But the defense held its own, too, forcing Jones and quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr . to scramble out of the pocket multiple times in 7-on-7 and in full-team periods.

 Additionally, cornerback Sauce Gardner had an athletic pass deflection against Downs to stop a red zone threat.

 More observations: 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon spoke to reporters for the first time in several months and revealed the details of her address to the team this week. On the heels of last season's massive collapse -- a seven-game losing streak to end the Colts' season -- Irsay-Gordon emphasized the need to finish.

 "As we reflected on last season, this one phrase just kept coming to my mind," she said. "And that was 'Find a way.' So that was the mantra that we settled on for this season. And we came to 'find a way' because we thought about what are the qualities that successful people have? And those qualities are consistency, those qualities are resilience."

 The Colts lost quarterback Daniel Jones and players such as  Sauce Gardner and DeForest Buckner down the stretch last season. But Irsay-Gordon emphasized that injuries would not be a cop-out this season, when general manager Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen are considered…

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jaguars' camp 
 
 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 
 
 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 Head coach Liam Coen is handing over playcalling duty to offensive coordinator Grant Udinski for the preseason games.

 The Jaguars will have a joint practice with the New Orleans Saints on Thursday and two days later will play the Saints at the Caesars Superdome at 4 p.m. ET. Starters are expected to get most of the reps in the joint practice and most will not play against the Saints.

 "Looking forward to it," Udinski said Sunday. "... So we'll put together a call sheet and a game plan accordingly so that way we can see what these guys can do and let them go out there and hopefully compete and have some fun."

 Udinski is in his second season as the Jaguars' offensive coordinator after joining Coen's staff last season following three seasons in Minnesota, moving from the assistant to head coach Kevin O'Connell/special projects in 2022 to the assistant offensive coordinator/assistant quarterbacks coach in 2024.

 Udinski, 30, interviewed for the head coaching jobs in Cleveland and Buffalo in the offseason.

 
 S Eric Murray notched his third interception of camp. Picked off  Trevor Lawrence . 
 Big day for WR Austin Trammell . Had two TD catches from Nick Mullens . Both were deep throws and Trammell made the catches against CB Preston Hodge . 
 S Rayuan Lane III punched the ball away from RB J'Mari Taylor  recovered the fumble. 
 OT Walker Little , TE Quintin Morris , DE Zach Durfee missed Sunday's practice with injuries. DT Arik Armstead had a vet day off. 
 

 

 Friday Aug. 7 
 Parker Washington picked up right where he left off at the end of the 2025 season: As the Jaguars' top pass catcher.

 Washington caught passes for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' Teal & White mock game on Friday (unofficial stats). He had a 50-yard catch and run and also had a 22-yard reception to go along with his 3-yard touchdown pass, one of three that quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw in the Teal's 19-12 victory.

 "It was nice to see Parker, Jakobi [WR Jakobi Meyers ], B.T. [WR Brian Thomas Jr .] make some plays and just getting the guys trying to spread it around a little bit and go execute," head coach Liam Coen said.

 Washington was thrust into a bigger role in the offense last season because of injuries to Travis Hunter and Thomas and by the end of the season was Lawrence's favorite target. Washington had 19 catches on 29 targets for 347 yards and two touchdowns in the final three games of the regular season. He also had seven catches for 107 yards and a touchdown in the playoff loss to Buffalo.

 Other unofficial stats and notes from the mock game: 

 
 Hunter played 14 snaps on defense and seven on offense. All of his snaps came while playing on the first units. He had no catches on two targets but he did carry the ball for 10 yards on a jet sweep. 
 Lawrence completed 15 of 29 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Washington, Thomas, and RB LeQuint Allen Jr . each had TD catches. 
 RG Patrick Mekari did not participate and RG Walker Little and LG Emmanuel Pregnon and were both injured during the mock game and did not return. LT Cole Van Lanen (knee) and OL Garrett DiGiorgio were already on PUP. This is potentially a problem area if the injuries to Mekari, Little and Pregnon linger. 
 CB Montaric Brown intercepted Nick Mullens to stop a drive in the red zone. CB Keni-H Lovely dropped an interception against Lawrence. 
 Second-year player B.J. Green II had at least two sacks and a tackle for loss. 
 Rookie S Jalen Huskey knocked the ball away from WR Chandler Brayboy and also recovered the fumble. 
 DE Josh Hines-Allen had a veteran rest day and did not participate. 
 

 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Talks between the Jaguars and receiver  Parker Washington 's camp on a contract extension remain active, but the fourth-year player out of Penn State isn't focusing on when a deal could get done and isn't upset that an agreement hasn't yet been reached.

 "It's there and it's a conversation, but my focus is just coming out here and I need to make plays for Trevor [Lawrence] ," Washington said Thursday. "So that's my mindset and that's how I'm going to attack it. I'm not going to step on my agent's toes. They can have those conversations. I'm going to come out here and do my job."

 Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said early in the offseason the team was working on extensions with Washington and tight end Brenton Strange . They reached a deal with Strange, signing him to a three-year extension worth up to $48 million in June but have yet to finalize anything with Washington.

 Washington was asked about his reaction to the four-year, $140 million extension  with $108 million guaranteed that receiver Zay Flowers agreed to with Baltimore and said he was happy for Flowers, who was the 22nd overall pick in 2023.

 "The receiver market is a little crazy and you see guys getting their opportunities and getting paid, I mean, that's cool," said Washington, whom the Jaguars drafted in the sixth round in 2023. "But like I said, for me, I just want to go out here and be my best self and just attack it."

 

 More observations: 

 
 OL Emmanuel Pregnon was injured during 11-on-11 and received treatment off to the side. He remained at practice but did not participate in any more team work. 
 S Preston Hodge intercepted QB Joey Aguilar and LB Ventrell Miller punched the ball away from RB Ameer Abdullah and recovered the fumble in 11-on-11 work. 
 The Jaguars will have a mock game on Friday morning at the team's practice facility. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Very good day for the defense on Tuesday in the Jaguars' second day in full pads.

 Safeties Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray and cornerback Jarrian Jones intercepted passes, Jones broke up another in the end zone, and linebacker Branson Combs broke up a pass on the goal line. Cornerback Jabbar Muhammad also had tight coverage on Travis Hunter on a throw into the end zone and forced an incompletion.

 Johnson's interception came off Trevor Lawrence while Murray and Jones picked off Nick Mullens .

 More observations: 

 
 Hunter had 17 snaps (10 defense, 7 offense) in 11-on-11 work. He has totaled 86 snaps (51 defense, 35 offense) through six practices. 
 LB Jared Bartlett was taken off the field after suffering a leg injury, which leaves the team down two linebackers ( Jack Kiser suffered a right knee injury on the first day of camp). The team is also limiting  Foyesade Oluokun 's snaps in team work, so the Jaguars could be looking to add at that spot. 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice as part of the team's plan to ramp up his participation. Rodriguez, who missed almost all of the spring with a left foot injury, did participate in Monday's practice. 
 DE Arik Armstead had a veteran day off on Tuesday, his second of camp.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Chargers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chargers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 During the first 11v11 period of Sunday's practice, the crowd roared for a Quentin Johnston reception that quarterback Justin Herbert perfectly placed by the outstretched arms of cornerback Nikko Reed .

 But had this not been training camp, Herbert likely would've been on his back or running for life before that ball had the chance to be released. Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu -- rushing from the interior on a front that featured Justin Eboigbe , Akheem Mesidor and Khalil Mack -- put a swift spin move on center Tyler Biadasz and was in Herbert's lap as the play was beginning. This sequence was a microcosm of Sunday's practice, as the defensive line controlled the day, constantly putting pressure on quarterbacks and stopping running plays before they could begin.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Branson Taylor , Kayode Awosika and Jake Slaughter rotated at left guard throughout practice. 
 Cornerback Tarheeb Still and left tackle Rashawn Slater both missed practice for a second straight day. Trey Pipkins and Taylor played left tackle in his absence. 
 Tre' Harris was active throughout practice with several receptions. 
 Avery Smith blew up a running play on a blitz, drawing celebrations from the defense. 
 Junior Colson pressured DJ Uiagalelei into a throw that landed in the hands of cornerback Isas Waxter , but Waxter dropped the interception. 
 Kyle Kennard had perhaps his best practice of camp, with several impressive wins in one-on-ones and pressures during 11-on-11 periods. 
 Trevor Penning had a good day, holding up well in one-on-ones and during team periods while working with the second and third groups. 
 Mesidor had one of the most impressive one-on-one wins of practice, beating Joe Alt cleanly with a spin move. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Rookie left guard Jake Slaughter got his first reps with the group blocking for Justin Herbert in a padded practice this training camp. The Chargers drafted Slaughter -- who played only center in college -- to be the team's starter at left guard, but he seemed to fall out of favor through camp as veteran Kayode Awosika and second-year lineman Branson Taylor emerged.

 Slaughter fared well in his reps at guard, showing a firm anchor when pressured from defensive tackles and the ability to pick up defensive stunts. His best moment came on a pancake block of defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson , but he was also beaten badly on a rep by defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe .

 Other observations: 

 
 Offensve lineman Trevor Penning appears to be falling back in the competition for the starting left guard job. He continues to work largely with the group, blocking for DJ Uiagalelei , though that could still change. 
 Rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson made an impressive toe-tap catch down the left sideline that drew a roar from the crowd. 
 Outside linebacker Khalil Mack was explosive throughout practice and had several would-be sacks. Tuli Tuipulotu and Nadame Tucker were also consistently disruptive off the edge. 
 Defensive tackles Jamaree Caldwell , Teair Tart and Eboigbe continued to disrupt the run game and generate pressure on the quarterback. 
 Uiagalelei, may have had the throw of the day, a 50 or so yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Derius Davis . 
 Herbert continues to be sharp and on target with his receivers. It appears he -- and the other quarterbacks -- has grown comfortable with the timing of McDaniel's offense. Receivers are getting passes early and in space. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Chargers' five-man race for guard continued Thursday with a new twist, as second-year lineman Branson Taylor took all the reps with quarterback Justin Herbert 's group at left guard. Before Thursday, two players had rotated at left guard, but Taylor got all of the reps with the first group in the team's first true padded practice.

 Taylor, a sixth-round pick in last year's draft who didn't make the 2025 53-man roster, was mainly a practice squad player last season. One year later, it seems that he has impressed the staff enough to have a legitimate shot at starting. On Thursday, Taylor fared well, creating running lanes and protecting Herbert throughout, a much-improved version of the player at camp last year.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said on Wednesday that veteran Kayode Awosika was leading the race to start, and that Taylor, Pipkins, Trevor Penning and rookie Jake Slaughter were in the mix.

 Other observations:  

 
 OLB  Tuli Tuipulotu participated in team drills during Wednesday's padded practice, his second day in a row after not participating in team drills for the first six days of training camp. Harbaugh originally said that Tuipulotu's absence was being "handled internally," then later said it was a "ramp up." Neither Tuipulotu, his representatives, or the Chargers have acknowledged a contract-related absence, but his return to the field signals that whatever matter was being handled internally is resolved. 
 Rookie S  Genesis Smith intercepted Justin Herbert after a pass went through Charlie Kolar's hands. 
 CB  Donte Jackson had an impressive diving pass breakup on a pass by QB  Trey Lance during 7-on-7 that led to an interception by safety Elijah Molden . 
 DT  Justin Eboigbe continued his strong camp, consistently generating interior pressure 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation on Wednesday could be a sign that things could be headed toward a resolution.

 Other observations:  

 
 After an injury scare Tuesday scare to the same left leg in which he sustained a season-ending patellar tendon rupture last year, left tackle Rashawn Slater was a full participant in practice Wednesday without any limitations.

title: 'Iron sharpens iron': New CB McDuffie elevating Rams' WRs
summary: True back-and-forths between WRs Adams, Nacua and new CB McDuffie hints at a promising season ahead for the Rams.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- Davante Adams was hesitant to put any pressure on new Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie . But midway through training camp, the veteran wide receiver couldn't resist the temptation to "gas him up" a little bit.

 "I can honestly say I don't know if I'll get a better look than what I get from Trent out there," Adams said. "I don't like putting big expectations, bulletin board material or any of that but at the end of the day, I can't remember the last time I felt about another corner the way I feel about him."

 Before the Rams traded for Myles Garrett on June 1, McDuffie was the defense-altering offseason acquisition for Los Angeles. The Rams traded for the All-Pro for a package of picks, including the No. 29 selection in the 2026 draft. Less than a week later, the Rams signed his former Kansas City Chiefs teammate Jaylen Watson to a three-year, $51 million deal to revamp their cornerbacks room.

 

 It didn't take long in the pair's first training camp with the team for his talent and technique to show up. Adams and fellow wide receiver Puka Nacua haven't been shy about the benefits of being able to go against McDuffie during training camp. And vice versa.

 Adams said "certain guys make plays because they fall into them," but that's not the case for McDuffie. 

 "But Trent's out there doing something every single play," Adams said. "... He's always got the right technique. He's got a great way of reading you out. He understands his position on any given play, whether it's his leverage or situationally a smart player and great technique.

 "I don't want to gas him up too much and have everybody thinking that he's going to win MVP this year, but I'm really happy with what I see. It's the epitome of iron sharpens iron. He's made some plays on me. I got him a couple times yesterday and I'm assuming that's how it'll be all year."

 On Monday, during what Rams coach Sean McVay called more of an "unscripted" practice, the back and forth was on display between McDuffie and Nacua. During a team drill, Stafford found Nauca down the field. But after Nacua got his hands on the ball, McDuffie knocked it away to force an incompletion.

 

 "Shout out to Puka," McDuffie said. "That boy was rolling, I'll tell you that much. He rolled right past me so I had to put my head down. Good ball, good catch and I was there and fortunate enough to knock it out."

 When Nacua recounted that play -- "[I] think I got it [for a touchdown] and there comes '22' [McDuffie] flying out of right field and being able to punch it out" -- he said it reminded him of the pair's days on the college practice field. Nacua and McDuffie played together at the University of Washington in 2019 and '20. Nacua was the first call McDuffie answered after he was traded to Los Angeles.

 Nacua said he has seen growth from McDuffie -- a first-team All-Pro in 2023 and a two-time Super Bowl champion -- since their days in college.

 "It's [McDuffie's] ability to have patience at the line of scrimmage," Nacua said when asked how McDuffie's game has changed. "I think that's something that Coach talks about all the time, especially in the DB room. When that ball is in the air you can see the body tense up and how they react when the ball is in the air, the look and lean. It's something that he stays patient and in that deep ball rep that we had the other day of him running and saying you got to take it all the way to the ground.

 "I think it's something that's been fun and working different movement at the line of scrimmage because he is so patient and trusts his feet. He knows he can roll too, so it's always fun. If I can take the top off, I think that means I was running pretty fast."

 The caliber of players on both sides of the ball -- including reigning MVP Matthew Stafford  and Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year -- has led to "a lot of really high-quality football," McVay said.

 "And not necessarily worried about who's winning or losing the drill," McVay said. "I want to see good, high-caliber ball.

 "... It's a blessing to be able to get out here, to be able to work hard, to work smart, to be able to protect one another, but push each other in a manner that's reflective of being able to have some productive failure on both sides of the football. That's what we want and I think that's what good teams do."

 And for as much as Adams praised McDuffie after practicing against the cornerback, McDuffie said he has "a lot of respect" for the veteran receiver. McDuffie called Nacua and Adams "two of the best receivers in the league," adding, "They have genuinely made me better every time I step on this grass."

 "Knowing who you're going to go against, knowing the type of player [Adams] is and knowing that every rep he gives you is going to be 100%, that's what I love," McDuffie said. "When I first came here, knowing who I was going to practice against, I was excited because they're going to get me better. 

 "... Yeah, he's going to beat me a lot of the time because I'm trying new things just like he's probably going to try new things. The more we can keep ping-ponging back and forth against each other, the more we can keep rising our standard, it's going to be a great year for both of us."

title: With De'Von Achane's workload safe, Dolphins sorting out backups' pecking order
summary: Expect Achane to get the workload Dolphins fans have gotten used to. But there's an interesting battle to be his backup.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- You can feel justified if you're looking to draft Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane in fantasy this season; his touches are about as safe as they've ever been.

 Over the past two seasons, Achane recorded the eighth-most touches in the NFL with 586, and his 145 receptions leads all NFL running backs in that span. The fourth-year running back handled that workload with wide receivers Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle on the roster, and Achane figures to be an even larger focal point of Miami's offense now that both players are gone.

 

 But the Dolphins feel like they have two capable backs behind Achane in Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright , and on an offense that plans to run the ball frequently, all three players could make an impact this season.

 Wright enters his third NFL season after the Dolphins traded a future third-round pick to select him in the fourth round in 2024. He played sparingly in his first two seasons but stood out on two occasions in place of an injured Achane, rushing for 86 yards against the New England Patriots in 2024 and 104 yards and a touchdown against the New York Jets last season.

 The speedy back, who ran a 4.38 second 40-yard dash at the NFL combine, said he has learned the value of patience -- both on and off the field -- as he waits for a bigger role within the offense.

 "Last year, my biggest thing was when I got in the game, it was, 'I gotta do this. I gotta make a play,' this, that and the third, and that's not good," Wright said. "Take what they're giving you. Take the little runs. The big runs will come. That's how I had to mature my mind about the game. Like I said, control what I can control.

 "I'll be ready when the opportunity is coming and those big runs come. You know it's gonna happen and I'm gonna go all the way to the house with it."

 Wright finished last season with the same number of carries as Gordon, albeit in seven fewer games, with Gordon being used more frequently in short-yardage and goal-to-go situations.

 

 Under first-year coach Jeff Hafley and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, the Dolphins don't want to pigeonhole Gordon as a short-yardage runner; they believe he is versatile enough to play all three downs if need be.

 "I want Ollie to compete to be an every-down back, and I think he's capable of doing it," Hafley said. "When Ollie has flashed and he knows what he's doing and he hits it, he has great speed, he has great size, and he can catch the ball out of the backfield, too. He gives us the ability with a bigger back to be good on third down and protection downs because he is a bigger person. But I want him to compete to be an every-down back."

 The Dolphins took Gordon in the sixth round of the 2025 draft, one year after he won the Doak Walker Award as college football's top running back.

 

 He said his first full professional offseason has felt markedly smoother than his rookie offseason, when he was still acclimating to the league after training to impress NFL front offices.

 "So basically this year to last year, I felt like it was way easier," he said. "Last year I felt like it was a bunch just thrown at me, and I'm like, 'Oh, I got to learn this. We got to train, got to do that,' but I feel like this year it's more like, 'OK, I can ease into it.'

 "I know my study habits. I know how to take care of my body also now, so I feel like just those things make it easier."

 Miami invested in its offensive line this offseason, drafting Kadyn Proctor and DJ Campbell , and signing Jamaree Salyer . In his introductory news conference in January, Hafley vowed for his team to be physical up front and run the ball as a byproduct of that physicality.

 Achane's role is solidified. Technically, there's a position battle to back him up. But two weeks into training camp, Miami's backs are focused more on finding ways to help the team succeed than they are on the pecking order behind Achane.

 "We all just work together," Gordon said. "So, I don't really look at it as going in as 'OK, running back two, running back two this.' Just whatever for the team, I'm here for."

title: 2026 Minnesota Vikings training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Minnesota Vikings ' camp is taking place in Eagan, Minnesota, and Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. We will update this file often. Who will win the starting quarterback battle between incumbent J.J. McCarthy and free agent addition Kyler Murray ? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What McCarthy-Murray QB battle means for Vikings' locker room 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 As the third week of training camp began in the evening, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was not ready to name a winner in the QB1 competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy .

 "Nothing has really changed from a standpoint of the timeline and things like that," O'Connell said before the Vikings took the field at TCO Stadium for their annual night practice. "So we'll see how the reps continue to go and when we feel like we're at that place, we're going to make sure we communicate that both in house and internally and obviously to you guys as soon as possible."

 The Vikings have a scheduled off day Monday to reset the competition if they desire. Murray entered training camp as the favorite for the job, and sources say they believe he still is. Asked Sunday where Murray is in the offensive system compared to where he thought he would be at this point, O'Connell said: "I think mentally he's definitely probably ahead of where I thought." O'Connell went on to say there are some parts of the offense that are new to everyone.

 
 It was a rough practice for the offense as defensive pressure made it difficult for quarterbacks Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy to get into a rhythm. Murray threw two interceptions, to cornerbacks James Pierre and Isaiah Rodgers , the latter when he was scrambling and tried to get the ball to Justin Jefferson on the sideline. McCarthy continued his theme of hitting deep out routes, including another to receiver Myles Price . McCarthy completed a deep pass to Jefferson down the right sideline but it forced Jefferson to slow down to bring it in, and he struggled later in a red zone drill. 
 Part of the protection issue was caused by the absence of left tackle Christian Darrisaw , who took a veteran's rest day. The Vikings also rested rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks , who remains on a maintenance plan to ensure full recovery from a broken left foot. 
 Defensive linemen Levi Drake Rodriguez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins also sat out the practice, giving rookie nose tackle Domonique Orange extensive first-team action. 
 Safety Jay Ward is in the latter stages of the concussion protocol, O'Connell said. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Two members of the Vikings' draft class -- both Day 3 picks -- made splash plays during a low-key practice.

 Rookie tailback Demond Claiborne ran about 70 yards off left tackle using a nifty jump cut to get outside. Claiborne, a sixth-round pick from Wake Forest, has mostly worked with the third team behind Aaron Jones Sr . and Jordan Mason . He could also get some work as a kick returner during the preseason.

 Meanwhile, cornerback Charles Demmings -- a fifth-round pick from Stephen F. Austin -- broke up a J.J. McCarthy pass intended for receiver Tai Felton near the goal line. For Demmings, it was the latest in a series of pass breakups, including two earlier in camp while he was defending Justin Jefferson . The Vikings seem to have their top three cornerbacks set with Byron Murphy Jr ., Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre , and it is always dangerous to get too excited when a rookie makes splash plays. But to this point, he has demonstrated he could provide an immediate contribution this season should defensive coordinator Brian Flores need him. 

 Other observations: 

 
 Veteran Jamal Adams said he appreciates the Vikings giving him a chance to work at safety, the position the New York Jets drafted him as in 2017, and that his new number of 32 is "definitely a better feeling" than the number he opened camp with (54). But Adams agreed it was likely he will also resume his linebacker duties at times in Flores' scheme. "I think it's going to be a little bit of everything, just being versatile in a lot of ways," he said. 
 Adams continued to get first-team work at safety in some packages with fellow safeties Jay Ward and Jakobe Thomas sitting out team drills. 
 Right tackle Brian O'Neill appeared to be taking a veteran's rest day. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison (left thumb) caught passes from quarterbacks for the first time since he suffered the injury while working in some team drills. 
 The Vikings will have their annual night practice Sunday at TCO Stadium. 
 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 NFL training camps can be tediously routine at times, but some days close observers can be surprised.

 The Vikings changed linebacker Jamal Adams ' jersey number from 54 to 32 and worked him in some of their safety specialty packages during full-team drills. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is well known for experimenting with personnel during training camp, and it's quite possible that Adams could alternate between linebacker and safety.

 Two other safeties, Jay Ward and rookie Jakobe Thomas , did not appear to be taking part in team drills.

 According to NFL rules, linebackers can wear numbers between 1-59 (and also 90-99). But defensive backs can't wear numbers higher than 49, which necessitated Adams' number change.

 Adams was drafted as a safety by the Jets in 2017, but he moved to linebacker for the Raiders last season. The Vikings signed him on the eve of training camp.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback J.J. McCarthy had one of his better days of camp as the competition with Kyler Murray continued. McCarthy hit wide receiver  Dontae Fleming  on a deep out, a route McCarthy has excelled at this summer, and also threw three touchdowns in a four-play red zone sequence. 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug.5 
 The Vikings haven't won a playoff game since 2019 and have three playoff victories in the past 25 seasons. So during his annual training camp meeting with reporters, co-owner/president Mark Wilf was asked about the patience his family has exhibited during its tenure as owners.

 "We try to be patient as an ownership, and that we know [leads to] ultimate success," he said. "But of course, patience isn't infinite. We understand that, but I feel really good about the direction of this football club and we're going to get to those benchmarks."

 Mark and Zygi Wilf hired general manager Nolan Teasley this spring to work with fifth-year coach Kevin O'Connell. Of their early interactions, Mark Wilf said: "I just think they work well together. I had an opportunity to watch them interact, and I just see how comfortable they are with each other. They have different characteristics but from my perspective, it's working well. And I think coach can focus on what he has to focus on. Nolan can focus on what he focuses on and they share and they collaborate and everyone in the building feels that."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Facing pressure during a two-minute drill, quarterback Kyler Murray made a smart decision: He lofted a jump ball for receiver Justin Jefferson . Predictably, Jefferson…

title: Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice?
summary: Gonzalez, who is still negotiating a contract extension, is leading by example at training camp.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Gonzo's voice: Early in his rookie season with the Patriots, cornerback Christian Gonzalez summed up his soft-spoken style: "I don't feel the need to express what I can do with my words. Just let your actions speak. I get a little more juice on game days, but that's kind of who I am."

 This was the Gonzalez way. One teammate even nicknamed him "Silent Assassin."

 All of which makes what has unfolded through the Patriots' 12 training camp practices this summer stand out that much more. The loudest and most demonstrative defender on the field? It's Gonzalez. And it probably isn't even close.

 Things hit their peak Thursday when Gonzalez seemed to be making a concerted effort to rattle receiver A.J. Brown and raise the overall intensity level of practice. After covering Brown tightly down the field and forcing an incomplete pass from quarterback Drake Maye , he began to follow Brown back to the sideline and let him hear it.

 Later, in a 2-on-2 red zone drill, he batted away a Maye pass to Brown and then turned toward a nearby camera to celebrate. Soon after, as players were transitioning to a new drill, Gonzalez seemed to be saying something to Brown and that led to a brief moment on the sideline where it looked like things could escalate as receiver Kayshon Boutte came over to pull Brown away. 

 

 Brown's presence has brought out a different side of Gonzalez.

 "He's going a little bit more, I'll say," Brown said. "With everyone else, he's real calm and relaxed; it's more fluid."

 Overall, Gonzalez acknowledged his shift from just letting actions speak.

 "Everybody thinks I don't talk at all. I talk a little, but I'm kind of quiet. It really depends on the day at practice," he said, adding that Brown brings it out of him from a competitiveness standpoint.

 "I like to figure out how to attack a receiver. Not every receiver you can talk to; some receivers get more mad if you don't say anything to them. You're trying to figure out how you can get an edge on them."

 Gonzalez's edge has been evident in other ways, too, such as the day he batted away a pass intended for tight end Hunter Henry and then gestured to the crowded bleachers to get a rise out of the thousands in attendance. Again, it was a different side of Gonzalez. 

 The willingness to draw more attention to himself, turn up the volume and help create a more competitive practice environment that raises the level of the entire team potentially puts him in position to become a team captain for the first time. Not to mention he has been a tone-setter despite an unresolved contract negotiation with the club.

 Coach Mike Vrabel had named Gonzalez a game captain for Super Bowl LX , and later said he asked Gonzalez if aspiring to become a permanent captain is a goal. When Gonzalez told him it is something he strives to be, Vrabel told him he hopes to help him get there. That, too, could be part of what has sparked the notable change from Gonzalez's approach in one of the most notable stories of training camp.

 

 2. New Gillette field: A new artificial turf playing field is being installed at Gillette Stadium this week, and here are key points as to why it is happening now:

 Once the World Cup concluded, the natural grass field required by FIFA was replaced with an artificial turf surface. The artificial turf surface installed was vetted by the Patriots and the  New England Revolution  and passed all NFL and MLS field tests, per chief operating officer Jim Nolan. However, the field was deemed noncompliant by the NFL.

 According to Nolan, the noncompliance was based on the NFL and NFL Players Association independent laboratory testing protocols. When the new field was lab tested last March, it was paired with an "E-layer," which is a rubber shock pad that sits underneath the field system, as the lab testing was conducted over concrete.

 The artificial turf/E-layer combination, however, was not suitable for Gillette Stadium, where the artificial turf is laid over a stone-dust base, and not concrete. As the field system was not installed over an E-layer, it was deemed noncompliant despite passing all NFL field tests.

 "We are confident the field would have passed if they had tested it in March without a pad, even over concrete," Nolan said.

 Nonetheless, a new artificial turf field must be installed for compliance. "The field we're installing is the latest version of the field we took out in January," Nolan said. "From a player perspective, it will be incredibly consistent with what they played on last year."

 The Patriots host the  Indianapolis Colts  in the preseason opener Thursday.

 3. Jacas impressions: Arguably the most significant development for the Patriots over the past week was getting rookie outside linebacker Gabe Jacas (second round, Illinois) on the field after he didn't sign his contract until two days into training camp and then worked behind the scenes on the non-football injury list (left knee) until returning Aug. 1.

 First impressions? His speed, power and suddenness make him the pass rusher most likely to win based on pure physical traits, rather than being reliant on scheme.

 

 "Real explosive off the edge," noted second-year outside linebacker Bradyn Swinson . "A calm dude, he's been learning things pretty fast. He's built like a freak house."

 4. A.J.'s focus: The Patriots' past two practices Thursday and Friday were their most humid and hot (temperatures in the 90s), which suited receiver A.J. Brown well based on what he told Sirius XM Radio was a top goal for him -- a focus on conditioning and perseverance.

 Told that he is a willing blocker, Brown said: "That's something I'm trying to pride myself even more right now. I wrote down in my notes, 'Just continue to be a complete player and I have to get in better game shape so I can show up more for my teammates.' ... The same momentum I have for the pass, that's the momentum I need to bring when it's a run play as well; I can survive eight plays, [but] I don't want to survive, I want to thrive. And it's a difference. I can be out there for a 10-play drive, but can I make an impact for those 10 plays, on the 10th play? That's what I'm chasing."

 5. DeVito's nickname : One of the lighthearted stories shared by Vrabel in his sit-down with Sirius XM NFL Radio last week was how he gave quarterback Tommy DeVito the nickname "Tommy 2 Chains."

 The moniker stuck after Vrabel said one of the first things he noticed in a team meeting last August was the two gold chains around DeVito's neck.

 "I love everyday walking in and seeing Tommy. He brings a spirit I love," Vrabel said, adding that the contrast between him and Maye is good for rookie quarterback Behren Morton (seventh round, Texas Tech) to see.

 DeVito was one of the top players in Friday's intrasquad scrimmage, throwing two touchdown passes and connecting with receiver DeMario "Pop" Douglas on a deep ball over the middle for 40-plus yards.

 6. Moses mentors Lomu : Starting right tackle Morgan Moses , the Patriots' oldest player (35), shared that rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu (first round, Utah) sits behind him in team meetings and that allows him to be a sounding board when questions arise. Moses shared his underlying message to Lomu, who has had some predictable rookie hiccups.

 Said Moses: "You have a laundry list of things you want to get completed, and I try to tell him, 'Don't take that laundry list out on the field with you. Take one of those things off the list every day.' When you go out there and try to work on this, that and other, your mind is spinning and you get up to the football, the snap count is going, and you play slower."

 7. Woodson as Byard: One of Vrabel's preferences is to avoid comparisons, so he treaded lightly in mentioning that part of why the Patriots selected safety Craig Woodson in the fourth round of the 2025 draft.…

title: 2026 New Orleans Saints training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Saints training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New Orleans Saints ' camp is taking place in Metairie, Louisiana, and Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. We will update this file often. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Sunday's practice featured the most 11-on-11 work yet, and it was an up-and-down day for the first-team offense.

 Quarterback Tyler Shough got off to a quick start with completions to Chris Olave , Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson in his first session. He was able to roll out and find Olave after an incompletion to Juwan Johnson . Later, Shough had three straight completions to Johnson, Olave and Tyson after a miss to Olave, but the offense was flagged for a false start, and then Shough was sacked on the next play. Shough targeted Olave downfield on the next session but couldn't connect and then was sacked before a completion to Travis Etienne Jr . His next period had completions to Etienne and Olave before he ran it himself for a first down. The unit finished the day working specifically on third down, and Shough had a completion to Noah Fant , incompletions to Vele and Barion Brown (with good coverage by Kool-Aid McKinstry ), and a completion to Tyson.

 Other observations:  

 
 Cesar Ruiz was back at starting right guard after playing second-team center Saturday. 
 Reserve guard Dillon Radunz is done for the season with a torn ACL. 
 Defensive end Cameron Jordan has a hamstring issue that could cause him to miss time in training camp. He was not at practice Sunday. 
 Kicker Charlie Smyth had his second straight three-miss day. After missing three kicks in a row during his last practice session Thursday, he went 4-of-7, missing from 47 and 56 yards and then missing a 50-yard field goal in the two-minute drill. 
 Alvin Kamara and Zach Wood were back at practice after attending Drew Brees' Hall of Fame ceremony (Jordan attended as well). 
 Rookie Bryce Lance had the play of the day, scoring a touchdown after a deep pass by Spencer Rattler . Running back CJ Donaldson had an impressive run with the third-team offense. 
 Quarterback Zach Wilson threw a deep touchdown to Ronnie Bell with the third-team offense. 
 John Ridgeway III  and Pete Werner left early with injuries. 
 Olave and Julian Blackmon practiced after both dealt with injuries in Saturday's practice. 
 Devin Neal , Kendre Miller , Christen Miller , Jeremiah Wright , Rejzohn Wright , Bub Means (personal) didn't practice. 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 It was Drew Brees day at practice as the former Saints quarterback goes into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

 The Saints painted a No. 9 on the practice field, and the staff, including coach Kellen Moore, wore No. 9 shirts. Running back  Alvin Kamara , defensive end  Cameron Jordan and long-snapper Zach Wood , along with coaches Josh Hill and Joel Thomas, were absent to watch the enshrinement in Canton, Ohio, but are expected back tomorrow.

 But the excitement of Brees being enshrined wore off early as the Saints dealt with some injuries. Offensive guard  Dillon Radunz  (knee) limped off the field after going up against Vernon Broughton in a one-on-one rep and did not return, while starting safety Julian Blackmon also left with a knee injury.

 Wide receiver Chris Olave walked to the sideline late in practice and had his wrist inspected and taped by athletic trainers before returning to take part in a "run down the clock" sequence at the end of practice, where he made a contested catch across the middle.

 Jordyn Tyson also had back-to-back catches from Tyler Shough in team drills, including one that Shough floated over the head of a defender attempting to break up a pass.

 Other observations:  

 
 Defensive tackle  John Ridgeway III  took over long-snapping duties with Wood out. 
 William Sherman played first-team right guard with Radunz out. The usual starting right guard, Cesar Ruiz , played second-team center. Moore said that was part of the plan to get Ruiz snaps there and that he will play in that position tomorrow as well. 
 Kicker Tanner Brown was 4-of-6 with misses from 39 and 54 yards. 
 Travis Etienne Jr . got all the first-team reps at running back.  
 Jordan Howden played first-team safety with Blackmon out. 
 Isaiah Stalbird intercepted Spencer Rattler in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Kendre Miller (back), Devin Neal (hamstring), Rejzohn Wright , Christen Miller (toe),  Chris Rumph II  (ankle) missed practice. 
 This was a scheduled shorter practice intended to end at 10:30 in front of the fans, but the Saints had to finish the final minutes inside because of lightning in the area.  
 New linebacker Deion Jones was at practice and wearing No. 45. 
 The Saints waived injured player Zxavian Harris . 
 

 

 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Rookie wide receiver Barion Brown continues to be the rising star of camp after he concluded Thursday's practice with a 46-yard touchdown from Spencer Rattler to finish out the two-minute drill.

 "Spencer got out of it -- we'll watch the film to see if there's a sack. There's always a debate of sack/no sack, it's never ending. So we let it play out and Barion did a great job adjusting to that ball, tracking it, those are deep balls and the ball usually tails one way or another because the QB is running, so awesome job making a play," coach Kellen Moore said.

 While Brown has mostly been with the second team to start camp, he's starting to get more opportunities, including some snaps with the first team in the two-minute drill, where he caught a pass from Tyler Shough for about a 15-yard gain.

 

 More observations:
