 The first-team two-minute drill was won by the defense after a sack (pressure from Cameron Jordan ) and an interception of Shough by Quincy Riley (pressure from Carl Granderson ) as time expired. The offense was moving the ball well prior to that, with Shough completing two passes to Juwan Johnson and then passes to Travis Etienne Jr ., Chris Olave and Brown before spiking the ball to stop the clock. 
 Shough was also picked off by Kool-Aid McKinstry in the previous set of team drills in the end zone. Moore said it looked like the pass came up short in a throwaway situation. Etienne had the ball four plays in a row prior to the interception.

title: No. 2 pick Bailey living up to hype, bringing 'juice' to Jets
summary: New York's rookie pass rusher has lived up to the Jets' expectations early on.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- In 1.62 seconds, the human heart beats anywhere from 1.6 to 2.7 times, depending on the resting pulse rate. In the same amount of time, New York Jets edge rusher David Bailey can explode out of his stance, cover 10 yards and be in position to make a sack.

 Two heartbeats ... and down goes the quarterback.

 Thump-thump ... crunch! 

 "He has a really quick get-off," said left tackle Olu Fashanu , who faces Bailey every day in practice. "He has no wasted movement with his first step, so he's really closing ground quickly. I think that's what makes him different."

 

 Bailey's impressive 10-yard split at the NFL scouting combine -- 1.62 seconds in a sizzling 4.5 40-yard dash -- solidified his status in the draft, one of the big reasons why the Jets selected him No. 2 overall. For an edge rusher, the 10-yard split often is more revealing than the 40-yard dash time. In the NFL trenches, a tenth of a second separates elite pass rushers from the pedestrian ones.

 Speed and efficiency are the hallmarks of Bailey's life. Raised in a family environment who stressed academics and discipline, Bailey graduated from Stanford in three years with a degree in science, technology and society. He transferred to Texas Tech, shifted his focus entirely to football and transformed himself into a blue-chip NFL prospect in one season -- one hellacious, 14.5-sack, 72-QB pressure season.

 Bailey, who turns 23 on Aug. 28, is accelerating into his rookie season, trying to deliver a rush job for the ages. He patterns his game after Von Miller , a former second overall pick by the Denver Broncos who entered the league in 2011 with the same height (6-foot-3), weight (250) and 10-yard split (1.62) as Bailey.

 Mirror images? Bailey hopes so. After all, Miller won NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year and ranks ninth on the all-time sack list with 138.5, positioning himself to be in the Pro Football Hall of Fame someday.

 "I wouldn't say I feel pressure, but it's in the back of your mind," said Bailey, addressing the question every high draft pick faces. "You're the No. 2 pick and there are high expectations from the fans and also from teammates and staff and everything. I try not to let that get to me."

 While expectations are high, the fanfare isn't.

 Bailey didn't make the NFLPA's 2026 rising stars list, which recognized 10 rookies based, in part, on marketing demands and social-media reach. New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese , compared to Bailey throughout the pre-draft process, made the list despite being picked three spots later.

 Not that Bailey minds the snub.

 Born in Orange, California, the former star at perennial power Mater Dei High School is the epitome of SoCal chill, according to those who know him. He's not obsessed with personal accolades, but that doesn't mean he's not driven. He knows what his job is, and he embraces it.

 "I play football for a lot of reasons -- I could go on and on why I love football -- but getting a sack, it's literally probably the best feeling it the world," he said, smiling. "It's like nothing else."

 And when he gets two or three sacks in a game?

 "Sometimes it feels like you're in a little bit of flow state, and everything is just falling," Bailey said.

 

 While there are no guarantees, recent history shows that highly drafted edge rushers usually make an immediate impact.

 Of the 14 edge rushers drafted in the top 10 from 2016 to 2025, four won Defensive Rookie of the Year ( Joey Bosa , Nick Bosa , Chase Young and  Will Anderson Jr .) and nine recorded at least seven sacks in their first season. Most are enjoying productive careers. Only two of the 14 haven't panned out --  Clelin Ferrell and Tyree Wilson , both drafted by the Raiders .

 "Obviously, they selected me for my pass rush ability," Bailey said, "but also, man, I want to bring a lot of energy to the team. Being a younger guy, I feel like it's my responsibility to bring a lot of juice."

 You'd expect a guy from Orange to deliver the juice, and he's doing that in training camp. Each day, he makes one or two "wow" plays, using his exceptional burst to cause problems for Fashanu and Armand Membou , the starting tackles.

 Bailey is known in the offensive-line room as "a pain in the ass," according to guard Joe Tippmann -- a high compliment.

 "I see him in the backfield all the time," defensive tackle Harrison Phillips said. "Oh, my gosh."

 Fashanu, beginning his third season, said Bailey's rush angles are different than any edge rusher he's faced. By that, he means that Bailey can take wider angles to the quarterback because of his ability to close quickly.

 Again, it goes back to that 1.62-second split. That puts additional stress on the tackle, who knows he must kick out quickly to cut him off. In doing so, it leaves the tackle vulnerable to inside counter moves.

 "He's everything that we expect him to be," coach Aaron Glenn said.

 

 "I think he's just scratching the surface of what he's going to become, which is pretty scary -- scary in a good way," Texas Tech defensive coordinator Shiel Wood told ESPN.

 Even though he was regarded as the most pro-ready pass rusher in the draft, Bailey's knock has been that he needs to develop counter moves and must learn to use his hands to disengage from blockers.

 He has huge hands -- 10.25 inches, which put him in the 80th percentile of edge rushers at the combine. There are questions about his run defense, to which defensive line coach Karl Dunbar responded, "Don't care. Can he rush the passer? That's what we're going to do with him."

 Learning has never been a problem for Bailey, who made it through one of the country's most rigorous academic institutions in only three years. His coach at Mater Dei, Bruce Rollinson, described Bailey as "a gifted writer and a gifted thinker." He recalled phone calls from Bailey's teachers, raving about his acumen in the classroom.

 Before committing to the Cardinal, he was prepared to attend Harvard, following in the footsteps of older brother D.J.

 Academics were important for his parents, Anthony and Monica, who emigrated from Jamaica and Ghana, respectively. Rollinson, finally convinced them that David was a special talent and needed to play at a higher level than the Ivy League.

 "David just had that ability to just turn a football game," said Rollinson, adding, "he could destroy a young offensive lineman's confidence in one [practice] period. He was uniquely freakish. People talk about his speed, but his hip bend was unreal."

 Bailey was a solid player for Stanford (12.5 sacks in three seasons), but he didn't blow up ESPN senior draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr.'s Big Board. The Cardinal used him mainly as an off-ball linebacker, which limited his pass-rushing opportunities. That wasn't an issue at Texas Tech, which let him do what he does best.

 He didn't arrive in Lubbock, Texas, until midway through the 2025 spring practice schedule. After only four practices, with little chance to study the playbook, Bailey was thrown into a scrimmage. He was paired with Romello Height as edge rushers; Height would become a third-round pick of the San Francisco 49ers .

 "I remember there were a couple of plays in that scrimmage where they met at the quarterback in a flash," Wood said. "Everybody thought, 'Man, this is going to be pretty neat.'"

 Bailey viewed his one season at Texas Tech as an NFL prep year, taking classes just to remain eligible and focusing on his football future. Everything he did, from conditioning to body maintenance to film study, was done with the NFL in mind.

 "It was a personal thing in terms of it being my last year and me wanting to put something I was proud of on tape," Bailey said. "I knew that I had to operate and function differently than I had in the past."

 He did it quickly, using that 1.62-second speed.

 Thump-thump.

title: 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Buccaneers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' camp is taking place at the Advent Health Training Center in Tampa, Florida, and Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bucs camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest new s from Bucs camp 
 
 Bucs GM Licht: 'No plans' for Vea trade, Mayfield still franchise QB 
 Mayfield felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by contract offers 
 History says Vea, Mayfield will play with Bucs this season 
 Vea requests trade from Bucs after stalled talks 
 2026 Bucs training camp preview 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst III made arguably the two biggest catches of the day -- both times were with the first-team offense and fans roared with approval. The first was an overlead leaping grab coming out of a trips formation with Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with Hurst running a deep out and cornerback Josh Hayes in coverage. Hurst fell hard onto his back and it knocked the wind out of him, making him slow to get up as he was checked out by the training staff. Then during the red zone period, he caught a beautiful fade route for a touchdown with Jacob Parrish in coverage.

 The Bucs' third-round draft pick out of Georgia State has gotten more opportunities with the first-team offense due to injuries for Jalen McMillan (knee) and Tez Johnson (groin) and said he feels like he's starting to turn the corner in terms of preparation and performance. 
 
"[I'm] just trying to be myself and exploit and show that that's my game, going up, attacking the ball," Hurst said. "Lately, I feel like I haven't been doing that much, but it kind of starts in the morning. Getting up and coming in at 6:30 a.m., getting the walk-through in before we even get outside so I can just play [as] fast as I want to, not thinking out there on the field."

 Other observations:  

 
 Second-year outside linebacker David Walker , who missed all of last season with a torn ACL, was once again a force in the backfield for the ninth consecutive day. Walker would have had a sack on Mayfield coming off the left side, as he's been getting work in with the first and second-team defense. Keep in mind though, that this was against backup Ben Chukwuma and not All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs , who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury. Outside linebacker YaYa Diaby also registered a would-be sack. 
 Veteran wide receiver Chris Godwin caught several passes from quarterback Baker Mayfield , including one in red zone for a touchdown. He's looked healthy and energized throughout practices and we've seen him show some versatility in lining up all over the formation. "I think he is healthy right now," Bowles said of Godwin. "In the past he has been hurt the last two but he is a lot healthier right now and he is into it mentally he is sharp and he is tough, he understands that he is a great mentor to the guys. He is still a playmaker for us, and he makes big plays in the passing and blocking game. He is peaking at the right time." 
 Safety Tykee Smith made an impressive stop on running back Bucky Irving during red zone work, blowing up the play for no gain which got everybody fired up on defense. 
 In the red zone, wide receiver Dennis Houston , who, like Hurst, has made the most of some opportunities due to injuries, hauled in an impressive Jake Browning touchdown coming across the back of the end zone with Scott in coverage. The coaching staff has been really excited about Houston's speed and believes he may be one of, if not the fastest on their roster. 
 Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson and running back Kenneth Gainwell, who both missed Friday's practice due to personal reasons, returned Sunday. 
 Still not practicing is cornerback Benjamin Morrison , who has been dealing with a hamstring injury since minicamp. Earlier in the week, Bowles expressed hope that he may be able to do some things next week at joint practices at the New York Jets . But Sunday Bowles said, "He's the same as usual," so there has been no change. 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 Quarterback Baker Mayfield connected with tight end Cade Otton on a slant route for a touchdown during a red-zone period. Meanwhile, cornerback Zyon McCollum intercepted Mayfield on a pass intended for Emeka Egbuka during the two-minute drill.

 That's the kind of back and forth that coach Todd Bowles has coveted after the defense had a dominant day Thursday.

 "I thought the offense started out very well," Bowles said. "I thought it was a lot more give and take today than it was yesterday. The energy was there and the intent was there. We still have some things to clean up. I think both sides made plays. One period, the offense won, one period, the defense won. There was a lot of back and forth, which is what you want to see, trying to make each other better."

 Other observations: 

 
 Starting left tackle Tristan Wirfs still isn't practicing due to a hamstring injury. Bowles added, "If he's healthy, we'd like to work him back in. It doesn't matter how much. We're not just going to throw him in there and give him a whole bunch of reps, but we'll see how he looks in individual [periods]." 
 Running back Kenny Gainwell was excused from Friday's practice because of personal reasons, according to Bowles, as was the case for offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. Bowles said both would be back at practice Sunday as the team has Saturday off. 
 Rookie guard  Billy Schrauth  missed practice as well, with Bowles saying he's "kind of banged up" and "I don't know how long he'll be sidelined, but he should miss a few days." 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 After going three straight days inside the indoor practice facility and having a rest day Wednesday, the Bucs returned outdoors.

 Quarterback  Baker Mayfield  felt the heat from the sun and from the defense, as the pressure got to him several times, and he was flushed from the pocket and forced to throw the ball away as he couldn't find any downfield options because of tight coverage by the secondary. And he was also picked off.

 Backup linebacker John Bullock jumped a route on a pass intended for tight end Cade Otton and returned the interception for a touchdown. Rookie inside linebacker Josiah Trotter , who has made his presence known now that the pads are on, immediately drilled Otton after catching a short pass from Mayfield. Overall, it wasn't a great day for Mayfield and the tight ends, with rookie Keionte Scott breaking up a Mayfield pass intended for Payne Durham .

 Rookie cornerback Ayden Garnes had a pass breakup on a Mayfield ball intended for rookie wide receiver  Ted Hurst III  along the right sideline. Rookie Rueben Bain Jr . also blew up a screen pass to running back Bucky Irving .

 Other observations: 

 
 Outside linebacker David Walker Jr., who missed his rookie season last year with a torn ACL, had a strip sack of backup quarterback Jake Browning and made the recovery at the end of practice. Walker has had a sack just about every practice. "We didn't get to see him in pads last year, but to see him out there and the way he moves -- he moves like an inside backer, but he plays like an outside backer and he's got great power," coach Todd Bowles said. 
 Wide receiver  Dean Patterson  hauled in an impressive deep ball catch working against cornerback Josh Hayes .

title: Can Carnell Tate develop into the WR the Titans need?

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Titans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Tennessee Titans ' camp is taking place at the Vanderbilt Health Football Center, and Titans reporter Turron Davenport has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Titans camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Titans news: 

 
 Extension makes Peter Skoronski NFL's top-paid guard 
 Titans DT Jeffery Simmons throws punch, sent to side field 
 Will Levis: There aren't 32 QBs better than me 
 Titans WRs join Cam Ward in Miami to build chemistry 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 Carnell Tate continues to impress in his first NFL training camp.

 One of his standout traits is how effectively Tate is running the full route tree.

 Tate was on the receiving end of three touchdown passes from Cam Ward . The rookie wideout caught a deep pass for a score on a go route with Alontae Taylor being the closest defender. Tate made an impressive catch over Cor'Dale Flott in the corner of the end zone on another play, and he caught a quick out-breaking route for his third score.

 "Tate has an innate ability to attack the ball," Titans receivers coach Greg Lewis said after practice. "He can make contested catches. He has long speed and is really smooth. The guy can also uncover."

 

 More observations: 

 
 - Joshua Williams was once again in the yellow "non-contact" jersey. Williams had the jersey on in the scrimmage on Friday as well. Titans coach Robert Saleh said Williams is dealing with a pectoral injury that cost him some time during minicamp. Williams was still working in team periods. 
 The center position is still a competition, but it seems like veteran Austin Schlottmann will win the job. Left guard Peter Skoronski said Schlottmann has helped accelerate the learning process for him because of the previous time with Titans offensive coordinator when they were with the Giants. Pat Coogan continues to get early reps but has struggled at times with off-target snaps to Mitchell Trubisky during team periods. 
 Right guard is another position battle to watch. Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater have been the primary competitors, with both getting opportunities to protect Ward during team periods. Rookie Fernando Carmona also got some early reps for the first time on Sunday. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Titans returned to the field after not practicing Wednesday. The pace was noticeably slower to start, but it livened up during team period.

 The offensive line continues to shuffle, especially along the interior, where Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater are the top contenders for right guard while Austin Schlottmann , Pat Coogan and Andre James are battling for the starting center spot.

 All five players have gotten first-team reps in different tandems. Schlottmann has enjoyed going against Jeffery Simmons during team period because "he's one of the best, if not the best interior defenders in the league." Coach Robert Saleh said they're not close to deciding who will start at this point but expects to be closer to a decision leading into the third preseason game.

 Other observations: 

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He caught a deep pass from Cam Ward on a go route in red zone team period to even the score with Alontae Taylor who broke up a pass on the same route earlier in practice. Ward went to Ayomanor again, but the pass fell incomplete. Ayomanor collided with S  Kevin Winston Jr . as they went up for the pass in what Saleh described as a "bang, bang" play. Ayomanor got up favoring his left shoulder after being down for a bit. He went inside for further evaluation. 
 Left tackle  Dan Moore Jr . returned to practice after leaving team period and walking into the building on his own with a trainer Tuesday. Moore took part in team period and got into a small pushing match with linebacker Cody Barton after one of the plays. 
 JC Latham came out during team period towards the end of practice after taking three reps. Reserve tackle Austin Deculus came on in Latham's place and stayed in when the next group of linemen came in. Latham returned for the final team period and had a couple nice blocks on run plays. 
 The Titans will host a Blue/White scrimmage at Nissan Stadium on Friday night. "We'll play move the ball," Saleh said after practice. "We'll play special teams and it'll flow like a game where you'll see first offense against first defense. We have a full scoring system to make it competitive and as game-like as possible. We'll try to get to like 90 plays." 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The middle linebacker competition is heating up. James Williams Sr . has strung three consecutive standout days.

 Williams said he's lost about 20 pounds this offseason. The converted safety looked like a defensive back on a jumping one-handed interception of a Mitchell Trubisky pass during team period. Williams got a pass breakup later in practice when Trubisky went to tight end  Kylen Granson  on an out-breaking route.

 Titans defensive coordinator Gus Bradley spoke glowingly of Williams before practice.

 "We like those guys that have played safety in their career and move them down the linebacker," Bradley said. "That pass coverage part of it, that safety background that he has, I think allows him to be a little bit more instinctive."

 Williams worked alongside rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr . mostly. Hill added a couple of interceptions as well, both off Trubisky. One of the interceptions came because Trubisky hit his hand on an offensive lineman's helmet.

 Other observations:  

 
 DT  Jeffery Simmons and OL  Austin Schlottmann with some extracurricular after a play. Simmons swung at  JC Latham in the scrum before Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons. Coach Robert Saleh didn't like it. Stopped practice and gathered the group for a cool-down talk. Simmons was forced to work on a side field with Brian Bell (strength coach) and wasn't allowed to return to practice. 
 QB  Cam Ward connected with WR  Carnell Tate on a beautiful pass for the play of the day. Tate ran a post and Ward launched a deep pass that traveled at least 50 yards in the air. Tate showed explosiveness as he pulled away from Alontae Taylor to run down the ball for the touchdown. 
 One-on-ones were a little different for WRs/DBs under Saleh. It's more like seven-on-sevens but only allowing man defense. Saleh said he uses this format to facilitate more authentic route running instead of the unreasonably long-developing routes. The offensive line versus defensive line setup was the same as normal. 
 Backup QB  Will Levis and WR  Bryce Oliver connected on two deep passes. Levis worked a play-action pass to Oliver on a deep crossing route. Oliver caught the pass in between the safety and cornerback Keydrain Calligan . Oliver made a jumping catch on a go route from Levis later in the day. 
 LT  Dan Moore Jr . left practice during the second team period. Saleh acknowledged after practice that Moore was hurt, but he didn't have any specifics regarding the injury immediately after practice. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 The first day of pads had a really good pace and tempo. Both the offense and defense did a good job keeping each other off the ground for the most part.

 The defense had big hits from cornerback Nazeeh Johnson and linebacker Sean Brown , and quarterback  Cam Ward had two hiccups throwing across his body while rolling out -- resulting in interceptions.
